Seeds 1 mm. long, with 6–7 longitudinal ridges on the dorsal facet, and 5–6 shallow concentric ridges on each ventral facet, and with numerous faint transverse striae between the ridges, uniformly light brown.
bibliographicCitation: Euphorbiaceae, A. R.-Smith. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1987

description: Herb to 1.2 m. tall. Tuber subglobose, ± 5 cm. in diameter. Leaves 1–2; petioles with basal sheaths imbricate, forming green crimson-speckled pseudstem to ± 45 cm. tall; free apical part (5–) 17–40 cm. long; blade usually laxly pedate, rarely compactly pedate, reniform in outline, leaflet bases (0.3–)0.7–2.2 cm. apart; leaflets (4–)6–8, elliptic-oblanceolate, long-acuminate with filiform tips up to 8 cm. long, (5–)8.5–32 cm. long, (1.2–)3–11 cm. broad, outermost smaller than the rest, margins entire or obscurely crisped. Inflorescence ± equalling or overtopping leaves; free part of peduncle 6–30 cm. long, green. Spathe 7–23 cm. long; tube cylindric to obconic, not constricted apically, 4–9.5 cm. long, 1.3–3 cm. in diameter, outer surface green with cream-yellow to white stripes; limb ovate, long-acuminate, arching forward and downward over tube-mouth, 7–16.5 cm. long, 2–4.7(–6) cm. broad, much longer than tube, with filamentous tip 2–7 cm. long, similar in colour to tube but with broader stripes basally. Spadix normally unisexual, 5–10(–11) cm. long, overtopping spathe-tube; sterile appendix cylindric to clavate, subtruncate basally, usually ± stipitate, 3–6 cm. long, 0.2–0.9(–1.2) cm. in diameter, apex rounded, green; staminate spadix with fertile part 3.5–4.5 cm. long, 0.3–0.5 cm. in diameter, rarely with sterile projections at appendix base; pistillate spadix with fertile part 2–2.5(–5.5) cm. long, 0.9–1.3 cm. in diameter, usually with sterile projections at appendix base. Staminate flower composed of 2–3 stamens. Pistil ovoid, 3–4 mm. long; ovary 2–3 mm. in diameter, narrowing upwards into a short style; stigma capitate. Berries subglobose, up to 1 cm. in diameter, 1–3-seeded, borne in subcylindric spike up to 9.5 cm. long, 4 cm. in diameter. Seeds subglobose, 0.6 cm. in diameter. Fig. 16/9–13, p. 62.
bibliographicCitation: Araceae, S.J. Mayo. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1985

description: Dioecious or sometimes monoecious delicate weakly and sparingly branched brittle glabrous or subglabrous shrub 1–1.5 m. tall. Stems greenish. Orthotropic shoots angular. Plagiotropic shoots (10–)15–30(–45) cm. long, angular, smooth or somewhat asperulous. Cataphylls narrowly lanceolate, 1.5 mm. long, dark purplish brown with a narrow hyaline margin. Cataphyllary stipules narrowly triangular-lanceolate, 1 mm. long, acute, entire, dark purplish brown with a narrow hyaline margin. Leaves of the plagiotropic shoots remotely distichous; petioles 1–2 mm. long; blades elliptic-obovate to oblanceolate-oblong, (1–)2–3.2 cm. long, (0.5–)1–1.4 cm. wide, obtuse or subacute, mucronulate or not, cuneate or attenuate, membranaceous, lateral nerves 9–13 pairs, not prominent above and scarcely so beneath, dark green above, paler beneath, sometimes reddening. Stipules linear-lanceolate, 2 mm. long, aristate, entire, reddish with a narrow hyaline margin. Male flowers 1–3 per axil, in the axils of the proximal half of the flowering shoots; ♀ solitary in the axils of the distal half. Male flowers: pedicels 3 mm. long; sepals 6, elliptic, 2 mm. long, 1.5 mm. wide, obtuse to rounded, pale green; disc-glands 6, free, obovate-suborbicular, flat, smooth; sta-mens 3, filaments connate into a column 1 mm. high, anthers ± free, horizontally held, reniform, 0.3 mm. across, laterally dehiscent. Female flowers: pedicels 3–5 mm. long, slightly thickened apically; sepals slightly larger than those of the ♂ flowers, otherwise similar; disc shallowly hexalobate, ± flattened, smooth; ovary trilobate-subglobose, 0.75–1 mm. diameter, smooth; styles 0.5 mm. long, ± united at the base, spreading, bifid to halfway, stigmas recurved. Fruit depressed-trilobate-subglobose, 2 mm. long, 2.5 mm. diameter, smooth. Seeds triquetrous, 1.5 mm. long, 1 mm. wide, with 8–9 shallow longitudinal ridges on the dorsal facet and 7 shallow concentric ridges on each ventral facet, slightly shiny, pale buff. Fig. 3/8, p. 22.
bibliographicCitation: Euphorbiaceae, A. R.-Smith. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1987

description: Monoecious glabrous shrub up to 3 m. Twigs greyish brown. Orthotropic stems slender, angular. Plagiotropic shoots 5–8 cm. long, angular, caducous. Brachyblasts present, co-axillary with the plagiotropic shoots, later themselves each giving rise to a lateral orthotropic shoot and/or one or more secondary plagiotropic shoots. Cataphylls linear-setaceous, 1 mm. long. Cataphyllary stipules lanceolate, 1 mm. long, purplish. Leaves of the plagiotropic shoots ± distichous; petioles 1 mm. long; blades elliptic, (7–)10–15(–19) mm. long, (4–)7–10(–12) mm. wide, rounded, obtuse or sub-acute, sometimes mucronulate, rounded or rounded-cuneate at the base, firmly membranaceous, lateral nerves 5–7 pairs, not or scarcely prominent above or beneath, pale dull green above, slightly glaucous beneath. Stipules linear, 1 mm. long, greenish. Male flowers 1–2 per axil in the proximal axils of the plagiotropic shoots, ♀ usually solitary in the distal axils. Male flowers: pedicels 2 mm. long; sepals 6, elliptic-ovate, 1 mm. long, 0.75 mm. wide, the 3 outer mucronate, the 3 inner acuminate, with a median yellowish-green band on either side of the midrib, and whitish hyaline margins; disc-glands 6, free, thick, bilobed, ± smooth; stamens 3, free, 0.5 mm. long, anthers reniform, apically and longitudinally dehiscent. Female flowers: pedicels 2.5 mm. long, extending to 3 mm. in fruit, slender, perceptibly distally dilated; sepals 6, elliptic-oblong, 1.3 mm. long, 0.8 mm. wide, obtuse, with a median pale green band on either side of the midrib, and narrow white hyaline margins; disc flat, shallowly 6-lobed, the lobes truncate, densely papillose on the outer edge; ovary sessile, depressed-globose, 1 mm. diameter, shallowly tuberculate-rugulose; styles 0.75 mm. long, free, divaricate, bifid to halfway, stigmas filiform. Fruit subglobose, 2 mm. long, 2.5 mm. diameter, tuberculate, olivaceous. Seeds roundly trigonous, 1.5 mm. long, 1 mm. across, ± smooth, indistinctly lineate, light brown. Fig. 3/9, p. 22.
bibliographicCitation: Euphorbiaceae, A. R.-Smith. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1987

description: Tree or shrub 4–35 m high, crown dense; trunk 5–60 cm in diameter, cylindrical; wood very hard. Leaves petiolate; blade broadly to narrowly ellipic to oblong, 10–27 cm long, 1.9–13 cm wide, apex abruptly acuminate with acumen 6–14 mm long, rounded to obtuse at the base; petiole 10–22 mm long. Inflorescence 6–10 cm long, 12–36-flowered; peduncle 2–37 mm long; bracts small; pedicels 2–20 mm long. Flowers with sepals broadly ovate to suborbicular; 3.5–7.5 mm long, 3.5–5 mm wide, obtuse to rounded at the apex; corolla tube often greenish, 14.5–21 mm long; lobes white to yellow, ovate, 13.5–30 mm long, 5.5–10 mm wide, obtuse at the apex; stamens inserted at 9.5–15 mm from the base; pistil 9.7–12.5 mm long; style 5–7.3 mm long; ovules 120–150 in each carpel. Fruits yellow to orange, smooth, irregularly pyriform or obovoid to ellipsoid, 8–15 cm long, 13–14 cm in diameter, apex rounded. Fig. 11 (p. 35).
bibliographicCitation: Apocynaceae, E.A. Omino. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 2002

description: Tree to 20 m with young branchlets glandular and pubescent. Leaves aromatic, oblong-elliptic, elliptic or elliptic-lanceolate, 5.5–17(–22) cm long, 2–6.5(–8) cm wide, rounded to obtusely acuminate at the apex, ± glabrous beneath. Flowers white, 4-merous, small in many-flowered panicles 5–12 cm long. Fruit subglobose, 5–10 mm diameter, densely covered with convex glands. Fig. 1/3–4, p. 4.
bibliographicCitation: Myrtaceae, B. Verdcourt, B.Sc., Ph.D. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 2001

description: Shrub or small slender tree 7.5–15 m tall; bark thin and scaly, peeling to produce a mottled trunk; essentially glabrous but with dense glands on stems and leaves. Leaves very aromatic, obovate to elliptic, 3–15 cm long, 1.2–7.5 cm wide, acute to broadly rounded at the apex, coriaceous. Flowers white, 5-merous, small, in many flowered ((5–)15–100) panicles 2.5–12 cm long. Fruit subglobose, 6–12 mm diameter, 1–4-seeded (2–8 fide T.T.C.L.).
bibliographicCitation: Myrtaceae, B. Verdcourt, B.Sc., Ph.D. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 2001

description: Herb to 120 cm. tall. Tuber depressed-globose, 2–6 cm. in diameter. Leaves usually 2; petioles with basal sheaths imbricate, forming green, purplish- or red-mottled pseudostem up to 100 cm. tall; free apical part 8–23 cm. long; blade subcircular to reniform in outline, compound, radiate to ± compactly pedate, divided to base, leaflet bases up to 0.7 cm. apart; leaflets 5–7(–9), central 1–3 the largest, lateral leaflets decreasing in size outwards, elliptic to obovate, acuminate, base unequally cuneate, largest 8–26 cm. long, 2.5–10.5 cm. broad, margins entire or crisped, rarely obscurely serrate-dentate. Inflorescence ± equalling or overtopping leaves; free part of peduncle 14–26 cm. long, green. Spathe 16–28 cm. long; tube cylindric to somewhat obconic, not constricted apically, 6–15 cm. long, 1.7–3.5 cm. in diameter, outer surface glaucous green with white, yellowish or purplish stripes along veins; limb ovate or oblong-ovate, long-acuminate, 10–13 cm. long, 3–5.5 cm. broad, longer or shorter than tube, often with filamentous tip up to 4 cm. long, green. Spadix normally unisexual, 9–17 cm. long, just overtopping spathe-tube; sterile appendix cylindric to clavate, sharply narrowed and subtruncate basally with short stipe, 5–9 cm. long, 0.7–1.4 cm. in diameter, apex rounded, pale green to greenish yellow; staminate spadix subsessile, fertile part subcylindric, 2.5–7 cm. long, 0.7–1.4 cm. in diameter, flowers distant; pistillate spadix subsessile, fertile part gradually tapering upwards, usually with a few subulate sterile projections at appendix base, ± 4.5 cm. long, 1.1 cm. in diameter, flowers ± congested. Staminate flower composed of 3–5 stamens; anthers dehiscing by subcircular oblique apical slits. Pistil ovoid, 3–4 mm. long, green; ovary 2–2.5 mm. in diameter, tapering to short style with capitate stigma. Fruiting spadix to 12 cm. long, without appendix. Berries subglobose, 0.5–1 cm. in diameter, 2–4-seeded. Seeds 4–5 mm. in diameter.
bibliographicCitation: Araceae, S.J. Mayo. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1985

description: Herb to 200 cm. tall. Tuber discoid to depressed-globose, up to 5 cm. in diameter or more. Leaves 2–3; petioles with basal sheaths imbricate, forming green pseudostem to ± 75 cm. or more; free apical part of petiole 5–40 cm. long; blade radiately divided to base, circular in outline; leaflets (5–)9–15, subequal in size, usually narrowly elliptic to elliptic or narrowly oblanceolate to obovate, 4.5–27 cm. long, 1–9 cm. broad, acuminate, base cuneate, margins usually finely serrate-dentate with acuminate teeth up to 2 mm, long, rarely subentire. Inflorescence equalling or overtopping leaves; free part of peduncle 9–35 cm. long, green. Spathe 8–31 cm. long; tube cylindric to narrowly obconic, not or hardly constricted apically, 3–12 cm. long, 0.8–3 cm. in diameter, outer surface green with white to yellow longitudinal stripes along veins; limb oblong-lanceolate, sometimes ovate, 5–21.5 cm. long, 1–5 cm. broad, shorter or longer than tube, sometimes with very long filamentous tip, green, rarely purple-brown tinged. Spadix usually unisexual, rarely with flowers of both sexes present, 3.8–12.8 cm. long, slightly longer than spathe-tube; sterile appendix cylindric to conic, 2–9 cm. long, 0.2–1.4 cm. in diameter, narrowed basally, sometimes truncate with stipe up to 1 cm. long, apex rounded, pale green to yellowish green; staminate spadix ± sessile, fertile part subcylindric, 1.4–4.3 cm. long, 0.4–0.8 cm. in diameter, flowers ± distant; pistillate spadix subsessile, fertile part gradually tapering upwards, 3–5 cm. long, 1.2–1.3 cm. in diameter, flowers congested to ± distant. Staminate flower composed of 2–3 stamens; anthers dehiscing by subcircular oblique apical slits. Pistils ovoid, 3–4.5 mm. long, green; ovary 2–2.5 mm. in diameter, tapering to short style with capitate whitish stigma. Berries subglobose, 0.5–0.8 cm. in diameter, scarlet when ripe, green with yellowish stripes when immature, 3–4-seeded. Seeds ± 4 mm. in diameter.
bibliographicCitation: Araceae, S.J. Mayo. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1985

description: Plant reproducing vegetatively by stolons. Leaf-blade up to 14 cm. long, 8 cm. broad, spathulate, obconic or oblong, apex rounded to truncate, green, paler and more densely pubescent beneath; main veins 5–7, prominently winged beneath. Spathe to 1.3 cm. long, whitish green, margins and exterior fimbriate-pilose. Berry to 0.5 cm. long, 0.3 cm. broad. Seeds to 0.2 cm. long, 0.1 cm. in diameter, reddish brown. Fig. 17.
bibliographicCitation: Araceae, S.J. Mayo. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1985

description: Herb to 100 cm. tall. Tuber depressed-globose, 3–4 cm. in diameter. Leaves 1–2; petiole with basal sheaths imbricate, forming green to brownish-red pseudostem; free apical part of petiole 30–34 cm. long, green to brownish red; blade radiately divided to base, circular in outline; leaflets 6–8, subequal in size, broadly elliptic to obovate, acuminate, base cuneate, 11–20 cm. long, 4–8 cm. broad, margins entire. Inflorescence subequal to leaves. Spathe 16–28 cm. long; tube cylindric to obconic, not constricted apically, 5.5–8 cm. long, 2.5–3 cm. in diameter, outer surface pale green, sometimes with reddish markings; limb broadly ovate, long-acuminate, base strongly auriculate with revolute margins, 11–20 cm. long, 5–8 cm. broad, longer than tube, dull green, darker than tube. Spadix unisexual, 8–10.5 cm. long, longer than spathe-tube; sterile appendix clavate-cylindric, 5–7 cm. long, 0.5–1.2 cm. in diameter, apex rounded, truncate and stipitate at base with 4–8 mm. long stipe, pale green; staminate spadix ± sessile, fertile part cylindric, 2.5–3.5 cm. long, 0.5–0.8 cm. in diameter, flowers distant; pistillate spadix subsessile, fertile part ± conic, ± 2.3 cm. long, 0.9 cm. in diameter, flowers ± congested. Staminate flower composed of 1–3 stamens; anthers dehiscing by subcircular ± oblique apical slits. Pistil ovoid, 3–4 mm. long, tapering to short style with capitate stigma. Fruiting spadix 9 cm. long, 4 cm. in diameter. Berries subglobose, ± 1 cm. in diameter, 1–3-seeded, turning orange (? eventually red). Seeds subglobose, 5–6 mm. in diameter.
bibliographicCitation: Araceae, S.J. Mayo. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1985

description: A terrestrial herb 1.5–4 dm. high, glabrous except for the roots. Tubers ellipsoid, ± 1 cm. long and 0.5 cm. in diameter, ± tomentose. Stem erect, slender, flexuous, with leaves scattered along its length, terete or angular. Leaves 4–7, the lowermost sometimes reduced to a sheath, the remainder erect or suberect, linear, acute, the largest 4–10 cm. long and 4–7 mm. broad, the upper ones smaller. Inflorescence up to 10 cm. long, 2.5–4 cm. in diameter, rather loosely (l-)3–8-flowered. Bracts leafy, lanceolate, acuminate, 1–2.5 cm. long, the lower ones longer than the pedicel with ovary. Flowers curving outwards, yellow or scarlet; pedicel with ovary curved, ± 2 cm. long. Dorsal sepal curved forwards, resembling a sickle from the side, very convex, lanceolate, acuminate, 1.3–1.7 cm. long, ± 6 mm. broad; laterals deflexed, narrowly lanceolate, very acute, 1–1.5 cm. long, ± 2.5 mm. broad. Petals erect, adherent to the dorsal sepal, linear, acute, 11–15 mm. long, nearly 1.5 mm. broad. Lip generally curved upwards from just above the base, linear, obtuse, 1–1.4 cm. long, ± 1.5 mm. broad. Spur dependent, swollen in the apical part, 1.2–1.6 cm. long. Anther erect, subacute, ± 6 mm. high, canals porrect or slightly curved upwards, ± 4.5 mm. long. Stigmas horizontal, swollen at the apex, fleshy, ± 3 mm. long. Rostellum placed in front of the anther, 4.5 mm. high, 3-lobed in the upper half, the middle lobe oblong-lanceolate, acute, 3 mm. long, the side lobes shorter, obliquely triangular, truncate.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: A terrestrial herb 2–6.5 dm. high, glabrous except for the roots. Tubers ellipsoid to cylindrical-ellipsoid, 1.5–2.5 cm. long, 5–15 mm. in diameter, tomentose. Stem erect, often somewhat flexuous, slender to rather stout, with leaves scattered along its length, terete or slightly angular. Leaves 5–9, the lowermost often reduced to a sheath, the remainder ± adpressed or the lower ones somewhat spreading, lanceolate, acute, the largest 2.5–9 cm. long, 5–13 mm. broad, the uppermost similar to the bracts. Inflorescence relatively short, 1.5–5.5 cm. long, 2–3.5 cm. in diameter, densely (l-)4- 12(–16)-flowered. Bracts broadly lanceolate, acute or acuminate, 1–2 cm. long, about equalling the pedicel with ovary. Flowers suberect, pale yellow to deep orange; pedicel with ovary straight or slightly curved, 1–2 cm. long. Dorsal sepal erect, very convex and forming a hood with the petals, broadly elliptical-ovate, 5–8.5 mm. long, 4.5–7 mm. broad; laterals deflexed, obliquely elliptical- or oblong-lanceolate, apiculate, 5–9 mm. long, 2–3 mm. broad. Petals erect, adherent to the dorsal sepal, narrowly or ligulate lanceolate, curved, obtuse or subacute, 3.5–7.5 mm. long, 1–3 mm. broad. Lip inflexed, ligulate or elliptical-ligulate, fleshy, convex, obtuse, 5–8.5 mm. long, 1–2 mm. broad. Spur dependent, swollen in the apical half, 1–1.8 cm. long. Anther erect, apiculate, ± 4 mm. high, loculi parallel, canals porrect, 2–3 mm. long. Stigmas horizontal or slightly decurved, thick with swollen truncate ends, 2–3 mm. long. Rostellum placed in front of the anther, the middle lobe narrow, acute, variable in length, sometimes overtopping the anther, the side lobes porrect with parallel sides.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: A terrestrial herb 1–4 dm. high, glabrous except for the roots. Tubers ellipsoid or almost globose, 8–18 mm. long, 5–10 mm. in diameter, densely tomentose. Stem erect, often somewhat flexuous, slender, terete or angled, with a tuft of leaves at the base and several more scattered along its length. Leaves 5–12(–16), the lowermost sometimes reduced to a sheath, the lower 3–8 forming a tuft, suberect or variously spreading, linear or linear-lanceolate, acute, the largest 1.5–6(–8) cm. long, 2–8 mm. broad, the upper ones at intervals on the stem, ± adpressed, lanceolate, acute, shorter than the basal ones. Inflorescence short, 0.5–2(–3.5) cm. long, 2–3.5 cm. in diameter, densely 2–6(–9)-flowered. Bracts leafy, lanceolate, acuminate, 7–18 mm. long, usually shorter than the pedicel with ovary. Flowers suberect or curving outwards, yellow or orange; pedicel with ovary ± curved, 14- 19 mm. long. Dorsal sepal erect or curved forwards, very convex, broadly ovate, acute, 6.5–12 mm. long, 3.5–7.5 mm. broad; laterals deflexed, obliquely oblong-lanceolate, acute or acuminate, 5.5–11.5 mm. long, 2- 3.5 mm. broad. Petals erect, adherent to the dorsal sepal, much curved, obliquely ligulate-lanceolate, subacute or obtuse, 4.5–10.5 mm. long, ± 2 mm. broad. Lip deflexed, often upcurved in the apical part, 3-lobed at the base, altogether 5–12 mm. long; middle lobe ligulate, fleshy, obtuse, 1–2 mm. broad, the side lobes ± spreading, almost tooth-like or up to nearly 2 mm. long, narrow, acute. Spur dependent, swollen in the apical part, 9–15 mm. long. Anther erect, obtuse or shortly apiculate, 2.5–4.5 mm. long, canals porrect, 1–2.5 mm. long. Stigmas horizontal or somewhat decurved, club-shaped, obtuse, 1.5–3 mm. long. Rostellum erect, 3-lobed, the middle lobe narrowly triangular, acute, 1–2.5 mm. long, the side lobes shorter, truncate.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: A terrestrial herb 2–5 dm. high, glabrous except for the roots. Tubers ellipsoid or almost globose, 0.5–2 cm. long, 5–12 mm. in diameter, sparsely tomentose. Stem erect, often somewhat flexuous, slender, terete, with leaves scattered along its length. Leaves 6–10, the lowermost 1–2 reduced to sheaths, the remainder suberect or ± spreading, the largest 2.5–6 cm. long and 4–9 mm. broad, the upper smaller. Inflorescence short, rarely up to 5 cm. long, 2.5–3.5 cm. in diameter, densely 2–5(–7)-flowered. Bracts broadly lanceolate, acuminate, 7–20 mm. long, shorter than the pedicel with ovary. Flowers curving outwards or suberect, orange; pedicel with ovary somewhat curved, 1.5–2.5 cm. long. Dorsal sepal erect, broadly ovate, very convex, acute, 7–11 mm. long, 5–6 mm. broad; laterals deflexed, obliquely oblong-lanceolate, acute, 8–10 mm. long, 2–3.5 mm. broad. Petals erect, adherent to the dorsal sepal, much curved, ligulate-lanceolate, 7- 10 mm. long, ± 2.5 mm. broad. Lip deflexed, 3-lobed at the base, 6.5- 10.5 mm. long, 1–2 mm. broad, the side lobes tooth-like or triangular, spreading, scarcely 1 mm. long. Spur dependent, swollen in the apical third, 1–1.7 cm. long. Anther erect, apiculate, 3–5 mm. tall, canals porrect, 1–2 mm. long. Stigmas horizontal, thick, club-shaped, 2–3 mm. long. Rostellum erect, nearly as long as the anther, the middle lobe narrowly triangular, just over 2 mm. long, the side lobes truncate, shorter.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: A terrestrial herb 2–5 dm. high, glabrous except for the roots. Tubers globose to ellipsoid or narrowly ovoid, 7–20 mm. long, 5–10 mm. in diameter, ± tomentose. Stem erect, ± flexuous, slender, with leaves scattered along its length, ± angular. Leaves 4–8, the lowermost often reduced to a sheath, the next 1 or 2 ± spreading or recurved, lanceolate, acute, the largest 2–6 cm. long and 3–9 mm. broad, the remainder erect and adpressed to the stem, spaced out at rather long intervals, the uppermost similar to the bracts. Inflorescence narrow, up to 8.5 cm. long, loosely l–5(rarely –7)-flowered. Bracts adpressed with the apices sometimes a little recurved, lanceolate, acute, 1–2.5 cm. long, much shorter than the pedicel with ovary. Flowers nearly erect or curved outwards above, the sepals green or greenish-orange, the remainder orange or dull orange; pedicel slender, erect, the ovary curved, altogether 2.5–4 cm. long. Dorsal sepal erect, very convex, elliptical or elliptical-ovate, subacute or obtuse, 5.5–8 mm. long, 3.5–6 mm. broad; laterals deflexed, obliquely oblong-lanceolate, subacute, 5–9 mm. long, 2–3.5 mm. broad. Petals erect, adherent to the dorsal sepal, obliquely triangular-lanceolate from a broad base, 5–7 mm. long, 2–3.5 mm. broad. Lip deflexed, convex and fleshy, narrowly oblong or elliptical, sometimes broader towards the base, 5–7 mm. long, 2.5–4 mm. broad. Spur dependent, slender towards the base, the apical half somewhat swollen, 2–3.5 cm. long. Anther erect, with a long apiculum, 2.5–4.5 mm. high, canals porrect, attached to the sides of the rostellum, 2–3 mm. long. Stigmas projecting forwards, thick with rounded or truncate apices, ± 2 mm. long. Rostellum placed in front of the anther and overtopping it, ± 4 mm. high, obscurely 3-lobed about the middle, the middle lobe very acute, the side lobes very short, shoulder-like.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: A laxly branched dioecious shrub or small tree of untidy habit, up to 9 m. tall. Bark smooth or rugulose, greyish brown. Young twigs greyish, striate or angular, lenticellate, minutely puberulous at first but soon glabrescent. Leaves unifoliolate; leaflet elliptic or elliptic-oblong, 6–32 cm. long, 2–12.5 cm. wide, obtusely acuminate, rounded or cuneate, undulate, coriaceous, midrib scarcely prominent above, prominent beneath, lateral nerves 10–14 pairs, glabrous above and ± so beneath, reddish when young, later becoming dark green and shiny above, drying pale green; petiole 0.5–10 cm. long, somewhat thickened at the base and apex, puberulous at first, later glabrescent. Stipules linear or narrowly elliptic, (1–)2–12 mm. long, up to 1 mm. wide, sharply acute, glabrous, sometimes 0. Bracts of the ♂ fascicles numerous, rufous pubescent. Male flowers: pedicels 1–1.5 mm. long; tepals elliptic, 2–2.5 mm. long, 1–1.25 mm. wide, ± obtuse, pubescent at the apex, yellowish; stamens 11–14, filaments 2 mm. long, glabrous, anthers 1 mm. long; pistillode truncate, shallowly 6-lobed. Pseudohermaphrodite flowers: pedicels 3–4 mm. long; filaments 4–5 mm. long, anthers 0.5 mm. long, sterile; disc lobulate; ovary subglobose, 3 mm. long and wide, glabrous; styles 1 mm. long. Female flowers: pedicels 4–6 mm. long, extending to 3 cm. in fruit; tepals oblong, 1.5–2 mm. long, 1 mm. wide, rounded at the apex, glabrous, quickly caducous; disc shallow; ovary subglobose-trilobed, 3 mm. long, 4 mm. diameter, smooth, sparingly pubescent; styles closely approximated, later becoming divaricate-deflexed, stigmas globose-reniform. Fruits trigonous, 1–1.2 cm. long, 1.2–1.5 cm. diameter, glabrous or subglabrous, smooth, somewhat shiny, reddish or purplish tinged, almost black when dried. Seeds oblong-triquetrous, 7 mm. long, 4 mm. wide, brown, very shiny. Fig. 22.
bibliographicCitation: Euphorbiaceae, A. R.-Smith. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1987

description: Shrub or small tree 1.5–8 m high; trunk very slender, smooth; bark and branches smooth. Leaves opposite, petiolate; blade elliptic to oblong, 5–17 cm long, 1.8–7.2 cm wide, apex acuminate with acumen 10–22 mm long, acute or cuneate at the base; petiole 4–11(–14) mm long. Inflorescence axillary, sometimes terminal at the same time, 1.5–2.5 cm long, 10(–15)-flowered. Flowers very fragrant; sepals ovate, up to 2.8 mm long; corolla pure white; tube (9.2–)10–15 mm long; lobes narrowly oblong to broadly ovate, 5–10.5 mm long, 1.5–5.5 mm wide; stamens inserted at 7.5–12 mm from the base; pistil 7.5–12.5 mm long; style 5.5–11 mm long; pistil-head oblong or ellipsoid; ovules 2 in each carpel. Fruits of 2 separate mericarps, these obovoid or ellipsoid, 11–18 mm long, 7–12 mm wide, rounded at the apex. Seeds ellipsoid, oblong or subglobose, 9–11 mm long, 3–7 mm in diameter.
bibliographicCitation: Apocynaceae, E.A. Omino. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 2002

description: Tree 1.5–20(–30) m high; trunk 2–50 cm in diameter; bark smooth or slightly rough, pale to dark grey; wood hard, durable. Leaves opposite or in whorls of 3–5, petiolate; blade narrowly elliptic to oblong, rarely obovate, 4–23 cm long, 1.1–8 cm wide, apex acute to acuminate with acumen 4–12 mm long, cuneate at the base or decurrent intothe petiole; petiole 5–20 mm long. Inflorescence axillary, rarely terminal, 10–30(–40)-flowered; pedicels 1–3 mm long. Flowers white, fragrant or not; sepals broadly ovate to elliptic, up to 2.5 mm long; corolla white to orange-yellow; tube greenish white, 6.2–10.5 mm long; lobes ovate or elliptic to suborbicular, 1.3–4.5(–4.8) mm long, up to 3.5 mm wide; stamens inserted 4.6–8(–9.5) mm from the base; pistil glabrous, 4.6–8.6(–9.7) mm long; pistil head ellipsoid to ovoid. Fruits yellow, subglobose to pyriform, sometimes stipitate, 13–23(–30) mm long, up to 24 mm in diameter; seeds ellipsoid to oblong, 6.5–13.5×4.5–9.5×2–4 mm. Fig. 13 (p. 40).
bibliographicCitation: Apocynaceae, E.A. Omino. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 2002

description: Tree 5–12 m high, deciduous; branchlets densely pilose. Leaves petiolate; blade narrowly ovate or obovate, 3.5–14.5 cm long, 1–5.5 cm wide, puberulous above, tomentose beneath on the main veins; petiole 3–5 mm long, densely pilose. Inflorescence several-flowered, 4.5–6.5 cm long, pubescent on all parts; bracts 2.2–3 mm long, sometimes glabrous; peduncle 1–2 cm long; pedicels 7–15 mm long. Flowers with sepals green, 2–3 mm long, 1–2 mm wide; corolla yellow and violet or dark red, 13.5–20 mm long; tube 6–9 mm long; lobes 7.5–11 mm long, 4–6 mm wide, minutely pubescent outside, papillose inside; corona appendages bright yellow, 7, broomlike and filiform to truncate; stamens inserted 1.5–1.6 mm below the corolla mouth; pistil 8–9 mm long; style 6–8 mm long; ovules 120–150 in each carpel. Fruit dark green, follicles 20–30 cm long, 5–7 mm in diameter; seeds 10–18 mm long, greenish with a dense, 35 mm long tuft of hairs at the apex. Fig. 25 (p. 72).
bibliographicCitation: Apocynaceae, E.A. Omino. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 2002

description: A cultivated shrub or tree from the Americas, to 8 m with white flowers.
bibliographicCitation: Apocynaceae, E.A. Omino. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 2002

description: Shrub or small tree from the Americas, to 9 m, much branched. Flowers white, yellow, pink or red.
bibliographicCitation: Apocynaceae, E.A. Omino. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 2002

description: A simple or sparingly-branched perennial herb up to 40 cm., arising from a woody rootstock. Stems sparingly puberulous or subglabrous. Leaves subsessile; leaf-blade linear to narrowly linear-oblanceolate, 3–7.5 cm. long, 4–7 mm. wide, acute or subacute, attentuate at the base, somewhat serrulate toward the apex, otherwise ± entire, chartaceous-subcoriaceous, lateral nerves 5–6 pairs, ascending, fairly prominent above and beneath, sparingly pubescent on the midrib and nerves beneath, otherwise ± glabrous. Stipules linear-subulate, 1.5–2.5 mm. long, with 1–2 subsessile glands on the margin, sparingly pubescent. Inflorescences uni- or bisexual, usually axillary, up to 4 cm. long, generally consisting of a ♂ spike with 1–2 ♀ flowers at the base; axis crisped-puberulous. Male bracts resembling the stipules. Male flowers very shortly pedicellate or subsessile; buds 4-lobate, subglobose, subglabrous. Female bracts cupular, accrescent, multifid, the segments linear, 3–4 mm. long, sparingly pubescent, eglandular or with 1–2 subsessile glands toward the apex, 1-flowered. Female flowers sessile; sepals 3–4, ovate-lanceolate, 1 mm. long, ciliate, pubescent without, glabrous within; ovary trilobate, 1 mm. diameter, pubescent except at the base; styles free, up to 1 cm. long, pectinate, red. Fruits trilobate, 2.5 mm. long, 3.5 mm. diameter, evenly to densely pubescent. Seeds ovoid-subglobose, 2.2 mm. long, 1.8 mm. wide, smooth, grey, with a flattened, elliptical caruncle running from the raphe to the apex.
bibliographicCitation: Euphorbiaceae, A. R.-Smith. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1987

description: A tree to 20 m. tall with grey bark and a flattish crown. Leaves up to 60 cm. long (sometimes more than double this length on sapling branches), imparipinnate; leaflets 7–11 pairs, chartaceous to coriaceous, lanceolate to ovate or broadly elliptic, frequently ± oblique, up to 13 cm. long by 5.5 cm. wide (sometimes nearly twice as large on saplings), acuminate, cordate to rounded at base, entire to shallowly undulate, stellate-pubescent beneath and sparsely so above when young, glabrescent; petiolules of paired leaflets on mature branches up to 0.8 cm. long, glabrous, but up to 3.5 cm. long and pubescent on sapling branches. Inflorescence-branches glabrous or almost so; primaries up to 30 cm. long by 3 mm. diameter; secondaries 1.0–4.5 cm. long by 0.5–1.0 mm. diameter, both orders racemosely borne; tertiaries (pedicels) 3–15 mm. long by 0.3–0.6 mm. diameter in umbellules. Flowers greenish-yellow. Styles 2, persistent. Fruits flattened-ovoid to -ellipsoid, up to 6.5 mm. long, ribbed, glabrous. Fig. 4/8, p. 13.
bibliographicCitation: Araliaceae, J. R. Tennant. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: A tree to 30 m. tall, often with a large grey extremely straight unbranched cylindrical bole of up to 15 m. tall and 1 m. diameter, generally dividing into a small number of main branches which themselves each branch in a similar manner. Leaves up to 80 cm. long, generally imparipinnate, less often paripinnate; leaflets (3–)6–7(–12) pairs, chartaceous to coriaceous, lanceolate to ovate (occasionally very broadly ovate), often markedly straight-edged, up to 14(–17) cm. long and up to 5.5(–7.5) cm. wide, acute to acuminate, generally apiculate, rarely retuse, rounded or obtuse, with a subcordate, truncate or rounded, rarely very broadly cuneate, occasionally slightly oblique base, and entire occasionally slightly undulate, generally very narrowly inrolled margins, densely stellate-tomentose when young, irregularly glabrescent to some degree (especially above) later; petiolules of paired leaflets (0–)5(–14) mm. long. Inflorescence-branches of three orders (fig. 4/2), racemosely borne, pubescent to tomentose, often irregularly glabrescent, sometimes galled (see p. 1); primaries up to 70 cm. long, 3.0–6.5 mm. diameter; secondaries up to 3–7(–12) cm. long, 0.7–1.7(–2.0) mm. diameter; tertiaries (pedicels) up to 4 mm. (not exceeding 2.5 mm. in Flora area) long, 0.3–0.8(–1.0) mm. diameter. Flowers greenish-yellow to cream; style, 2, persistent in fruit. Fruits ovoid to obovoid, occasionally ellipsoid, shortly cylindroidal or subspheroidal, 3.5–6.0 mm. long by 3.0–4.5 mm. maximum width, generally ribbed and markedly flattened, glabrous or very sparsely stellate-hairy. Fig. 4/1–5, p. 13.
bibliographicCitation: Araliaceae, J. R. Tennant. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: A tree to 25 m. tall, often with an unbranched bole up to 12 m. tall and 1.2 m. diameter. Leaves up to 55 cm. long, imparipinnate, less frequently paripinnate; leaflets (3–)4–5(–6) pairs, coriaceous, rarely chartaceous, lanceolate to narrowly ovate, very occasionally rotund, often straight-edged or oblique, up to 14.5 cm. long by 6.5 cm. wide (or larger in saplings), acute to acuminate, rarely emarginate, with a rounded to cordate (often subcordate) base, with the margins entire, often very narrowly inrolled, densely stellate-tomentose when young, later glabrescent to some extent, especially above where occasionally glabrous; petiolules of paired leaflets (0–)2–5(–14) mm. long. Inflorescence-branches puberulous to tomentose; primaries up to 40 cm. long by 2.5–4.0 mm. diameter; secondaries up to 2.7 cm. long by 0.8–1.2 mm. diameter, both orders racemosely borne; tertiaries (pedicels) up to 9 mm. (commonly 2–5 mm.) long by 0.5–0.8 mm. diameter in umbellules. Fruits flattened-ovoid, -ellipsoid, -cylindrical or ± spheroidal, 4.0–7.5 mm. long, ribbed, apart from the stylopodia and persistent styles densely (often interruptedly) covered with stellate hairs. Fig. 4/8, p. 13.
bibliographicCitation: Araliaceae, J. R. Tennant. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: A tree to 20 m. tall with grey or whitish bark and often with a large spreading crown, or a large spreading shrub (fide Gardner). Leaves up to 40–60 cm. long, often less, almost always imparipinnate, with no clear-cut differentiation between juvenile sapling leaves and leaves from mature branches, glabrous; leaflets 4–5 pairs, coriaceous, narrowly ovate to obovate, up to 12 cm. long by 5.5 cm. wide, commonly only about half these dimensions, obtuse to minutely retuse, occasionally acute or with a broad rounded apiculum, broadly cuneate to attenuate at base, entire to repand and narrowly inrolled at the margin; petiolules of lateral leaflets 4(–8) mm. long. Inflorescence-branches glabrous (occasionally somewhat tuberculate); pedicels umbellulately borne (occasionally flowers borne singly); other orders of branching may be umbellate or racemose. Petals dark reddish-brown to purple-black. Styles 5, persistent. Fruits urceolate, 7–9 mm. long, terete, deeply 5-sulcate when mature, glabrous.
bibliographicCitation: Araliaceae, J. R. Tennant. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: Shrub 1.5–5(–6) m. tall with long slender glabrous branchlets (see note). Leaf-blades elliptic to oblong-lanceolate or lanceolate, 3.3–18.5 cm. long, 1.2–6 cm. wide, typically quite large, shortly acuminate at the apex, broadly cuneate to rounded at the base, glabrous; petioles 0.6–1.2(–1.8) cm. long; stipules triangular, 1.5–2 mm. long. Inflorescences sessile, the two axillary parts forming a globose cluster up to 2 cm. diameter appearing to be more bracteated than in other species with imbricated groups of bracts and bracteoles; bracts and secondary bracts semicircular, 2 mm. long and wide, adpressed pubescent; main bracteoles cupular, 1.5–2 mm. long, adpressed brown sericeous-pubescent, second and third bracteoles beneath the main cup also cupular and ± 2 mm. long. Calyx similarly pubescent; tube 1.2 mm. long; limb 2.5 mm. long, 4-toothed or ± truncate. Corolla creamy white, adpressed pubescent outside, acuminate in bud; tube 4.5–5 mm. long; lobes broadly ovate, 3 mm. long and wide, acute; throat densely white hairy. Style 7.5–8(–9.5) mm. long, densely white pubescent save near base. Fruit subglobose, 7–10 mm. wide, very slightly didymous with slight lateral groove, glabrous or puberulous around the base of the persistent calyx-limb remnant.
bibliographicCitation: Rubiaceae, B. Verdcourt. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1976

description: Shrub 1.5–6 m. tall; stems glabrous, the older ones covered with pale longitudinally fissured corky bark. Leaf-blades lanceolate or narrowly oblong-lanceolate, 5–14 cm. long, 2–4 cm. wide, narrowed to an acute apex, cuneate at the base, mostly thin, glabrous; petiole 8 mm. long; stipules triangular, 3 mm. long, 2.5 mm. wide, keeled, glabrous, ± persistent. Flowers in sessile or shortly pedunculate inflorescences; peduncles up to 4 mm. long; bracts and bracteoles 1.5–2.5 mm. long, variable, those next to the calyx joined to form a truncate or bilobed cup, sometimes apiculate, never completely enclosing the bud, finely densely adpressed silky; sessile inflorescences form a globose nodal cluster up to 1.5 cm. diameter. Calyx enclosing the bud in young flower, with similar indumentum, the sub acute apex slightly toothed, splitting into 2 lobes as the flower develops; tube 1 mm. long, limb 4 mm. long. Corolla creamy white, glabrous or sparsely puberulous; tube funnel-shaped, 4 mm. long; lobes oblong-ovate, 2–2.5 mm. long and wide, rounded to an apiculate apex. Style densely hairy save at base, 6 mm. long; stigmatic lobes ± 1 mm. long. Fruits ripening from white to purplish black, subglobose or depressed globose, often somewhat didymous, 7–10 mm. long and wide, puberulous around the persistent calyx base.
bibliographicCitation: Rubiaceae, B. Verdcourt. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1976

description: Shrub or less often a small tree, 1.5–7(–9) m. tall with graceful glabrous rather compressed branches, bark pale brown or grey, flaking. Leaf-blades lanceolate or oblong-lanceolate, 5.4–16.6(–21.5) cm. long, (1.5–)2–4.9(–5.8) cm. wide, acute, acuminate or obtuse at the apex, cuneate or somewhat rounded at the base, sometimes those below lateral branches reduced, ± round to oblong-lanceolate, glabrous, thinly coriaceous, shiny; lateral nerves 7–12; petiole 5–8 mm. long; stipules broadly triangular, 1.5–6 mm. long, 2.5–3 mm. wide, abrupdy drawn out into an acumen 1 mm. long, deciduous. Inflorescences sessile many-flowered glomerules 1.2 cm. in diameter. Flowers scented, sessile, bracteolate; lower bracteoles connate into an irregularly bilobed cup, 1.5–2 mm. tall, puberulous outside, white-ciliate on the margin; upper forming an ovoid calyptra 4.5–5(–7) mm. long, 2.7–3 mm. wide, puberulous outside, strigose hairy inside with a curved beak at apex, at first closed and enclosing bud but later irregularly circumscissile or sometimes divided longitudinally into 2 lobes. Calyx pale pink turning brown, closed in bud, scarious, sparsely to rather densely puberulous outside either all over or only towards the apex, silky-strigose inside, 4–5.5 mm. long; tube 1.5–2.5 mm. long, 2-lobed, lobes broadly ovate, 2.25–3 mm. long, 3.25–3.5 mm. wide at the base, apiculate at the apex. Corolla white or whitish rose, obovoid in bud, 6 mm. long, acute, puberulous or glabrous outside; tube tinged greenish, 3.5–4.75 mm. long, 2.5–3.5 mm. wide at throat; lobes ovate-triangular, 2.5–2.8 mm. long, 1.7–2 mm. wide. Style white, ± 6.5 mm. long, densely pubescent save at the base, bifid at the apex. Fruit green, flushed red, becoming wine-red or black, globose, 6–8 mm. diameter, glabrous, crowned by the persistent calyx-limb; flesh green and sweet. Fig. 96.
bibliographicCitation: Rubiaceae, B. Verdcourt. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1976

description: Slender spreading shrub 1.2–3.5 m. tall (see note after subsp. harleyi); stems glabrous, the older with grey fissured bark. Leaf-blades usually narrowly lanceolate, or narrowly elliptic to oblong-elliptic, 2.5–16(–19) cm. long, 1.3–5.7 cm. wide, mostly slenderly acutely acuminate at the apex but sometimes obtuse or the actual acumen rounded to subacute, cuneate to almost rounded at the base, rather thin, glabrous; petioles 0.4–1 cm. long; stipules triangular, 1.5–5 mm. long, 2–5 mm. wide, keeled, often apiculate, glabrous or pubescent, deciduous. Flowers not scented (?always), in sessile or shortly to distinctly pedunculate 3–8-flowered pubescent to glabrous inflorescences; when sessile the two at each side appearing as a single cluster; peduncles 0.2–1.8 cm. long; secondary peduncles 0–3 mm. long; bracts andbracteoles ovate-triangular, all rather similar, 1.5–3.5 mm. long, usually united into boat-shaped cups, acute, apiculate or caudate at the apex, mostly rather coarsely ± spreading pubescent or glabrous. Calyx with similar indumentum; tube 0.5–2.5 mm. long; limb-tube 1.3–2 mm. long, usually with distinct but distant acute or apiculate teeth, or shallowly undulate-toothed or even ± truncate. Corolla very pale lilac, white or pink-tinged, glabrous, slightly pubescent or usually puberulous all over with minute adpressed or slightly spreading hairs; tube 4.5–7 mm. long; lobes oblong-ovate to ovate, 1.7–2 mm. long and wide, obtuse or acute. Style up to 1.1 cm. long, densely hairy; stigmatic lobes 1.5–2 mm. long. Fruit often glaucous at first, becoming red-purple or black, subglobose, usually slightly compressed and obscurely didymous, 6–9 mm. long, 9–12 mm. wide, 7–8 mm. thick. Seeds ± shiny, chestnut, hemispherical, 6–7.5 mm. long, 3.5 mm. thick.
bibliographicCitation: Rubiaceae, B. Verdcourt. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1976

description: Small tree up to 10 m. tall with glabrous compressed branches. Leaf-blades ovate-oblong to oblong-lanceolate or elliptic, (5.5–)9.5–17 cm. long, (1.7–)3–6.8 cm. wide, obtuse to acute or ± acuminate, rounded to broadly cuneate at the base, sometimes those below lateral branches smaller and broadly elliptic, glabrous, shining or dull, often drying brown beneath, midrib often slightly impressed above and prominent beneath, the venation mostly raised on both surfaces; lateral nerves ± 8–11; petiole (4–)6–10 mm. long; stipules triangular or ovate-triangular, 3.5–6.5 mm. long, 3.5–5 mm. wide, shortly mucronate, puberulous outside, glabrous inside but with numerous small hair-like glands at the base, persistent or falling. Inflorescences sessile or shortly pedunculate, 2–4-flowered; peduncle 0–1.1 cm. long; bracts ovate or triangular, 2–4 mm. long, acute; pedicels 0–9 mm. long, with 1–2 pairs of bracteoles 3–7 mm. long, irregularly connate to form a cupule; bracts, bracteoles and peduncle densely shortly pubescent Calyx-tube obconic, 2.5 mm. long, glabrous; limb at first oblong-ellipsoid to elongate-suburceolate, 0.72–1.3 cm. long, with ± 4 triangular teeth 1–2 mm. long, but during flowering becoming deeply split on one side, puberulous outside, densely adpressed pubescent inside. Corolla white, glabrous outside; tube 1–1.1 cm. long, 1.5–2 mm. wide and widened to the densely hairy throat; lobes spreading, ovate-oblong, 1.2 cm. long, 5 mm. wide, acute. Style 2.3 cm. long. Fruit subglobose, 1.2–1.4 cm. long, 1.2 cm. wide glabrous, obscurely to rather distinctly 8–9-ribbed in dry state, crowned by the persistent calyx-limb. Seeds 9 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Rubiaceae, B. Verdcourt. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1976

description: Shrub or small tree 1–3(–4.5) m. tall, occasionally weak and almost trailing; stems glabrous, the bark peeling in long strips on older stems. Leaf-blades elliptic, oblong-elliptic or lanceolate, 2–11.5(–19) cm. long, 1–4.2 (–4.5) cm. wide, ± acute, the actual apex± obtuse, less often acuminate (in some cultivated specimens), cuneate to subcordate at the base, thinly coriaceous, glabrous, often with pale minute white specks particularly near the midrib above; petiole 5–9 mm. long; stipules triangular, 2.5–4 mm. long, keeled, glabrous. Inflorescences sessile or practically so, the two opposite together forming a globose cluster up to 1.5 cm. diameter or peduncles up to 4 mm. long in one variant; components quite glabrous outside or almost imperceptibly puberulous; bracteoles cupular, tightly surrounding the calyx-base, ± 1 mm. tall. Calyx shallowly cup-shaped, 1.5(–2) mm. long, glabrous outside or imperceptibly puberulous or in one variant silky pubescent, glabrescent to densely pubescent inside, often with pale marks outside, usually truncate, sometimes undulate or faintly toothed or becoming lacerate. Flowers sweetly scented; corolla white; tube (2–)4 mm. long, glabrous outside or adpressed puberulous in one variant, densely white hairy at the throat; lobes ovate, 1.5–2 mm. long and wide. Style densely white hairy; disc prominent. Fruits globose, 7–9 mm. diameter, glabrous, ± white-dotted, somewhat didymous. Seeds ± semiglobose, ± 6 mm. long, 4 mm. wide.
bibliographicCitation: Rubiaceae, B. Verdcourt. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1976

description: Small tree or shrub 0.6–9(–?12) m. tall but probably rarely over 3.5 m.; stems slender, glabrous or more often shortly pubescent; bark reddish brown, peeling in long strips on the older stems. Leaf-blades oblong, elliptic, ovate-elliptic or sometimes ovate or almost round, 0.4–9(–11) cm. long, 0.4–4.5(–4.7) cm. wide, subacute to acuminate at the apex, cuneate to rounded or truncate at the base or in the case of leaves supporting lateral branchlets often subcordate to distinctly cordate, glabrous to distinctly pubescent or coarsely hairy particularly beneath; occasionally there are some pairs of very small leaves; petiole 3–5 mm. long, glabrous or more usually pubescent; stipules 1 mm. long with apiculum 1 mm. long, hairy. Inflorescences sessile or rarely peduncles up to 2.5 mm. long, the opposite parts usuallyjoined to form a globose cluster at the node; paired basal bracts ovate-triangular, 3 mm. long, 2 mm. wide, acuminate; secondary bracts triangular, 1.5 mm. long, 2 mm. wide, each pair supporting 3 triads of flowers each with another set of bracts; main bracteoles at base of calyx joined to form a 2–3-lobed cup. Flowers practically scentless (Palways). Calyx mostly with spreading white hairs; tube ± 0.5 mm. long, limb-tube about equal with distinct triangular teeth ± the same length. Corolla white or tube sometimes greenish, usually densely spreading pubescent, less often glabrous or glabrescent; tube funnel-shaped, 3–4.5 mm. long, sometimes constricted near the base; lobes ovate, 1.5–2 mm. long, 1.3 mm. wide. Style densely white hairy. Fruits globose, red or orange-red, 7–10 mm. diameter, glabrous or slightly pubescent. Fig.95.
bibliographicCitation: Rubiaceae, B. Verdcourt. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1976

description: A small epiphytic or lithophytic herb to 8 cm. high. Pseudobulbs clustered, ovoid, 1.5 cm. long, 1 cm. in diameter, 2–3-leaved above. Leaves erect-spreading, ligulate or linear-ligulate, 5–7 cm. long, 7–9 mm. wide, rounded and slightly unequally bilobed at the apex, green. Inflorescence erect, unbranched, 3.5–7 cm. high, 3–8-flowered; peduncle terete, 2–3 cm. long, pubescent; bracts broadly ovate or ovate-orbicular, 4–6 mm. long, 3 mm. wide, acuminate. Flowers erect-spreading, acrid smelling; sepals and petals lime-green with a purple wash at the base; lip white, side lobes with purple spots. Dorsal sepal lanceolate, acuminate, convex, 7 mm. long, 2.5–2.75 mm. wide; lateral sepals obliquely triangular, 3-nerved, 8–9 mm. long, 5–5.5 mm. wide, acuminate; mentum 4.25 mm. high; sepals all sparsely pubescent on outer surface. Petals linear-ligulate, 5.5–6 mm. long, 1 mm. wide, acute. Lip strongly recurved, shortly clawed, 3-lobed in the middle, 7 mm. long, 5 mm. wide; side lobes erect, suborbicular; mid-lobe fleshy ovate-lanceolate, acuminate, 3.5–4 mm. long, 2.75 mm. wide, slightly rugulose-bullate; disc pubescent, with a semi-spherical rugulose almost glabrous callus. Column short, semi-terete; column-foot 4.3 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: A small epiphytic herb up to 16 cm. high. Pseudobulbs ovoid or subspherical, 1–2.5 cm. long, 5–10 mm. wide, browny green, clustered, covered when young with 2–3 obtuse ± scarious sheaths, 3–4-leaved above. Leaves spreading or almost recurved, oblanceolate, oblong or elliptic-lanceolate, subacute, 0.8–8 cm. long, 5–13 mm. wide, green with a purple margin and irregularly purple-spotted. Inflorescence racemose or rarely poorly branched, erect, 6–14 cm. high, laxly 7–12-flowered; peduncle 2–6 cm. long, terete or slightly compressed; bracts broadly ovate, acuminate, 6–11 mm. long, 5–7.5 mm. wide, sparsely pubescent. Flowers ± secund, aniseed scented; pedicellate ovary 5–7 mm. long. Dorsal sepal lanceolate, acuminate, convex, incurved, 8.5–11.5 mm. long, 1.75–3.25 mm. wide; lateral sepals obliquely or subfalcately triangular, apex longly subulate-acuminate, 11–15 mm. long, 4–5.5 mm. wide; mentum 3–4.5 mm. long; sepals all sparsely pubescent, yellowish olive-brown. Petals curved-lanceolate or oblanceolate, acute or acuminate, 6–7.5 mm. long, 1.25–2 mm. wide, olive-ochre-yellow. Lip recurved, shortly 3-lobed, with a short claw, 4–5 mm. long, 3.5 mm. wide, pubescent; side lobes erect, rotund-triangular, 0.5–0.7 mm. long; mid-lobe strongly recurved, ovate-lanceolate, acute, slightly grooved, 2.75–3.75 mm. long, 1.5–2.75 mm. wide; lip white with purple side lobes and a purple-margined mid-lobe. Column short, broad; anther hemispherical.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: A suberect to pendent epiphytic plant, to 50 cm. long. Pseudobulbs subspherical, dorso-ventrally compressed, prostrate on the substrate, conspicuously 1-noded, 1–4.8 cm. in diameter, 2–3-leaved at the apex. Leaves petiolate, oblanceolate, oblong-lanceolate or oblong-elliptic, 9–28 cm. long, 2.6–6 cm. wide, acute to shortly acuminate; petiole subcylindrical, articulated at or above middle, 5–14 cm. long. Inflorescence erect, suberect or pendulous, unbranched or branched, laxly many-flowered, 6–40 cm. long; peduncle ± covered with imbricating scarious acute sheaths; rhachis terete, densely pubescent; branches suberect, 1–few, 3–11 cm. long; bracts papery, ovate-lanceolate, long-acuminate, densely pubescent, 6–14 mm. long. Flowers white, yellow or mustard-yellow, commonly marked with brown or red-brown, fragrant, pubescent on outer surface. Dorsal sepal elliptic-lanceolate to oblong-elliptic, 6.5–7 mm. long, 2.7–4 mm. wide, rounded; lateral sepals obliquely triangular-ovate, 6.5–8 mm. long, 4.5–6 mm. wide, acute; mentum 4.3–5.8 mm. high. Petals oblanceolate, 5.7–6.5 mm. long, 1.6–2.2 mm. wide, truncate. Lip recurved, obscurely 3-lobed, 6.3–7.3 mm. long, 4.7–5.7 mm. wide; side lobes erect, narrowly oblong; mid-lobe oblong-ovate to semirotund, 2.2–2.8 mm. long, 2.6–3.6 mm. wide, subacute to rounded; disc with a central fleshy ridge, puberulent. Column short, stout, semiterete, 1 mm. long. Fig. 85.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: A very variable, erect, epiphytic or rarely lithophytic plant, 10–50 cm. long. Stems clustered, terete, to 30 cm. long, 4–7 cm. wide, clothed below by up to 3 tubular sheaths, 2–5-leaved above. Leaves linear-ligulate to linear-lanceolate, suberect, acute or subacute, 10–23 cm. long, 0.7–2 cm. wide, articulated to a tubular sheathing base. Inflorescence often shorter than the leaves, racemose or shortly branched, 5–20 cm. long; peduncle terete, covered with papery sheaths, 2–70 cm. long; rhachis terete, short, glabrous; branches short, suberect, 1–5 cm. long; bracts more or less imbricate, ovate, acute or acuminate, 2–4(–8) cm. long. Flowers glabrous on outer surface, white, tinged yellow and purple, to greenish yellow. Dorsal sepal lanceolate, acute, 6.6–8.4 mm. long, 2.8–3.7 mm. wide; lateral sepals very obliquely triangular-ovate, acute, 7.6–11 mm. long, 5.7–8 mm. wide, mentum conical, 5.5–9.5 mm. high. Petals oblanceolate, subacute or obtuse, 5.5–6.7 mm. long, 1.5–1.8 mm. wide. Lip clawed, 3-lobed above the middle, 6–9 mm. long, 5–7.3 mm. wide, ± pubescent on claw and in apical half; side lobes erect, rounded sinus between mid-lobe and side lobes obvious; mid-lobe triangular-ovate, acute, reflexed; disc with a fleshy central ridge dilated towards the apex. Column short, terete, truncate, 1 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: An epiphytic herb, 13.5–33 cm. high. Pseudobulbs tightly clustered, from a short creeping rhizome, narrowly cylindric, 6–18 cm. long, 1–1.5 mm. in diameter, clothed in membranous basal sheaths. Leaf linear, obtuse or rarely subacute, cuneate below, 7.5–15 cm. long, 2.5–10 mm. broad, coriaceous, articulated 1–3 mm. above the pseudobulb apex. Inflorescence mostly shorter than the leaf, racemose or paniculate, 6.5–17.5 cm. long, up to 20-flowered; peduncle slender, 4.5–8.5 cm. long, with a 10 mm. long basal sheath; bracts triangular-ovate, apiculate, amplexicaul, 3–4.5 mm. long. Flowers yellow, spotted purple. Dorsal sepal triangular-ovate to triangular, 3–6 mm. long, 3–5 mm. broad; mentum conical, up to 5 mm. long. Petals broadly elliptic, obtuse, 3.8–6 mm. long, 0.8–1.8 mm. broad. Lip strongly recurved, subsessile, obscurely 3-lobed, 3.5–7 mm. long, 1.8–4.8 mm. broad; side lobes erect, rounded; mid-lobe geniculate, shortly apiculate, 1.7–2.5 mm. long, 0.9–2.5 mm. broad. Column 1–1.5 mm. long; foot 3–3.5 mm. long; pollinia ovoid-globose
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: An erect epiphytic plant, 15–20 cm. high. Pseudobulbs ellipsoid-lenticulate, glossy yellow-orange when dry, up to 4 cm. long, 2 cm. wide, 1–2-leaved at apex and usually subtended by ± 2 cataphylls. Leaves leathery, elliptic or oblong-ligulate, rounded and a little unequally bilobed at the apex, 5–16 cm. long, 1.8–2.7 cm. wide, petiolate. Inflorescence erect, pubescent, simple or branched, up to 25 cm. high, subdensely many-flowered; peduncle up to 10 cm. long, terete or subangled, pubescent. Flowers suberect, yellow or gold; pedicellate ovary arcuate, densely pubescent. Dorsal sepal lanceolate, acute, 12–14 mm. long, 3–3.5 mm. wide, slightly concave; lateral sepals obliquely triangular-lanceolate, acute, 15–17 mm. long, 5–5.5 mm. wide. Petals linear-oblanceolate, acute, 8.5–11 mm. long, 1.5 mm. wide. Lip somewhat lanceolate, indistinctly 3-lobed, 9.5–11.5 mm. long, 4.8–5.5 mm. wide; side lobes erect, shortly rotund-triangular, 1 mm. long; mid-lobe strongly recurved, lanceolate-triangular, acuminate, 4.5–5 mm. long, 2.5 mm. wide, fleshy; disc with a linear low callus at base. Column slightly incurved, 2.5–3.5 mm. long, 3-lobed at apex.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: A glabrous epiphytic, or rarely terrestrial, herb, 11–55 cm. high. Pseudobulbs from a short creeping rhizome, loosely clustered, narrowly to broadly conical, ± ridged, 6–29 cm. long, 2–11 mm. in diameter, clothed in 2–3 basal membranous sheaths. Leaf ovate to obovate, acute or obtuse, auriculate at the base, 5.6–26 cm. long, 1.6–2.9 cm. broad, coriaceous, articulated 5–8 mm. above the apex of the pseudobulb. Inflorescence shorter than the leaf, a 1–6-branched raceme, 7.7–23.5 cm. long, up to 30-flowered; peduncle stout, 3.4–10.2 cm. long; basal sheath membranaceous; bracts spreading, ovate-triangular, apiculate, 5–10.5 mm. long. Flowers white, pink or purple. Dorsal sepal ovate-triangular, apiculate, 8–12.5 mm. long, 3.3–4.4 mm. broad; lateral sepals oblique, triangular, 9–11.5 mm. long, 8–9.5 mm. broad, spreading, strongly erosely keeled on outer side, mentum conical, up to 9 mm. high. Petals spathulate or linear, acute to obtuse, 7.5–9.5 mm. long, 2.5–3.5 mm. broad. Lip strongly recurved in basal third, ± clawed, distinctly 3-lobed in lower third, 8–10.5 mm. long, 5.5–7.5 mm. broad; side lobes rounded, erect; mid-lobe rounded-subquadrate, shortly apiculate, 2.5–5 mm. long, 2.5–4.5 mm. broad; callus central in apical half. Column semi-terete, 1.5–2.5 mm. long; foot 9–11 mm. long; pollinia quadrate-globose.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: An erect, suberect or arching epiphytic herb. Pseudobulbs superposed, new shoots given off just below centre of previous year’s pseudobulb, fusiform, 5 cm. long, 4 mm. in diameter, 2-leaved, covered when young by 2–3 scarious sheaths. Leaves linear, grass- like, 4.5–17 cm. long, 5–6 mm. wide, acute. Inflorescence erect, cylindrical, 4–10 cm. long, racemose, subtended at base by 1–2 long compressed acuminate sheaths, the upper sheath more or less overlapping the basal flowers; bracts setaceous, 1–4 mm. long. Flowers white or pink. Dorsal sepal ovate, 2.5 mm. long, 1.6 mm. wide, shortly acuminate; lateral sepals slightly obliquely ovate or oblong-ovate, acute, 3 mm. long, 1.7 mm. wide; mentum obscurely rounded. Petals elliptic, subacute, 2.5 mm. long, 1.5 mm. wide. Lip 3-lobed just above base, shortly clawed, hastate, 3.5 mm. long, 1.7 mm. wide; side lobes small, triangular or obliquely triangular; mid-lobe lanceolate, acute, 3.2 mm. long, 1.3 mm. wide; callus on base of mid-lobe of 2 curved, fleshy raised ridges. Column very short, truncate.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: A small epiphytic plant to 12 cm. high. Pseudobulbs clustered, ovoid to ovoid-conical, 1–23 cm. long, 0.5–0.9 cm. diameter, 2–3-leaved at the apex. Leaves narrowly oblong, oblong-oblanceolate or linear, subcoriaceous, spreading or suberect, 5–10.5 cm. long, 0.7–2.1 cm. wide, rounded or minutely apiculate at apex, articulated at base to a conduplicate petiole, 1–1.6 cm. long. Inflorescence erect, longer than the leaves, 2–6-flowered; peduncle subcompressed, pubescent, 5 cm. long; bracts ovate to cordate, carinate, densely pubescent, mucronate, 5–7 mm. long, up to 5 mm. wide. Flowers variable in colour and size, pubescent on outer surface; sepals green, olive-green or yellow-green (rarely yellow); lip white, lined on side lobes with purple; callus yellow, often spotted crimson. Dorsal sepal ovate, concave, acute or apiculate, 8–13 mm. long 4.5–7 mm. wide; lateral sepals obliquely ovate-triangular, acute, 8–14 mm. long, 7–10 mm. wide; mentum broadly conical, 6.5–9.5 mm. high. Petals oblanceolate, obtuse or apiculate at apex, 6.5–9.6 mm. long, 2–3 (–4) mm. wide. Lip shortly and broadly clawed, 3-lobed, strongly recurved in basal half, 8–11 mm. long, 6–9.5 mm. wide, when spread out; side lobes erect, rounded, 4 mm. wide, densely clavate-pubescent; mid-lobe oblong or ovate, fleshy, 4–5 mm. long, 2–3 mm. wide, acute, glabrous; disc fleshy, densely clavate-pubescent, with a conical callus at base of mid-lobe between the side lobes. Column short, stout, 3 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: An epiphytic herb, 25–33 cm. high. Pseudobulbs tightly clustered, from a creeping rhizome, narrowly cylindric, 11.8–13 cm. long, 2.5 mm. in diameter, clothed in 1–3 membranous basal sheaths. Leaf linear, fleshy, cuneate below, retuse above, 11.7–21 cm. long, 2.5–6.5 mm. broad, articulated 3 mm. above the pseudobulb apex. Inflorescence shorter than the leaf, unbranched, 6.2–7 cm. long; peduncle slender, 5–6 cm. long, lacking a basal sheath; bracts triangular, amplexicaul, 1.5–2 mm. long. Flowers white. Dorsal sepal triangular-ovate, shortly apiculate, 6–8.7 mm. long, 2.5–3.6 mm. broad; lateral sepals obliquely triangular, 7–7.5 mm. long, 6.4–7 mm. broad; mentum conical, 6–6.5 mm. long. Petals obovate-lanceolate, obtuse, 6.5–7 mm. long, 2–2.5 mm. broad. Lip strongly recurved, sessile, distinctly 3-lobed in the basal half, 9–9.5 mm. long, 6.5–7 mm. broad; side lobes erect, triangular-ovate; mid-lobe subquadrate, truncate or retuse, bullate, glandular-pubescent in basal two-thirds, 4.5–5 mm. long and broad. Column subterete, 2–2.6 mm. long; foot 6–6.5 mm. long; pollinia subquadrate-globose.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: A small epiphytic herb to ± 15 cm. tall. Pseudobulbs borne on a short creeping rhizome, curved-conical, 2–3-noded, 3–5 cm. long, 5–8 mm. in diameter. Leaves unknown. Inflorescences produced after the leaves have fallen (?), simple or few- branched, up to 7.5 cm. long, up to 20-flowered; peduncle and rhachis sparsely pubescent; bracts ovate or triangular, acuminate, up to 3 mm. long. Flowers white, glabrous on outer surface. Dorsal sepal ovate, acute, 4.2 mm. long, 2.4 mm. broad; lateral sepals obliquely ovate-triangular, subacute, 5.5 mm. long, 4.5 mm. broad, forming a rounded subconical mentum 3.5 mm. high. Petals spathulate, apiculate, 3.3 mm. long, 1.2 mm. broad. Lip obscurely 3- lobed, rhombic in outline, pubescent in apical half, 4 mm. long, 3.6 mm. broad; callus fleshy, 1/3–1/2 length of the lip, papillose. Column short, stout, 1 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: An epiphytic plant to 35 cm. long. Stems approximate, pseudobulbous at the base, slender above, 3–4-leaved, 10–12 cm. long, 1–2 mm. diameter; pseudobulbs conical- ovoid, 5–10 mm. long, 4–7 mm. diameter. Leaves suberect, linear, obtuse or unequally bilobed at the apex, 13–22 cm. long including the sheath, 3.4–5 mm. wide, yellow-green. Inflorescence more or less erect, unbranched or with up to 4 secund branches, 7–24 mm. long; peduncle 4–15 cm. long, clothed in scarious imbricating sheaths; branches 1.5–4.5 cm. long; rhachis terete, pubescent; bracts spreading and recurved, broadly ovate or suborbicular, caudate-acuminate, 5–11 mm. long, 5–6 mm. wide, ± crimson, glabrous or sparsely pubescent. Flowers white or cream marked with red, lip red-spotted, fragrant. Dorsal sepal lanceolate or oblong-lanceolate, subacute or apiculate, 7.5–9 mm. long, 2.5–3.25 mm. wide, convex; lateral sepals obliquely triangular-lanceolate, acute or apiculate, 8.5–12 mm. long, 4–6 mm. wide; mentum rounded, 3.5–5 mm. long. Petals oblanceolate or subspathulate, acute or subacute, 6.5–7.75 mm. long, 1.5–2 mm. wide. Lip recurved, shortly clawed, 3-lobed in middle, 8–10.5 mm. long, 6.25–7 mm. wide; side lobes erect, triangular-ovate, obtuse or rounded, 2.3–2.6 mm. long; mid-lobe recurved, quadrate-suborbicular or broadly semi-elliptic, rotund, 3–3.75 mm. long, 2.74–4 mm. wide, very slightly undulate; disc with a low longitudinal callus to base of mid-lobe, clavate-pilose on to side lobes and base of mid-lobe. Column porrect, semiterete, 2.75 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: An epiphytic plant. Pseudobulbs not seen. Leaf obovate, acute, auriculate at the base, 12.5 cm. long, 2.7 cm. broad, articulated 4.5 mm. above the apex of the pseudobulb. Inflorescence ± equal to leaf in length, a simple raceme, 11.8 cm. long, up to 9- flowered; peduncle stout, 5.3 cm. long; basal sheath membranaceous; bracts broadly ovate, amplexicaul, 1 mm. long. Dorsal sepal ovate-lanceolate, acuminate, 10 mm. long, 2.5 mm. broad; lateral sepals obliquely triangular, 9 mm. long, 7.5 mm. broad; mentum conical, 7 mm. long. Petals linear-lanceolate, 9.5 mm. long, 2 mm. broad. Lip weakly recurved, elliptic, obscurely 3-lobed, 11 mm. long, 5 mm. broad; side lobes elliptic, suberect; mid-lobe subquadrate, truncate, margin erose, 4.5 mm. long, 4 mm. broad; disc with 5 crispate longitudinal lamellae to apex. Column subterete, arcuate, 4–5 mm. long; foot 7 mm. long; pollinia 8.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: A small epiphytic plant up to 5.5 cm. high. Pseudobulbs very small, conical, 1.3 cm. long, 0.6 cm. in diameter, 2-leaved at the apex. Leaves ligulate to oblong-ligulate, 4 cm. long, 0.7 cm. wide, rounded and unequally bilobed at apex. Inflorescence erect, up to 4 cm. high. 2–6-flowered; peduncle terete, shortly pubescent; bracts ovate, acuminate, 3–4 mm. long, 1.5 mm. wide. Flowers erect, sparsely pubescent on outer surface, sepals and petals rose-red to pale pink; lip yellowish; column dark purple. Dorsal sepal ovate, acuminate, 6 mm. long, 2.6 mm. wide; lateral sepals obliquely ovate-triangular, 7–9 mm. long on longer margin, 6–7 mm. wide. Petals oblong-ligulate, acute, 4–5 mm. long, 1.2 mm. wide. Lip with a long narrow claw, fleshy especially in apical half, 7–9 mm. long, 3.2–3.6 mm. wide, 3-lobed in middle, only slightly recurved; side lobes erect, very narrow, triangular, subacute; mid-lobe fleshy, oblong, acute to apiculate. Column 1.3 cm. long; rostellum pointed.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: A glabrous epiphytic or lithophytic plant, 6–24.5 cm. tall. Pseudobulbs from a short creeping rhizome, loosely clustered, narrowly cylindric to conical, 1.4–18 cm. long, 0.2–1.2 cm. in diameter, clothed in 1–6 membranous basal sheaths. Leaf obovate, ovate or elliptic, acute, to obtuse, auriculate at the base, 3.2–36 cm. long, 1.2–5.5 cm. broad, coriaceous, articulated 2–6 mm. above the apex of the pseudobulb, Inflorescence usually longer than the leaf, paniculate or rarely racemose, 4.4–29 cm. long, bearing up to 50 flowers successively; peduncle slender to stout, 3.2–21.5 cm. long; basal sheath membranous; bracts ovate-triangular, acuminate, amplexicaul, 2.5–4.5 mm. long. Flowers very variable in colour and size, white, yellow, green, pink or purple, ± yellow at the base of the lip. Dorsal sepal ovate-triangular, apiculate, 4–8 mm. long, 2–4.5 mm. broad; lateral sepals obliquely triangular, apiculate, 5–8 mm. long, 3–6 mm. broad; mentum conical, up to 7 mm. high. Petals linear to spathulate, acute or obtuse, 3.5–7.5 mm. long, 1–2.5 mm. broad. Lip strongly recurved, ± shortly clawed, distinctly 3-lobed in the apical half, 4–7.8 mm. long, 3–6 mm. broad; side lobes porrect, rounded in front; mid-lobe oblong-quadrate, shortly apiculate, 1.2–4.5 mm. long, 1.5–3.5 mm. broad; callus fleshy, ± central. Column semiterete, 0.5–3.5 mm. long; foot 1.5–6.5 mm. long; pollinia ellipsoid-globose.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: A dwarf epiphytic herb to 7 cm. high. Pseudobulbs clustered, ovoid, 1.1 cm. long, 1 cm. in diameter, commonly 3-leaved at the apex. Leaves narrowly elliptic-lanceolate, spreading, curved, conduplicate, obtuse or rounded at the apex, to 4 cm. long, 0.8 cm. broad, sage-green, spotted and lined with purple. Inflorescence unbranched, erect, 3–9-flowered, to 5.5 cm. long; peduncle terete, villose, to 2 cm. long; bracts ovate, acuminate, 3 mm. long, 2 mm. wide. Flowers yellow or dull light green; sepals lined with red; lip magenta with a greeny yellow callus. Dorsal sepal ovate or oblong-ovate, concave, subacute, 5.5 mm. long, 3 mm. broad; lateral sepals obliquely ovate-triangular, acute, 6.5–8.5 mm. long, 6–7 mm. broad, forming with the column-foot a prominent conical mentum to 6 mm. high. Petals narrowly linear-lanceolate, subacute, 5.2 mm. long, 1.1 mm. wide. Lip geniculate, with a long claw nearly half the length of the lip, 3-lobed in the middle, 9–12 mm. long, 5 mm. broad; side lobes erect, rounded, 2.5 mm. long and broad; mid-lobe fleshy, bullate, oblong-lanceolate, acute, 4 mm. long, 2.4 mm. broad; callus fleshy, glabrous; disc pubescent at base. Column short, subterete, stout, 1 mm. long, with a cluster of long bristles below the stigma, washed and spotted crimson; foot long, slender, pubescent. Fig. 83A–H, p. 388.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: An epiphytic or rarely lithophytic herb, 11.5–28.5 cm. high. Pseudobulbs spaced on an ascending rhizome, narrowly conical, 3–8 cm. long, 2–6 mm. in diameter, clothed in 3–4 loose basal sheaths. Leaf lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, acute, cuneate below, 7.5–15.5 cm. long, 1.1–2.3 cm. broad, coriaceous, articulated 2–6 mm. above the pseudobulb apex. Inflorescence shorter or longer than the leaf, a simple raceme, 3.5–15 cm. long, up to 11 flowers borne in succession; peduncle slender, 2.4–12.7 cm. long, with a membranous basal sheath; bracts triangular to obovate, amplexicaul, ± acuminate, 3–7 mm. long. Flower lemon-yellow, sometimes with red streaks or darker spotting at the base of the lip. Dorsal sepal ovate to ovate- triangular, 6–10 mm. long, 3–5 mm. broad; lateral sepals spreading, obliquely ovate-triangular, 6–11 mm. long, 5–11 mm. broad; mentum ovoid-conical, to 10 mm. long. Petals narrowly obovate, obtuse, 6–10 mm. long, 1.3–3.3 mm. broad. Lip strongly recurved in the middle, ± distinctly 3-lobed in the apical third, 6.5–11 mm. long, 4–8 mm. broad; side lobes erect, broadly elliptic; mid-lobe rounded-subquadrate, apiculate, to 5 mm. long, 5.5 mm. broad; callus obscure, fleshy, ± central. Column subterete, 1.5–2.5 mm. long; foot 5.5–9.5 mm. long; pollinia ovoid.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: An epiphytic or lithophytic plant, 8–39 cm. high. Stems clustered, erect, fleshy, somewhat pseudobulbous at base, narrowly conical, to 20 cm. high, 8 mm. diameter at base, 3–5-leaved towards apex; roots pinkish purple when cut. Leaves deciduous, suberect, narrowly linear-lanceolate, grass-like, acute, to 29 cm. long, 6–8.5 mm. wide, Inflorescence unbranched, mostly borne after the leaves have fallen, shorter than the leaves, 4–11 cm. long, subdensely many-flowered; peduncle covered with 2 scarious acute sheaths; rhachis sparsely setulose-pubescent; bracts broadly deltoid-ovate, acuminate, 1–2 mm. long. Flowers erect-spreading, pale lilac-rose with purple to magenta. Dorsal sepal oblong-elliptic, rounded or slightly emarginate, 3.5–4 mm. long, 1.7–2 mm. wide; lateral sepals rotund-triangular, obtuse, dorsally shortly cuspidate below the apex, 4–5 mm. long and wide; mentum conical, subacute, 3–3.5 mm. long. Petals ligulate or spathulate-ligulate, 3.5 mm. long, 0.6–1.4 mm. wide. Lip shortly clawed, ecallose, very broadly 3-lobed in apical half, 3.5–4.5 mm. long, 6–7.1 mm. wide, whole surface farinaceous pubescent; side lobes spreading, elliptic-oblong, 3 mm. long, 2–2.5 mm. wide; mid-lobe broadly triangular, obtuse, 1–1.5 mm. long, 1.5–2 mm. wide. Column 2 mm. long, almost terete.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: A pendulous epiphytic plant. Stems (or pseudobulbs) superposed, given off from the middle of the preceeding growth, cylindrical or more or less fusiform, 4–12 cm. long, 3–4 mm. wide, covered at first with leaf-bases, 3–5-leaved above. Leaves more or less spreading, lanceolate or ligulate-oblong, acute, 2–8 cm. long, 5–15 mm. wide. Inflorescence laxly branching, 4–7 cm. long, many-flowered; branches 3–4; peduncle slender, slightly compressed, pubescent, 2–3 cm. long; bracts lanceolate, acuminate, 1.5–6 mm. long. Flowers spreading, glabrous, green with a yellow-green lip, anther brown or crimson. Dorsal sepal slightly incurved, elliptic-oblong, concave, obtuse, 4–5 mm. long, 2.5 mm. wide; lateral sepals obliquely triangular-ovate, apiculate, 6 mm. long, 4.5–5 mm. wide, forming with the column-foot a broadly rounded mentum 3.5 mm. long, 3 mm. wide, shortly bilobed at apex. Petals spathulate-oblong, rounded at apex, 3.5 mm. long, 1.25 mm. wide. Lip strongly curved, broadly clawed, 3-lobed, 5.5 mm. long, 3.5 mm. wide, margins recurved; side lobes short, rotund; mid-lobe broadly quadrate-ovate, more or less truncate, fleshy, rugulose, 2.25 mm. long, 2.8 mm. wide, margins crenulate, apex recurved, Column semiterete, 2–2.5 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: A glabrous epiphytic herb, 12–16 cm. high. Pseudobulbs distantly placed on an elongated rhizome, conical, 2.6–4.5 cm. long, 4–5 mm. in diameter, ± ridged, shiny, clothed in 3–4 membranous basal sheaths. Leaf linear, acute to obtuse, cuneate below, 9.5–11.3 cm. long, 6–9.5 mm. broad, coriaceous, articulated 4–5 mm. above the pseudobulb apex. Inflorescence shorter than the leaf, simply racemose, 4–5 cm. long, up to 5 flowers borne successively; peduncle slender, 2.6–3.5 cm. long, with a membranaceous basal sheath; bracts triangular, amplexicaul, 1.5–2 mm. long. Flowers white; callus ochre-yellow; anther-cap purple. Dorsal sepal ovate-lanceolate, acuminate, 7.5–11.5 mm. long, 2.5–3.2 cm. broad; lateral sepals narrowly triangular, oblique, acuminate, 8–14 mm. long, 5–7 mm. broad; mentum broadly conical, to 5–6 mm. high. Petals spreading, linear-lanceolate, acute, 6.5–8 mm. long, 1–2 mm. broad. Lip strongly recurved in the middle, sessile, distinctly 3-lobed in the middle, 10–12.5 mm. long, 4–6 mm. broad; side lobes ovate or elliptic, porrect; mid-lobe ovate-lanceolate, acuminate, 5–7 mm. long, 1.4–3 mm. broad; callus central, fleshy. Column subterete, 1–1.5 mm. long; foot 4–5.5 mm. long; pollinia ovoid.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: An erect epiphytic herb to 25 cm. tall. Pseudobulbs ovoid to narrowly conical, more or less covered by sheathing cataphylls below, up to 3 cm. long, 1 cm. broad, 2–3-leaved at the apex. Leaves suberect to arcuate, linear to narrowly oblanceolate, obtuse or rounded, 7–11 cm. long, 0.7–1.2 cm. broad. Inflorescence erect, 6–15 cm. long, rather laxly few–many-flowered, densely pubescent; bracts broadly ovate or cordate, mucronate and recurved at the apex, 6–10 mm. long, 6 mm. broad. Flowers pubescent on outer surface, yellow, flushed with red; anther-cap crimson; callus golden yellow. Dorsal sepal ovate-lanceolate or lanceolate, acuminate or acute, 6.5–8 mm. long, 3 mm. broad; lateral sepals obliquely triangular-lanceolate, acuminate, 7.5–9 mm. long, 5 mm. broad, forming a short conical mentum ± 4.2 mm. high. Petals oblanceolate, rounded, 6 mm. long, 1.7–2 mm. broad, papillose in apical half. Lip 3-lobed, strongly recurved in basal half, sparsely clavate-pubescent on disc, callus, side lobes and mid-lobe, ± 6 mm. long, 5 mm. broad; side lobes extending below geniculation in lip, somewhat oblong- elliptic, truncate in front; mid-lobe ovate, subacute, fleshy but not bullate. Column short, stout, less than 1 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: An epiphytic herb, 14.5–37.5 cm. high. Pseudobulbs loosely clustered, from a short creeping rhizome, articulated in basal half, cylindric, 5.2–9.5 cm. long, 1–3 cm. in diameter, clothed in 3–4 sheaths. Leaf linear-lanceolate to ovate, acute or obtuse, cuneate below, 7.2–18 cm. long, 6–11 mm. broad, coriaceous, articulated 1–2 mm. above the pseudobulb apex. Inflorescence shorter than the leaf, a simple or rarely branched raceme, 5.5–14.5 cm. long, pubescent, up to 20-flowered; peduncles stout, 4.5–9 cm. long, with a basal membranous sheath; bracts lanceolate to ovate- triangular, amplexicaul, 4–7 mm. long. Flowers yellow, yellowish green or greenish white, mottled purple. Dorsal sepal oblong-triangular, apiculate, 6.5–7.5 mm. long, 3–4 mm. broad; lateral sepals obliquely triangular, apiculate, 7.5–9.6 mm. long, 6.5–8.5 mm. broad; all sepals ± abaxially pubescent; mentum conical, 6.5–8 mm. long. Petals narrowly elliptic or obovate lanceolate, subacute to obtuse, 3.5–6 mm. long, 1–2 mm. broad. Lip strongly recurved, ± sessile, fleshy, distinctly 3-lobed, 7.5–10 mm. long, 3.6–5 mm. broad; side lobes porrect, broadly elliptic; mid-lobe rounded-subquadrate, shortly apiculate, 2.5–4 mm. long, 2–4.5 mm. broad, glandular-pubescent below; callus obscure, central. Column subterete, 1–1.5 mm. long; foot 4.5–8.5 mm. long; pollinia subglobose.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: A suberect to pendulous epiphytic or rarely lithophytic plant to 60 cm. or more long. Stems (pseudobulbs) narrowly cylindrical to fusiform, superposed, given off from about the middle of previous growth, 5–23 cm. long, 0.3–0.4 cm. in diameter, acute, covered by deciduous leaf-bases when young, drying yellow and longitudinally ridged, 3–6-leaved in the apical half. Leaves suberect, lanceolate, oblanceolate or oblong- lanceolate, 5–15 cm. long, 0.4–3.2 cm. wide, acute or subacute, largest leaves towards the apex. Inflorescence terminal, paniculate, densely many-flowered, 3–8 cm. long, shorter than the 2 terminal leaves; peduncle terete, pubescent, to 3 cm. long; bracts lanceolate, acuminate, 1.5 mm. long. Flowers minute, persistent after ovary has developed, cream or yellow-green, variously tinged with purple or completely mauve or purple. Dorsal sepal elliptic, subacute, 2.2 mm. long, 1.4 mm. wide; lateral sepals obliquely ovate, subacute, 2.8 mm. long, 2.3 mm. wide, forming with the column-foot a 2 mm. long mentum. Petals oblong-obovate, obtuse, 2 mm. long, 1 mm. wide. Lip 3-lobed in the middle, shortly and broadly clawed, 2.3 mm. long, 2.5 mm. wide; side lobes suberect, somewhat oblong, curved forwards, shorter and much narrower than the mid-lobe; mid-lobe fleshy, rotund-subquadrate, obtuse. Column terete, 1.5 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: An erect or pendulous epiphytic plant 20–30 cm. long. Stems slender, obscurely pseudobulbous at base, terete above, 4–9 cm. long, 1.5–3 mm. wide, 3–4-leaved; pseudobulbs conical, 5–15 mm. long, 5–7 mm. wide. Leaves linear, suberect, grass-like, acute, 10–22 cm. long 4–7 mm. wide. Inflorescence erect to arcuate, racemose, 3–5-flowered, 3–7 cm. long; peduncle terete, densely pubescent, nearly covered by 2–3 scarious acute sheaths; rhachis densely pubescent, terete; bracts ± papery, lanceolate, acute or acuminate, 3–8 mm. long. Flowers large, sepals and petals white, yellow, yellow-green or greenish; lip white with a central yellow ridge at base. Dorsal sepal lanceolate, acute, 9–14 mm. long, 3.5–5.8 mm. wide; lateral sepals obliquely triangular-lanceolate, 13–14.6 mm. long, 6.7–8.5 mm. wide, acute; mentum broadly conical, 6.5–8 mm. high. Petals oblong-oblanceolate, obtuse to subacute, 9–12 mm. long, 3.5–4.1 mm. wide. Lip shortly clawed, 3-lobed just below the middle, 11.6–14.5 mm. long, 9–10 mm. wide, clavate-pubescent all over; side lobes erect, narrowly oblong, rounded in front; mid-lobe rotund-subquadrate, apiculate, apex recurved, 5.5–6.5 mm. long, 6–7 mm. wide; disc with a fleshy keel almost to the base of the mid-lobe. Column subterete, dilated above, 4.5 mm. long.
