Stem erect, slender, with 1–2 leaves at the base and a few lanceolate acuminate sheaths above, sparsely glandular hairy or glabrous. Leaves spreading or suberect, lanceolate, ovate or elliptical, shortly acuminate, 2.5–13 cm. long, 1–5 cm. broad, glabrous. Inflorescence rather laxly up to 40-flowered, up to 24 cm. long; rhachis ± glandular hairy. Bracts lanceolate, acuminate, shorter than the ovary. Flowers white to pink with red or purple spots on the lip, spreading or ascending; pedicel with ovary 1 cm. long. Dorsal sepal ovate, very convex, 3.5–5.5 mm. long; laterals spreading, obliquely semi-orbicular or semi-obovate, obtuse, 4–8 mm. long. Petals curved-lanceolate or oblong, obtuse, 3–5.8 mm. long. Lip distinctly 5-lobed, widest in the middle, 5–9.5 mm. long, 3–7 mm. broad; lower side lobes triangular, acute; upper side lobes longer, linear or oblong, subacute or obtuse; middle lobe broader, oblong or obovate, 2.5–4.5 mm. long. Spur cylindrical, incurved, 3–9 mm. long. Column ± 1.5 mm. long; anther-canals short, auricles ± clavate, rugulose; rostellum middle lobe very small, tooth-like, side lobes elongated. Ovary ± glandular hairy. Fig. 9.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: Terrestrial or rarely epiphytic herb 15–50 cm. high. Root-tubers ellipsoid, up to 2.5 cm. long and 1 cm. in diameter, ± woolly. Stem slender, erect, glandular hairy, especially in upper part, with 1 or 2 sheaths and a single leaf (rarely 2 leaves) at the base and several lanceolate acuminate sheaths above. Leaf erect or spreading, lanceolate, elliptical-lanceolate or oblanceolate, acute or acuminate, 4–20 cm. long, 1–4 cm. broad, glabrous. Inflorescence laxly or rather densely 4–22-flowered, 3–10 cm. long; rhachis glandular hairy. Bracts lanceolate, acuminate, shorter than the ovary, glandular ciliate. Flowers pinkish-purple or mauve, suberect; pedicel with ovary 1–2 cm. long. Dorsal sepal very convex, ovate, hooded at the apex, 5–7 mm. long; laterals spreading, obliquely ovate or lanceolate-ovate, obtuse, 6.5–8 mm. long; all ± sparsely glandular hairy outside. Petals obliquely lanceolate, acute, 4.5–7.5 mm. long, adnate at the inner base to the column. Lip ovate or broadly lanceolate in outline, ± distinctly 3-lobed at the middle, 5–8.5 mm. long, 2.5–5 mm. broad, the middle lobe ± triangular and much larger and longer than the side lobes. Spur descending, cylindrical, 6–9 mm. long. Column short and stout; anther-canals short; rostellum projecting forward, almost equally 3-lobed; stigmas shortly clavate. Ovary glandular hairy.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: Terrestrial herb 10–45 cm. high. Root-tubers ovoid or ellipsoid, 1–2.5 cm. long, 5–12 mm. in diameter, woolly. Stem erect, slender or rather stout, with 1–2 scarious sheaths and a single leaf at the base and usually 1 lanceolate acuminate sheath about half-way up, glabrous. Leaf erect or spreading, oblong-lanceolate or oblong-elliptical, shortly acuminate, 5–22 cm. long, 2–5.5 cm. broad, glabrous. Inflorescence short, up to 5 cm. long, rather closely 1–11-flowered; rhachis glandular hairy. Bracts long-acuminate from an ovate base, up to 1.5 cm. long, shorter than the ovary, glabrous. Flowers pink or mauve, the lip pale yellow in centre, suberect; pedicel with ovary 2.5–3.5 cm. long. Dorsal sepal erect, ovate, very convex, ± 5 mm. long; laterals spreading, obliquely elliptical, obtuse, ± 6 mm. long. Petals adhering to the dorsal sepal, obliquely oblong or elliptical, 5 mm. long. Lip projecting forwards, 10–15 mm. long and broad, almost equally 4-lobed or 3-lobed with the middle lobe deeply divided, the outer lobes broader than the inner, all oblong or widened slightly towards their apices. Spur slender, pendent, 2–2.5 cm. long. Column stout, ± 2.5 mm. long; anther-canals short; rostellum middle lobe triangular, projecting forwards; stigmas shortly clavate. Ovary glabrous.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: Terrestrial or rarely epiphytic herb 12–45 cm. high. Roots tuberous or slender, densely woolly; tubers ellipsoid, up to 2cm. long and 1cm. in diameter. Stem slender, erect, glandular hairy in the upper part, with 1 leaf or rarely 2 leaves at the base and several distant sheaths above. Leaf erect, lanceolate or oblanceolate, acute, 4.5–16.5 cm. long, 1–3 cm. broad, glabrous. Inflorescence rather laxly several- to many-flowered, up to 9 cm. long, ± 3 cm. in diameter. Bracts lanceolate, acuminate, much shorter than the ovary, sparsely glandular hairy. Flowers pink, mauve or violet, suberect. Dorsal sepal ovate, subacute, convex, 5–6 mm. long, 3–4 mm. broad; laterals spreading, obliquely ovate-elliptical, obtuse, 7.5–10 mm. long. Petals falcate-oblong, subacute, 5–7 mm. long, forming a hood with the dorsal sepal. Lip ligulate or linear, obtuse, ± 7 mm. long, 1–2.5 mm. broad. Spur incurved, narrowly cylindrical, nearly 2 cm. long. Column short; rostellum middle lobe erect, triangular, slightly overtopping the anther. Ovary densely glandular hairy.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: Terrestrial herb 13–25 cm. high. Root-tubers ellipsoid or ovoid, up to 1.5 cm. long and 1 cm. in diameter, woolly. Stem slender, with a few scarious acute sheaths and 2 leaves at the base and 1–3 lanceolate sheaths above. Leaves spreading, lanceolate, oblanceolate or elliptical, acuminate, 3–11.5 cm. long, 8–24 mm. broad, glabrous. Inflorescence rather laxly 6–25-flowered, up to 11 cm. long; rhachis sparsely glandular hairy. Bracts lanceolate, acute, shorter than the ovary. Flowers white, mauve or rose-red, suberect; pedicel with ovary ± 7 mm. long. Dorsal sepal ovate, very convex, ± 3.5 mm. long; laterals spreading, obliquely semi-obovate, obtuse, 4–5.5 mm. long. Petals curved-lanceolate, ± 3 mm. long, attached to the column at the base. Lip lanceolate in outline, 5-lobed, 5–7 mm. long; basal lobes short, rounded; side lobes half-way up, shortly triangular, acute. Spur ± incurved, 5–7 mm. long. Column short and broad; anther-canals linear, auricles stalked, swollen at end; rostellum truncate, cleft in centre, stigmas equalling the anther-canals. Ovary glandular hairy.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: Terrestrial herb 10–35 cm. high. Root-tubers ellipsoid or ± fusiform, 1–3.5 cm. long, 5–15 mm. in diameter, densely woolly. Stem sometimes prostrate at the base, erect above, slender, bearing 1–2 scarious sheaths at the base, a pair of leaves 1–9 cm. above the base and a few rather tight lanceolate sheaths above, glabrous. Leaves spreading or suberect, lanceolate, oblanceolate, oblong, elliptical or ovate, apiculate or shortly acuminate, 3.5–16 cm. long, 1–5 cm. broad, glabrous. Inflorescence rather laxly 3–17-flowered, up to 16 cm. long; rhachis glabrous. Bracts lanceolate, acuminate, shorter than the ovary. Flowers pink, mauve or purple, spreading; pedicel with ovary 1–1.5 cm. long. Dorsal sepal elliptical-ovate, obtuse, convex, ± 5 mm. long; laterals obliquely semi-ovate, subacute, 4–6 mm. long. Petals very obliquely ovate or orbicular-ovate, acute, 4–6 mm. long, ± 4 mm. broad. Lip transversely elliptical or obreniform from a narrow base, 3-lobed in front, 8–14 mm. long and a little broader; side lobes large and rounded; middle lobe much smaller and triangular-acute. Spur strongly incurved, with a broad mouth and much swollen apex, ± 8 mm. long. Column stout, 2 mm. long; rostellum middle lobe short, triangular; stigmas shortly clavate. Ovary glabrous.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: Terrestrial herb up to 23 cm. high. Tuber ellipsoid, ± 1 cm. long, tomentose. Stem slender, erect, glabrous at base, glandular hairy above, with 2 or 3 leaves at the base and several lanceolate acuminate sheaths above. Leaves spreading, oblong or oblong-lanceolate, to 2.5 cm. long and 1 cm. broad, glabrous. Inflorescence rather laxly 6–20-flowered, 6–8 cm. long; rhachis glandular hairy. Bracts lanceolate, acute, shorter than the ovary. Flowers suberect. Dorsal sepal ovate, subacute, ± 2.5 mm. long, convex; laterals obliquely semi-orbicular or semi-oblong, subacute, nearly 4 mm. long; all glabrous. Petals obliquely ovate or oblong, subacute, equalling the dorsal sepal. Lip cuneate, tridentate at the apex and slightly swollen on each side at the base, 5 mm. long. Spur pendent, slightly incurved, cylindrical, slightly swollen towards the apex, 5 mm. long. Column short, obtuse; rostellum middle lobe very small, stigmas shortly clavate. Ovary glandular hairy.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: Liana 3–25 m high with white latex; branches dark brown with pale brown lenticels; branchlets glabrous. Leaves petiolate; blade (narrowly) elliptic, 3–9 cm long, 1–4 cm wide, acuminate or caudate at the apex, cuneate or rounded at the base, glabrous, with 4–9 pairs of secondary veins forming an angle of 45–60° with the midrib; petiole 1–5 mm long, glabrous. Inflorescence terminal and often also axillary, few-flowered, glabrous; peduncle 3–16 mm long; pedicels 3–10 mm long. Flowers fragrant; sepals ovate, 1.2–2.2 mm long, 0.8–1.4 mm wide, obtuse, glabrous, with one colleter near the edge; corolla white, tube often partly pink outside; mature bud with an ovoid head about as long as the tube; tube 5–9 mm long, widest at the insertion of the stamens; lobes obliquely oblong or obliquely ovate, 4.5–12 mm long, 2.5–8 mm wide, rounded, spreading or recurved; stamens with apex 1.2 mm below to 1 mm above the mouth of the corolla tube, inserted at 2–5 mm from the base; anthers 2.8–4.5 mm long; style 2.2–4 mm long; pistil head 0.5–1 mm long, stigmoid apex minute; ovules ± 100 in each carpel. Fruit brown, 15–40 cm long, 0.5–1 cm wide, glabrous; seed 15–25 mm long; coma 2.5–3.5 cm long.
bibliographicCitation: Apocynaceae, E.A. Omino. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 2002

description: Large liana up to 15 m high, with white latex; trunk 3–10 cm in diameter; bark smooth; branches dark brown with cream lenticels; branchlets puberulous. Leaves petiolate; blade elliptic, rarely obovate, 15–32 cm long, 4–15 cm wide, apiculate at the apex, rounded or less often cuneate at the base, glabrous above, densely pubescent beneath, with 5–20 pairs of rather straight secondary veins forming an angle of 45–80° with the midrib; petiole 3–10 mm long, puberulous. Inflorescence terminal, 4–12 cm long, many-flowered, dense, puberulous; peduncle 5–30 mm long; pedicels 1–3 mm long. Flowers fragrant; sepals ovate, 1.5–3 mm long, 1.3–2 mm wide, obtuse, with one large colleter near the edge; corolla yellow, orange, orange-brown or cream, red in the throat and often also outside the tube; mature bud with anellipsoid or (narrowly) ovoid head about 0.5–1×as long as the tube, ciliate; tube 7–11.5 mm long, 1.5–2 mm wide; lobes obliquely obovate, 5–9 mm long, 4–6.5 mm wide, rounded; stamens inserted 3.5–5.5 mm from the base; style 2–3.1 mm long; ovules 50–100 in each carpel. Fruit dark brown, 26–62 cm long, 0.7–1 cm wide, pubescent; seed up to 25 mm long; coma 3–7 cm long.
bibliographicCitation: Apocynaceae, E.A. Omino. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 2002

description: An epiphytic or lithophytic herb, often forming large masses; stems 15–30 cm. or more long. Leaves linear, narrowly oblong or narrowly elliptic, rarely oblanceolate, 12–22.5 cm. long, 1.6–3.6 cm. wide. Infloresences 6–20 cm. long, 5–14-flowered; peduncle 1.5–2 cm. long; bracts cymbiform, ovate, acute or subacute, 15–33 mm. long, 5–17 mm. apart. Flowers white with a greenish spur, sweedy scented; pedicel and ovary 20–40 mm. long. Sepals lanceolate, acuminate, recurved, 18–49 mm. long, 5–7 mm. wide. Petals similar, 14–27 mm. long, 4.5–6 mm. wide. Lip lanceolate, acuminate, recurved, 15–36 mm. long, 4–6 mm. wide. Spur incurved to somewhat sigmoid, 30–70 mm. long. Column 2–2.5 mm. long; rostellum pendent, 4.5–5 mm. long; viscidium bipartite.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: An epiphyte with stems 8–20 cm. long. Leaves very coriaceous, linear, unequally bilobed at apex, 7–8.5 cm. long, 7–8 mm. wide. Inflorescences 3–9 cm. long, densely up to 12-flowered; peduncle 2–2.5 cm. long; bracts elliptic, obtuse, 6–8 mm. long, 3–4 mm. apart. Flowers white; pedicel and ovary 3 mm. long, much shorter then the bract Sepals lanceolate or elliptic-lanceolate, acuminate or acute, 10–13.5 mm. long, 2.4–3.3 mm. wide. Petals oblong-lanceolate, acuminate, 8.4–9.5 mm. long, 2.4–2.6 mm. wide. Lip lanceolate, acuminate, recurved, 8.5–10.5 mm. long, 2.5–3 mm. wide. Spur straight, 2–2.5 cm. long. Column 1.3–1.5 mm. long; rostellum 2.5–3.2 mm. long; viscidium hyaline.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: A pendulous epiphyte with a long stem. Leaves linear-oblanceolate, unequally roundly bilobed at apex, 11–25 cm. long, 1.9–3.2 cm. wide. Inflorescences 13–23 cm. long, 7–10-flowered; peduncle ± 3 cm. long, covered by sheathing bracts; bracts cymbiform, broadly ovate, obtuse, 18–23 mm. long, 10–22 mm. apart. Flowers white, scented; pedicel and ovary 42–45 mm. long. Sepals linear-lanceolate, long-acuminate, recurved, 45–49 mm. long, 6.5–9 mm. wide. Petals similar, 40 mm. long, 5.5 mm. wide. Lip linear-lanceolate, long-acuminate, recurved, 40–42 mm. long, 5 mm. wide. Spur incurved to sigmoid, 9.5–14.5 cm. long. Column 2.5 mm. long; rostellum 6.5 mm. long; viscidium bipartite. Fig. 141.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: A dwarf epiphyte or lithophyte with a very short stem, up to 4 cm. long. Leaves very fleshy, conduplicate, recurved, oblong, unequally bilobed at apex, 1.5–4(–6) cm. long, 6–12 mm. wide, grey-green. Inflorescences 1.5–3 cm. long, 3–6-flowered; peduncle less than 1 cm. long; bracts papery, elliptic, obtuse, 3–4 mm. long. Flowers white, fading to cream, sweedy scented of hyacinths at night; pedicel and ovary 7–12 mm. long. Sepals oblong-lanceolate, acute, 7–11.5 mm. long, 2.5–3 mm. wide. Petals lanceolate, acuminate, 5.9–8.6 mm. long, 2.5–2.7 mm. wide. Lip obscurely 3-lobed, lanceolate, acuminate, recurved, 6.5–8.5 mm. long, 3.5–5.3 mm. wide. Spur slightly incurved, 1.8–2.4 cm. long. Column 1–1.5 mm. long; rostellum 3.3 mm. long; viscidium hyaline.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: An epiphyte with 6–12 cm. long pendent stems. Leaves 8–10, linear-oblong, unequally roundly bilobed at apex, 22–40 cm. long, 2.3–3 cm. wide. Inflorescences 22–25 cm. long, densely 15–22-flowered; peduncle 7.5–8.5 mm. long, covered by a sheath; bracts broadly ovate, obtuse, 8–11 mm. long, longer than the ovary, 5–15 mm. long. Flowers white; pedicel and ovary 6–7 mm. long. Sepals lanceolate, acute to acuminate, 13–15 mm. long, 3.9–4.5 mm. wide. Petals similar, 11–12 mm. long, 3–3.5 mm. wide. Lip lanceolate, acute, 11–12 mm. long, 4 mm. wide. Spur straight or sigmoid, 2.5–3.2 cm. long. Column 1.5 mm. long; rostellum 3.5–4.3 mm. long; viscidium hyaline.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: A pendent epiphyte with an elongate stem 20–80 cm. long. Leaves oblanceolate or narrowly elliptic, tapering to both ends, roundly unequally bilobed at the apex, 10–21 cm. long, 3–5 cm. wide, often rather crinkled. Inflorescences pendent, 18–32 cm. long, 10–20-flowered; peduncle slender, 5.5–8 cm. long; bracts broadly ovate, obtuse, 5–8 mm. long, 7–23 mm. apart. Flowers well spaced, white, tinged with orange-brown on the spur; pedicel and ovary 13–15 mm. long. Sepals lanceolate, acuminate, 15–18 mm. long, 4.5–5.3 mm. wide. Petals similar, 14–15 mm. long, 4–4.5 mm. wide. Lip lanceolate, acuminate, 14–15 mm. long, 5 mm. wide. Spur slightly incurved, 3.5–4.5 cm. long. Column 2 mm. long; rostellum 4.5–5 mm. long; viscidium hyaline.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: An erect epiphyte with a 20–40 cm. long, rarely branching stem. Leaves suberect, coriaceous, linear, unequally roundly bilobed at apex, 8–24 cm. long, 1.4–2.8 cm. wide. Inflorescences 3.5–9 cm. long, 4–10-flowered; peduncle 10 mm. long, covered by sheathing sterile bracts; bracts elliptic, obtuse, 5–11 mm. long, 4–10 mm. apart, brownish black. Flowers white with a salmon-coloured spur; pedicel and ovary 18–22 mm. long. Sepals lanceolate, acuminate, 12–19.5 mm. long, 4–7.6 mm. wide. Petals similar, 10–16 mm. long, 3.3–5.7 mm. wide. Lip recurved, lanceolate, acuminate, 12–16.5 mm. long, 5–6 mm. wide. Spur ± straight, 3.5–5 cm. long. Column 2–2.5 mm.long; rostellum pendent, 4.5 mm. long; viscidium bipartite. Fig. 142.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: An erect or pendent epiphyte or lithophyte with stems up to 20 cm. long. Leaves coriaceous-fleshy, conduplicate, recurved, linear, unequally bilobed at apex, 4.5–10 cm. long, 8–12 mm. wide. Inflorescences 6–10.5 cm. long, 3–11-flowered; peduncle 8–12 mm. long; bracts ovate-triangular, obtuse, 4–5 mm. long, 3–5 mm. apart. Flowers white with a greenish spur; pedicel and ovary 9–11 mm. long, scabrid. Sepals lanceolate or oblong-lanceolate, acute or acuminate, 8–11 mm. long, 2.5–4.8 mm. wide. Petals oblong-lanceolate, acuminate, 8–8.5 mm. long, 2–3.4 mm. wide. Lip recurved, lanceolate, acuminate, 8.5–9.5 mm. long, 1.8–3 mm. wide. Spur incurved, 1.8–2.8 cm. long. Column 1 mm. long; rostellum 3–4 mm. long; viscidium hyaline.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: An epiphyte with arcuate or ascending stems up to 20 cm. long. Leaves linear, unequally roundly bilobed at apex, 7.5–12.5 cm. long, 1.2–2.5 cm. wide. Inflorescences 4–7 cm. long, densely 5–8-flowered; peduncle 1 cm. long or less, covered by sterile bracts; bracts ovate, obtuse, 3–8 mm. long, 4–7 mm. apart. Flowers white with an ochre-salmon spur, sweetly scented; pedicel and ovary 10–13 mm. long. Sepals lanceolate, acute or shortly acuminate, 9.5–11.6 mm. long, 3–5.5 mm. wide. Petals similar, 9–9.7 mm. long, 3.4–4 mm. wide. Lip lanceolate, acuminate, recurved, 9.5–10.5 mm. long, 3–4.5 mm. wide. Spur incurved to straight, 2–3.3 cm. long. Column 1–1.5 mm. long; rostellum 3–5 mm. long; viscidium hyaline.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: An epiphytic herb with pendent stems, 9–15 cm. long. Leaves up to 14, linear, unequally roundly or obtusely bilobed at apex, 9–17 cm. long, 9–16 mm. wide. Inflorescences 5.5–7 cm. long, 5–6-flowered; peduncle 1.5 cm. long, covered by sheaths; bracts ovate, subacute, 12–16 mm. long, 7–11 mm. apart. Flowers white with a greenish or salmon-coloured spur, sweetly fragrant; pedicel and ovary 26–28 mm. long. Sepals linear-lanceolate, acuminate, 19–31 mm. long, 4.3–6.75 mm. wide. Petals similar, 18.5–20 mm. long, 4–5 mm. wide. Lip lanceolate, acuminate, 17.5–26 mm. long. Spur sigmoid, 5.5–6.3 cm. long. Column 2–3 mm. long; rostellum 6–7 mm. long; viscidium bipartite, hyaline part distinctly longer than the indurated part; anther-cap broadly beaked.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: Large liana 4–45(–70) m long with white latex; trunk up to 18 cm in diameter; bark dark brown to pale grey, rough; branchlets glabrous. Leaves petiolate; blade obovate, 4–15 cm long, 2–7 cm wide, rounded to shortly and bluntly acuminate, cuneate at the base, with 4–8 pairs of rather straight secondary veins, forming an angle of 45–60° with the midrib; petiole 2–6 mm long, glabrous. Inflorescence terminal, occasionally axillary, 3–11 cm long, dense, many-flowered, puberulous or glabrous; peduncle 5–25 mm long; pedicels 4–7 mm long. Flowers fragrant; sepals (broadly) ovate, 1.2–2 mm long, 1–1.5 mm wide, with 1–3 colleters near the edge; corolla yellow or cream, throat dark red; mature bud head about half as long as tube, ciliate with long curled hairs; tube 4–7 mm long; lobes dolabriform, 6–10 mm long, 4–9 mm wide, truncate at the apex; stamens with apex above or below mouth of corolla tube; style ± 2 mm long; ovules ± 100 in each carpel. Fruit dark brown, 24–75 cm long, 0.3–1.5 cm in diameter; seed up to 23 mm long, coma ± 3 cm long.
bibliographicCitation: Apocynaceae, E.A. Omino. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 2002

description: Liana 3–15 m high with white latex; branches dark brown with large pale brown lenticels; branchlets glabrous or puberulous. Leaves petiolate; blade (narrowly) elliptic, 3–9 cm long, 1–5 cm wide, bluntly acuminate to obtuse at the apex, cuneateor rounded at the base, glabrous on both sides or puberulous beneath; with 11–14 pairs of rather straight secondary veins at an angle of 40–50° with the midrib; petiole 2–5 mm long, glabrous or puberulous. Inflorescence terminal, few- to many-flowered, 2–5 cm long, glabrous or puberulous; peduncle 1–18 mm long; bracts sepal-like; pedicels 5–15 mm long. Flowers with sepals ovate, up to 2.8 mm long, with 1–2 colleters near the edge inside; corolla white or greenish white; tube often partly reddish, throat red; mature bud with a narrowly ovoid head about twice as long as the tube; tube 4–6.5 mm long; lobes twisted in bud, spoon-like with a shallow concave apex, obliquely obovate or elliptic, 9–14.5 mm long, 3–5.5 mm wide, rounded at apex; stamens inserted 2.2–4 mm from the base; style 2–2.2 mm long. Fruit brown, 40–50 cm long, 0.5 cm in diameter; seed up to 15 mm long; coma 3 cm long.
bibliographicCitation: Apocynaceae, E.A. Omino. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 2002

description: Liana to 40 m long, with little or no white latex; trunk to 20 cm in diameter; branchlets glabrous. Leaves glabrous, blade elliptic, 5–15 cm long, 2–6 cm wide, apex apiculate with acute acumen, base rounded, with 5–8 pairs of upcurved secondary veins forming an angle of 45–60° with the midrib; petiole 5–20 mm long. Inflorescence terminal, many-flowered, 3–6 cm long, dense, glabrous or puberulous; peduncle 3–17 mm long; pedicels 2–7 mm long. Flowers fragrant; sepals ovate, 2.5–3.5 mm long, 1.5–2.5 mm wide, obtuse, with 1–5 colleters; corolla white; mature bud with a narrowly ovoid or ovoid head about half of the bud length, ciliate; tube 8–12 mm long; lobes obliquely suborbicular to ovate or obovate, 6.5–13 mm long, 5.5–11 mm wide, rounded, ciliate; stamens with apex 0–2.5 mm below mouth of the corolla tube, inserted 3.5–5.5 mm from the base; style 3.5–4.5 mm long; ovules ± 120 in each carpel. Fruit dark brown, 40–110 cm long, 0.5–1 cm in diameter; seed 18 mm long, 2–4 mm wide; coma 3–5 cm long. Fig. 32 (p. 97).
bibliographicCitation: Apocynaceae, E.A. Omino. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 2002

description: Liana or climbing shrub 2–15 m high, without latex; trunk 1.5 cm in diameter or more; branches dark brown with pale brown lenticels; branchlets glabrous. Leaves petiolate; blade (narrowly) elliptic or ovate, 1.5–6.5 cm long, 0.6–3 cm wide, obtuse to acuminate at the apex, cuneate or rounded at the base, glabrous, with 5–8 pairs of rather straight secondary veins forming an angle of 45–55° with the midrib; petiole 1–3 mm long, glabrous. Inflorescence terminal, 1.5–2.5 cm long, few-flowered, rather lax, glabrous or puberulous; peduncle 2–12 mm long; pedicels 2–10 mm long. Flowers fragrant; sepals (narrowly) ovate, 2–2.6 mm long, 0.8–1 mm wide, acute or acuminate at the apex, with one colleter near the edge; corolla white or cream; mature bud with a narrowly oblong or ovoid head about 2/3 of the bud length, ciliate; tube 6–8.7 mm long; lobes obliquely and narrowly elliptic or oblong, 9–9.3 mm long, 2–3.3 mm wide, rounded, ciliate; stamens with apex above and below mouth of the corolla tube, inserted 3.5–4.5 mm from the base; style 3–4 mm long; ovules ± 50 in each carpel. Fruit brown, 15–40 cm long, 0.3–0.5 cm in diameter; seed 9–15 mm long, 1.5–2.5 mm wide; coma 2.5–3.5 cm long.
bibliographicCitation: Apocynaceae, E.A. Omino. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 2002

description: Moderate-sized to large tree, 9–24 m. tall, bark smooth and grey. Branchlets purple-brown, never spiny, at first pubescent later glabrous. Leaves very variable, narrowly elliptic to broadly ovate, usually ovate, cuneate, truncate or subcordate at the base, asymmetric, often markedly so, acuminate at the apex, entire when adult but seedling leaves and leaves from coppice shoots are often palmately lobed and much larger than adult leaves. Lamina 4–19 cm. long and 2.5–10 cm. wide (up to 25 × 27 cm. in juvenile leaves), at first pubescent, later glabrescent; petiole 0.5–2.5 cm. long, velvety pubescent or glabrous; main lateral nerves 4–6, the basal ones confocal and sharply ascending so that the lamina is 5–7-nerved from the base, tertiary venation close, approximately parallel and at right angles to the costa. Flowers golden pubescent, white, cream or yellow, sweetly scented, 8–16 mm. long and 1.5–3.5 mm. wide, 5–8-merous, 3–23 in pedunculate 1–4-branched pubescent or glabrescent inflorescences, peduncles 0.4–1.8 cm. long, secondary branches 0.1–2.6 cm. long and pedicels 3–5.5 mm. long. Buds cylindrical, usually swollen at the base. Calyx-tube cylindrical or funnel-shaped, 1.5 mm. long, limb spreading, 1 mm. tall, denticulate. Petals ligulate, 8–13.5 mm. long and 1–1.7 mm. wide, pubescent outside, glabrescent inside save for a densely hirsute area near the base. Stamens the same number as the petals, anthers narrow, 5–9 mm. long. Style pilose, cylindrical, clavate apically, stigma lobed, together 7–10 mm. long. Fruit laterally compressed, globose or ellipsoidal, rather costate in the dry state, basally rounded, apically rather tapering, minutely pubescent, 1–2-celled, 8–10 mm. long, 6.5–9 mm. wide (maximum) and 4–5.5 mm. wide (minimum). Fig. 1.
bibliographicCitation: Alangiaceae, B. Verdcourt. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1958

description: A hirsute and pubescent prostrate creeping or climbing perennial with stems up to 3.5 m. long arising from a woody stock. Stipules lanceolate, 5–7 mm. long. Petioles 2–9 mm. long; blade quinquepartite, the median lobe lanceolate to elliptic-lanceolate, 3–10 cm. long, 1–2.5 cm. wide, acute, serrate to subentire, constricted at the base, the lateral lobes slightly and successively smaller; base of the blade deeply cordate; stipels ± 1 mm. long; blade sparingly pubescent above and beneath, more evenly so along the midrib, main veins and margins, dark green above, lighter beneath. Inflorescences axillary; peduncles up to 17 cm. long, leafless or with a small leaf near the base; bract-stipules as the foliar stipules; bracts ± ovate in outline, trifid, 3–5 cm. long, 1.5–4 cm. wide, the lobes lanceolate, acute or subacute, glandular-serrate to subentire, cordate at the base, 7–9-nerved from the base, pubescent, yellow or greenish yellow, with green veins. Male peduncles 5–7 mm. long, involucre 8 mm. across, 7–11-flowered; mass of fused bracts and aborted flowers adaxial, flattened. Male flowers: pedicels 3 mm. long; calyx-lobes 5, ovate or lanceolate, 2 mm. long, subglabrous; stamens ± 25. Female bracts 4, very unequal, the adaxial bifid, 1.5 mm. long, 2 mm. wide, the abaxial ovate, 5 mm. long, 3–5 mm. wide, the laterals elliptic, 1–2 mm. long, 0.5–1 mm. wide, all ciliate. Female flowers subsessile, but developing pedicels up to 1 cm. long in fruit; sepals 10–12, rhachis linear, 1 mm. long, extending to 1–1.5 cm. in fruit, lateral lobules 10–11 pairs, gland-tipped, pubescent and with urticating hairs; ovary 1 mm. diameter, pubescent; stylar column 8 mm. long, shortly trilobate at the apex. Fruits 5 mm. long, 9 mm. diameter, ± smooth, hispidulous, reddish brown or blackish. Seeds 4 mm. long and wide, ± smooth, brownish, streaked or mottled with pale grey.
bibliographicCitation: Euphorbiaceae, A. R.-Smith. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1987

description: Slender twiner to 7 m. Stems thinly pubescent. Petiole up to 10 cm. long; stipules linear or linear-lanceolate, up to 1 cm. long; blade simple, triangular-ovate, occasionally shallowly or deeply 3-lobed, 4–12 cm. long, 2–7 cm. wide, acute, acuminate, moderately to deeply cordate, margin slightly glandular-toothed, especially in the lower half, or subentire, puberulous along the nerves and otherwise glabrous or subglabrous above, moderately or densely pubescent along the nerves and otherwise sparingly pubescent or puberulous beneath, glands at the base stipelliform, subulate, 1.5 mm. long. Inflorescences axillary, or terminal on lateral shoots; main peduncles up to 14 cm. long, puberulous or glabrescent, stipules of the bracts resembling the foliar stipules; involucral bracts triangular-ovate, rarely 3-lobed, 2–3.5 cm. long, 1.5–3 cm. wide, acute, shallowly cordate, margin ± entire, glandular, with or without small tufts of hairs associated with the glands, glabrous or subglabrous without and within, 5-nerved from the base, pale green or yellowish. Male peduncles 4–5 mm. long, minutely puberulous; involucre 5–6 mm. in diameter, minutely puberulous, 14–20-flowered. Mass of fused bracts central, flattened. Male flowers: pedicels 2 mm. long; sepals elliptic-ovate, 2 mm. long, 1.3 mm. wide, later becoming reflexed, but remaining inflexed at the tip, minutely puberulous outside, pale yellow; receptacular column 1.5 mm. long, puberulous; stamens 10–20, filaments minute, anthers pale yellow. Bracts subtending the 3 ♀ flowers transversely ovate, 2 mm. long, 3.5 mm. wide, ciliate. Female flowers: pedicels 1 mm. long, extending to 1.2 cm. in fruit; sepals 6, pinnatifid (elliptic-ovate in outline), 2.5 mm. long, but extending to 1 cm. in fruit, with 6 pairs of linear lateral lobes which are acute and not glandular at the apex, glabrous above and beneath, but with the lobes densely strigose-hirsute on the margins, the hairs white and urticating; disc 0; ovary pubescent; style up to 7 mm. long, abruptly dilated and excavated at the apex. Fruits 3-lobed, 5 mm. long and 8 mm. wide, puberulous, grey or brownish. Seeds spherical, 3 mm. diameter, brown, grey-mottled.
bibliographicCitation: Euphorbiaceae, A. R.-Smith. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1987

description: A slender twiner to 3 m. Stems glabrous or finely pubescent, arising from a woody  stock. Petiole 5(–10) cm. long; stipules linear-lanceolate, 5–7(–12) mm. long; blade trifid or trilobate, rarely quinquelobate, the lobes obovate to elliptic-oblanceolate or lanceolate, acute or obtuse, glandular-toothed or quite entire, up to 14 cm. long and 4.5 cm. wide, shallowly to deeply cordate, puberulous along the nerves and otherwise glabrous, or evenly pubescent, rarely completely glabrous above and beneath, glands at the base stipelliform, linear-subulate, 1–3 mm. long. Inflorescences axillary, or terminal on lateral shoots; main peduncles up to 17 cm. long, glabrous or pubescent; stipules of the bracts resembling the foliar stipules; bracts ovate in outline, deeply or shallowly 3-lobed, the lobes triangular or lanceolate, acute, toothed or entire, up to 5 cm. long and wide, although commonly much less, rounded or shallowly cordate at the base, glabrous or pubescent without and within, 7-nerved from the base, yellow with green nerves at first, later becoming uniformly greenish. Male peduncles 3–5 mm. long, pubescent; involucre 8 mm. across, glabrous or almost so, 13-flowered. Mass of fused bracts adaxial, flattened. Male flowers: pedicels 3 mm. long; sepals elliptic-ovate, 2 mm. long, 1.5 mm. wide, later becoming reflexed, but remaining in-flexed at the tip, minutely puberulous outside, glabrous within, greenish yellow. Bracts subtending the ♀ flowers 2–3, the abaxial one ovate, 3 mm. long, ± entire, ciliate, often glandular near the apex, the other(s) oblong or ovate, 2 mm. long, undulate or repand-denticulate and often glandular at the apex, ciliate. Female flowers: pedicels 2 mm. long, extending to 1.5 cm. in fruit; sepals 6, pinnatifid, elliptic in outline, 2.5 mm. long, extending to 1 cm. in fruit, with 6 pairs of linear lateral lobes each terminating in a yellow clavate gland, puberulous above and beneath, but with the lobes densely strigose-hirsute on the margins, the hairs whitish and urticating; disc 0; ovary densely pubescent; style up to 1 cm. long, abruptly dilated and excavated at the apex. Fruits 3-lobed, 5 mm. long and 8 mm. wide, pubescent, brownish. Seeds spherical, 3 mm. diameter, greyish, streaked and mottled with dark brown.
bibliographicCitation: Euphorbiaceae, A. R.-Smith. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1987

description: Perennial semi-prostrate herb up to 40 cm., subscandent or not. Stems slender, pilose, up to 60 cm. long, arising from a woody stock. Petiole 1–3.5 cm. long. Stipules triangular-lanceolate, 2–3 mm. long, pubescent. Leaf-blade 3-partite or trifoliolate, rarely the lateral leaflets with a basal lobe or leaves 5-partite; petiolules 0 or 1 mm.; basal glands minute, somewhat flask-shaped, 0.5 mm. long; leaflets linear-lanceolate or lanceolate, the median ones up to 4.6 cm. long and 1 cm. wide, the lateral ones up to 3.8 cm. long and 1.1 cm. wide, acute or subacute, rarely obtuse, the median ones symmetrically attenuate or cuneate at the base, the lateral ones asymmetrically cuneate or rounded at the base, ± entire, rarely toothed, subglabrous or pubescent along the midrib and margins above, evenly or sparsely pubescent below, midrib and nerves prominent beneath. Inflorescences axillary, or terminal on lateral shoots; main peduncles up to 11 cm. long, pubescent; stipules of the bracts resembling the foliar stipules; involucral bracts lanceolate or ovate-lanceolate, entire or 3-fid, the adaxial one smaller than the abaxial, up to 2.3 cm. long and 1 cm. wide, with the lateral lobes (when present) up to 7 mm. long, acute, margin glandular-denticulate and crisped puberulous, cuneate at base, sparsely pubescent without, subglabrous within, 5-nerved from the base, the nerves becoming prominent in the fruiting state, yellow-green in flower, pale green in fruit. Male peduncles 3–4 mm. long (rarely up to 1.5 cm.), puberulous; involucre 3–5 mm. across, glabrous or almost so, 12-flowered. Mass of fused bracts central, convoluted, white. Male flowers: pedicels 3 mm. long; sepals elliptic-ovate, 1.5 mm. long, 1 mm. wide, minutely puberulous outside, greenish yellow; stamens 9, anthers ochre-yellow. Bracts subtending the ♀ flower 4, the median ones oblong, 2 mm. long, ciliate, the lateral ones triangular-ovate, 1 mm. long, ciliate. Female flower: pedicel 0.5 mm. long, extending to 2 mm. in fruit; sepals 6, linear-lanceolate, 2 mm. long, extending to 7–9 mm. in fruit, with 1–2(–5) linear lateral lobes on each side, puberulous above and beneath, with the lobes somewhat hirsute on the margin; disc 0; ovary puberulous, 1 mm. long; style 5.5 mm. long, abruptly dilated and excavated at the apex, pale green. Fruits 3-lobed, 4 mm. long, 7.5 mm. wide, puberulous. Seeds spherical, 2.5 mm. diameter, greyish, streaked with dark brown. Fig. 56/11, p. 288.
bibliographicCitation: Euphorbiaceae, A. R.-Smith. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1987

description: Medium-sized tree or climbing shrub with rough light brown bark. Branchlets grey- or purple-brown, often with strong spines up to 1.2 cm. long, pubescent or glabrous. Leaves variable, cuneate or rounded at the base, rounded or acute at the apex, at first pubescent later glabrous, 3–23 cm. long and 1.4–9 cm. wide, petiole up to 1.5 cm. long; lateral nerves 3–9, venation openly reticulate, prominent below. Flowers cream with a slight orange tinge, 5–10-merous, 13–31 mm. long, 1–17 in almost sessile inflorescences, pedicels 2–8 mm. long. The pedicels and cylindrical buds are velvety with golden-brown hairs. Calyx tube urceolate 0.75–2.5 mm. long, lobes triangular 0.25–1.5 mm. long. Petals ligulate, densely pubescent outside, internally pubescent or glabrous, 12–28.5 mm. long and 1–2.3 mm. wide. Stamens 10–32, anthers narrow, 5–14 mm. long. Style glabrous, slightly dilated above, stigma capitate or conical, somewhat lobed, 8.5–27.5 mm. long. Fruit ellipsoidal, shortly pubescent, 9–22.5 mm. long, one-celled.
bibliographicCitation: Alangiaceae, B. Verdcourt. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1958

description: Climbing herb with branched stems 6–30 m. long, pubescent or puberulous when young but soon glabrescent. Leaf-blades obovate, elliptic or obovate-oblong, 3–12 cm. long, 1–6 cm. wide, shortly acuminate at the apex, cuneate at the base, glabrous; petioles 0.7–1.5 cm. long; stipules broadly triangular or acuminate, 1.5–2 mm. long, ± glabrous. Flowers in terminal and axillary inflorescences, sometimes forming ample panicles 2.2–6 cm. long, glabrous to pubescent; peduncles 0.4–3.5 cm. long; pedicels up to 3 mm. long; bracts subulate, 2–3.5 mm. long. Calyx-tube subglobose, 1 mm. long, pubescent or glabrous; lobes deltoid or ovate, 0.5–1 mm. long, up to 0.5 mm. wide, the margins and midrib ciliolate. Corolla at first yellow or greenish-white but later orange-red or tube white and lobes bright vermilion; tube 2.5–6 mm. long, 1 mm. wide at the base, 1.7 mm. wide at the apex, glabrous outside, densely yellow pilose in the throat, particularly in long-styled flowers; lobes lanceolate, 2.5–4 mm. long, 1–1.2 mm. wide, thickened at the apices, glabrous. Stamens included in long-styled flowers but long-exserted in short-styled flowers. Style 7–8 mm. long in long-styled flowers and 3 mm. long in short-styled flowers, the stigma-arms filiform, 2–3(–4) mm. long. Capsule subglobose, 3 mm. in diameter, glabrous or puberulous, the valves sulcate. Seeds brown, 0.5–1 mm. in diameter, with a broad irregularly lacerate circumferential wing. Fig. 20, p. 182.
bibliographicCitation: Rubiaceae, B. Verdcourt. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1976

description: A much-branched often aromatic (vars. fruticosa, villosa, leaves smelling of hops when crushed) shrub or small tree up to 4 m. tall. Stems sparingly to densely puberu-lous or pubescent or tomentose at first, later ± glabrescent, greenish at first, later becoming reddish-, greyish- or purplish-brown. Petioles 0.2–4.5(–7) cm. long, hairy ± as the stems; leaf-blade ovate, elliptic-ovate, triangular-ovate or ovate-rhomboid, (1–)3–7(–9) cm. long, (0.7)–1–4.5(–5.5) cm. wide, obtuse or obtusely, sometimes sub-acutely, gradually acuminate, mucronulate, cuneate or rounded, rarely shallowly cordate (var. eglandulosa), coarsely crenate or crenate-serrate, membranous to thinly chartaceous, (3–)5(–7)-nerved from the base, lateral nerves 4–5 pairs, the undersurface sparingly or evenly beset with small pellucid yellow glands (except var. eglandulosa), subglabrous or sparingly pubescent or pilose above and beneath, and more so on the midrib and main veins, bright yellow-green or dark green. Stipules triangular-lanceolate to subulate-lanceolate, 2–5 mm. long, keeled, ciliate or not, evenly pubescent, or sometimes pubescent only on the keels. Inflorescences ± spicate, axillary, solitary, up to 5.5 cm. long, sometimes unisexual, but usually androgynous, with a sessile, subsessile or shortly pedunculate terminal male portion, densely congested at first but later ± interrupted, and 1–7 bracteate female flowers at or near the base; allomorphic flowers 0; axis evenly puberulous to densely tomentose; outer male bracts broadly ovate, somewhat cupular, 1 mm. long, densely pubescent; inner male bracts linear-subulate, 0.5 mm. long, gland-tipped (except var. eglandulosa), pubescent; female bracts somewhat leaf-like, strongly accrescent, broadly ovate or reniform, cupular, 0.2–1.2 cm. long, 0.3–1.7 cm. wide, rounded at the apex, rounded or shallowly cordate at the base, dentate or crenate-dentate, yellow gland-dotted beneath (except var. eglandulosa), often fairly prominently ribbed beneath, glabrous or subglabrous above, glabrous or sparingly or evenly pubescent beneath, especially on the ribs, 1-flowered. Male flowers subsessile or shortly pedicellate; buds tetragonous-subglobose, densely pubescent. Female flowers sessile; sepals 3, ovate-lanceolate, 1 mm. long, ciliate; ovary subglobose-trilobate, 0.7 mm. diameter, ± smooth, with numerous yellow glands in the grooves between the lobes (except var. eglandulosa), densely pubescent or pilose; styles ± free to the base, 4 mm. long, laciniate, pink or red. Fruits trilobate, 2 mm. long, 3 mm. diameter, yellow gland-dotted (except var. eglandulosa), evenly pubescent or pilose. Seeds ellipsoid-ovoid, 1.5–2 mm. long, 1–1.3 mm. wide, smooth, brown, with an elliptic vulviform caruncle.
bibliographicCitation: Euphorbiaceae, A. R.-Smith. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1987

description: A ± erect monoecious but functionally dioecious coppicing shrub or scandent, densely and irregularly branched deciduous small tree of open habit up to 8 m. tall, but more commonly not exceeding 4.5 m., and spreading to 9 m. across. Bark smooth, brown. Twigs lenticellate, greyish- or purplish-brown, robust. Buds perulate, ovoid, 4 mm. long, brown. Young shoots and petioles sparingly puberulous or subglabrous. Petioles 1–7(–9) cm. long, commonly with a distal and proximal pulvinus; leaf-blade ovate-lanceolate, oblong-ovate or occasionally somewhat oblong-oblanceolate, 7–18 cm. long, 3–8 cm. wide, obtusely, subacutely or acutely acuminate, often caudate, rounded or occasionally cuneate, shallowly crenate to subentire, membranous, 3-nerved from the base, lateral nerves 4–7(–9) pairs, sometimes with 2(–4) small glandular patches beneath at the base, and occasionally with others elsewhere on the leaf-surface, stipellate, very sparingly puberulous on the midrib and main veins above and beneath, soon glabrescent, but with persistent tufts of hairs in the axils of the main veins beneath, dark green when growing in the shade, yellow-green when growing in the open. Stipules filiform, setaceous, linear or linear-oblong, 2–7 mm. long, sparingly puberulous or subglabrous. Stipels subulate-filiform, 1–3 mm. long, glabrous. Male inflorescences axillary, developing on the older twigs after leaf-fall and the development of the fruits, and before or during the development of the new terminal flush of leaves, solitary or more rarely paired, spicate or subracemose, up to 9 cm. long; axis sparingly puberulous or subglabrous; bracts ± ovate, concave, (1.5–)2.5–5 mm. long, 1–2 mm. wide, subacute, ± entire or somewhat erose, minutely puberulous, scarious, chestnut-brown, dense at first, but later laxly disposed along the expanded spike; second-order bracts linear-setaceous, 1–2 mm. long, ciliate. Male flowers ± sessile or very shortly pedicellate; buds subglobose, 0.7 mm. long, apiculate, sparingly pubescent or subglabrous, greenish white; sepals 2–4(–5), if 2 then suborbicular and cupular, if more then ovate, reflexed; stamens 8–9, the united filaments forming a basal plate; pistillode 0, minute or columnar, up to 0.5 mm. long, 2–3-lobed. Female inflorescences terminal, solitary or more rarely paired, spicate, few-flowered, lax, up to 15 cm. long, but usually not exceeding 10 cm.; axis very sparingly puberulous or ± glabrous; bracts ovate-lanceolate, 2–3 mm. long, acute, sparingly puberulous, with 2 sessile glands on the axis below the base, 1-flowered; bracteoles linear-lanceolate, 1 mm. long. Female flowers sessile; sepals 5–6, suborbicular-ovate, 0.5–0.7 mm. long, somewhat unequal, subacute, slightly denticulate, subglabrous; ovary subglobose, scarcely 3-lobed, 1 mm. long, 1.5 mm. diameter, smooth, evenly minutely ad-pressed puberulous; styles (2–)3, united at the base, linear-filiform, (0.3–)0.5–1.5 cm.  long, sparingly puberulous beneath at the base, minutely papillose, bright red or pinkish. Fruits 3(–4)-lobed, 5–7 mm. long, 7–8 mm. diameter, ± smooth, sparingly puberulous. Seeds ovoid-subglobose, 4 mm. long, 3 mm. wide, ± smooth or slightly rugulose, somewhat shiny, pale yellowish brown. Fig. 51.
bibliographicCitation: Euphorbiaceae, A. R.-Smith. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1987

description: A monoecious or dioecious shrub up to 3 m. Twigs lenticellate, greyish. Buds perulate, ellipsoid, 2–3 mm. long, dark brown, outer perulae setaceous. Young shoots and petioles pubescent, often with an admixture of coarser, longer hairs. Petioles 1–4(–5.5) cm. long; leaf-blade (5–)8–12(–14) cm. long, 2–5(–7) cm. wide, elliptic-ovate to ovate-lanceolate, obtuse or obtusely to subacutely acuminate, rounded or slightly cordate, coarsely and shallowly crenate or crenate-serrate, membranous, penninerved, lateral nerves 8–12 pairs, often with 2–4(–6) small glands beneath at the base, stipellate, pubescent along the midrib and main veins above, otherwise sparingly hirsute, patent-hirsute along the midrib and main veins beneath, otherwise subglabrous, dark green above, paler beneath. Stipules linear-setaceous, 4–8(–12) mm. long, pubescent. Stipels subulate-filiform, 2–5 mm. long, glabrous or subglabrous. Male inflorescences terminal or axillary, developing with the leaves, solitary, racemose or subpaniculate, up to 20 cm. long; axis pubescent; bracts linear-lanceolate to linear-setaceous, arcuate, 2–3(–5) mm. long, pubescent; second-order bracts minute. Male flowers densely clustered in the axils of the bracts; pedicels articulate; buds subglobose, 1 mm. long, sparingly pubescent; sepals (2–)3(–4), ovate-surborbicular, subacute or obtuse; stamens 7–8, the united filaments forming a basal plate; pistillode 0. Female and bisexual inflorescences terminal, solitary, spicate, few-flowered, lax, up to 25 cm. long, but usually not exceeding 15 cm.; axis pubescent; bracts triangular-lanceolate, 3–4 mm. long, acute, puberulous, with a pair of sessile discoid glands on the axis below the base. Female flowers solitary to the bracts (unless surrounded by evanescent ♂ flowers), sessile; sepals 4–6, lanceolate, 2–3 mm. long, acute, puberulous; ovary sub-globose, 1.5 mm. long, 1.5 mm. diameter, verrucose, densely pubescent; styles 3(–4), united at the base, filiform, 0.8–1.5(–2) cm. long, glabrous, ± smooth, crimson. Fruits rounded-trilobate, 5–6 mm. long, 7–8 mm. diameter, the upper half covered with conical warts, otherwise ± smooth, pubescent. Seeds ovoid-subglobose, 4 mm. long, 3.5 mm. wide, shallowly rugulose, somewhat shiny, yellowish brown.
bibliographicCitation: Euphorbiaceae, A. R.-Smith. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1987

description: A shrub 1–1.5 m. tall. Branchlets puberulous, soon glabrescent, sparingly lenticellate. Buds perulate. Petioles 2–3 mm. long, densely puberulous; leaf-blade obovate-oblanceolate, 4–7 cm. long, 1.5–3 cm. wide, narrowly acuminate, attenuate and narrowly rounded at the base, serrate, membranous, beset with small refringent glands above and beneath, sparingly puberulous on the midrib and main veins above and beneath, otherwise glabrous or subglabrous. Stipules linear, 1 mm. long, subglabrous, readily deciduous. Inflorescences racemose, terminal or arising from the axils of fallen leaves, up to 6 cm. long, the lower half to two-thirds ♀, the upper part ♂; axis puberulous; bracts resembling the stipules. Male flowers very shortly pedicellate; buds globose, subglabrous, gland-dotted at the apex, green. Female flowers: pedicels 2–3 mm. long, extending to 5–8 mm. long and becoming reflexed at the apex after flowering, puberulous; calyx-lobes ovate, 1 mm. long, subglabrous; ovary 1.5 mm. diameter, tuberculate and beset with small refringent glands; styles ± free, 3 mm. long, laciniate, glabrous. Fruits 2 mm. long, 2.5 mm. diameter. Seeds globose, 1.5 mm. long, dark brown.
bibliographicCitation: Euphorbiaceae, A. R.-Smith. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1987

description: A tree up to 15 m. tall, with spreading pendulous and ascending branches. Young shoots scurfily fulvous to ferruginous stellate-pubescent. Petiole 4–16(–22) cm. long, evenly scurfily or shortly stellate pubescent or puberulous; leaf-blade ovate to ovate-lanceolate or ovate-trullate, entire or sometimes shallowly 3–5-lobed, (9–)12–25 cm. long, 6–15(–24) cm. wide, apex and lobes subacute to shortly acutely acuminate, cuneate or rounded or (if the leaves lobed) truncate or shallowly or moderately cordate, with 2 circular, sessile, shining contiguous glands adaxially at the base, 3–5(–7)-nerved from the base, densely fulvous to ferruginous stellate-pubescent above and beneath at first, later becoming almost or quite glabrous on both surfaces. Stipules cylindric, 1 mm. long, rounded at the apex, stellate-pubescent, readily caducous leaving 2 small circular scars. Inflorescences conical, up to 15 cm. long and wide, branching from the base; axes densely fulvous stellate-tomentellous; bracts 2–3 mm. long, acute, densely fulvous stellate-tomentellous. Male flowers: pedicels slender, 5–7 mm. long, stellate-pubescent; buds ovoid, 2 mm. long, obtuse, the calyx rupturing to the base into 2 ± equal lobes, stellate-tomentose without, glabrous within; petals spathulate-oblanceolate, 5 mm. long, 2 mm. wide, obtuse, glabrous except for a few hairs within at the base, yellowish white; disc-lobes somewhat convolute, thick; stamens 17–20, the filaments 1 mm. long, simply puberulous, the anthers 0.5 mm. long; receptacle simply puberulous. Female flowers: pedicels 2–3 mm. long, 1.5–2 mm. thick, stellate-pubescent; buds ellipsoid, 5 mm. long, otherwise as in the ♂ flowers; petals linear-oblanceolate, 1 cm. long, 2 mm. wide, otherwise as in the ♂ flowers; disc-glands small, rounded; ovary subglobose, 1.5 mm. long, 2 mm. diameter, densely stellate-tomentose; styles  1 mm. long, glabrous. Fruits fleshy, ovoid-subglobose or transversely ovoid with 4 low longitudinal ridges, 4–4.5 cm. long, 4–6 cm. diameter, evenly to sparingly stellate-pubescent. Seeds broadly ovoid, 2.5–3 cm. long and wide, gibberulous, greyish, mottled brownish. Fig. 34.
bibliographicCitation: Euphorbiaceae, A. R.-Smith. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1987

description: An epiphyte with 5–25 cm. long pendent stems, 2–2.5 mm. diameter, often forming dense clumps. Roots prominent, much longer than leaves. Leaves 5–12 in upper part of stem, falcate, linear, unequally bilobed at apex, 3.5–12 cm. long, 1.5–5 mm. wide, twisted at base and articulated to a 7–10 mm. long leaf-sheath. Inflorescences 1–several, 2–3.5 cm. long, 3–8-flowered; peduncle 2–7 mm. long; bracts amplexicaul, 2 mm. long. Flowers green or pale yellowish green; pedicel and ovary up to 2 mm. long. Dorsal sepal lanceolate, acute, 2–2.5 mm. long, 1 mm. wide; lateral sepals lanceolate, acute, 3–3.2 mm. long, 1 mm. wide. Petals ovate, obtuse or rounded, 2.1 mm. long, 1.2 mm. wide. Lip entire, ovate, obtuse, 2 mm. long and wide, ecallose. Spur clavate, 1.5–2 mm. long. Column 0.7 mm. long; stipites 2; viscidia 2; rostellum pendent, clavate.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: An epiphyte with an elongate, slender, pendent stem up to 50 cm. long, 2–6.5 mm. diameter. Leaves up to 22, distichous, twisted at base to lie in one plane, ovate-elliptic, acute, to an unequally bilobed apex, 6.5–17 cm. long, 1.1–3.1 cm. wide, articulated at base to a longitudinally ridged sheathing base 10–25 mm. long. Inflorescences all along upper part of stem, 4–22 cm. long, up,to twice length of leaf, up to 25-flowered; peduncle short, ± 5 mm. long, covered in sheathing bracts; bracts amplexicaul, conical, 1–1.5 mm. long. Flowers whitish; pedicel and ovary 2–5 mm. long. Dorsal sepal oblong-lanceolate or triangular, acute, 2.5–7 mm. long, 1.2–2.4 mm. wide; lateral sepals broadly triangular, 2.5–6.5 mm. long, 1–2.8 mm. wide. Petals lanceolate to ovate, 2.5–6 mm. long, 0.6–2 mm. wide. Lip pandurate, retuse to apiculate, 3–7 mm. long, 2.6–6 mm. wide, with a tooth in the mouth of the spur. Spur inflated, 3–7.3 mm. long. Column 1.5–2 mm. long; stipites 2; viscidium 1. Fruit ellipsoidal, 6–16 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: An epiphyte or rarely a lithophyte with elongated, pendent stems up to 50 cm. long, 2.5–5 mm. diameter. Leaves up to 16 in upper half of stem, distichous, twisted at base to lie in one plane, oblong-elliptic or obovate, unequally bilobed at apex, 3.5–8 cm. long, 1.5–3 cm. wide, articulated to longitudinally veined sheaths 1–1.8 cm. long. Inflorescences 1–several, often 2–3 per node in upper part of stem, 2–8.5 cm. long, up to twice length of leaf; peduncle very short, covered by bracts; bracts very close, 2–3 mm. apart, amplexicaul, conical, acute, 1–2 mm. long. Flowers white, pale cream or green; pedicel and ovary 1–1.5 mm. long. Dorsal sepal oblong, obtuse, 3.8–4.7 mm. long, 2.1–3.4 mm. wide; lateral sepals oblique, oblong-elliptic, obtuse, 5–5.3 mm. long, 2.1–2.9 mm. wide. Petals obovate to elliptic, obtuse, 3.6–3.9 mm. long, 2.1–2.9 mm. wide. Lip obscurely 3-lobed, 4.7–5.5 mm. long, 3.6–3.7 mm. wide, with an obscurely bilobed tooth in the mouth of the spur; side lobes narrowly elliptic; mid-lobe deflexed, transversely elliptic, deeply incised at apex so that mid-lobe appears bilobed. Spur dependent, slightly incurved, cylindrical, 7.8–8.3 mm. long. Column 2 mm. long; stipites 2; viscidia 2; rostellum somewhat spathulate.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: An epiphyte with a short stem ± 1.5 cm. long, 5 mm. diameter. Leaves ± 5, slighdy falcate, linear, unequally bilobed at apex, 4–7 cm. long, 0.5–1.5 mm. wide, twisted at base to lie in one plane, articulate to a short 2–3 mm. long sheath. Inflorescences 5–7 cm. long, laxly many-flowered; peduncle 6–12 mm. long; bracts amplexicaul, 1 mm. long. Flowers pale yellow; pedicel and ovary 5–8 mm. long. Dorsal sepal elliptic-lanceolate, subacute, 6–8.6 mm. long, 2.7–4 mm. wide; lateral sepals elliptic, obtuse, 5.6–8.7 mm. long, 2.6–3.7 mm. wide. Petals linear to obovate, obtuse, 5–8 mm. long, 1.3–2.2 mm. wide, erose. Lip ovate, subacute, 8–9 mm. long, 4–4.5 mm. wide, with an obscure tooth in the mouth of the spur. Spur swollen and slightly lobed at apex, 15–15.5 mm. long. Column 3.5 mm. long; stipites 2, usually coherent, ciliate; viscidium 1, orange-red; rostellum pointed, entire. Fruit ellipsoidal, 9–11 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: An epiphyte with a short stem ± 5 cm. long, 3–4 mm. diameter. Leaves ± 5, linear to oblanceolate, unequally bilobed at rounded apex, 3–4 cm. long, 5–7 mm. wide, twisted at base and articulated to a longitudinally ridged leaf-bases 5 mm. long. Inflorescence laxly 6–8-flowered, 9 cm. long; peduncle 4 cm. long; bracts conical, somewhat amplexicaul, 1.5–2 mm. long. Flowers pale yellowish green; pedicel and ovary 3 mm. long, emerging from rhachis 2–3 mm. above axil of bract. Dorsal sepal broadly elliptic or subcircular, obtuse, 2.3–2.5 mm. long, 2 mm. wide; lateral sepals falcate, elliptic, obtuse, 3–3.5 mm. long, 1.5–2 mm. wide, fused behind spur at base. Petals circular, obtuse, 2 mm. long and wide. Lip flabellate, bilobed, 3.5–4 mm. long, 2–2.5 mm. wide, erose. Spur pendent, incurved towards apex, cylindrical, 6–6.5 mm. long. Column 1.5 mm. long; stipites 2, with papillose margins; viscidia 2; rostellum clavate, pendent.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: An epiphyte with a long pendent stem, 10–43 cm. long, 3–4 mm. diameter. Leaves distichous, many in upper half of stem, elliptic to oblong or oblanceolate, acute and obliquely unequally bilobed at apex, 4–10 cm. long, 1–2 cm. wide, twisted at base and articulated to a slightly compressed leaf-sheath 7–15 mm. long. Inflorescences solitary or paired at nodes, 1–many, 1–3 cm. long, densely many-flowered; peduncle 5 mm. long or less; bracts amplexicaul, 1–1.5 mm. long. Flowers waxy, white, campanulate; pedicel and ovary 2.5–3 mm. long. Dorsal sepal oblong-elliptic, obtuse, 2.2–3 mm. long, 1.7–2 mm. wide; lateral sepals obliquely elliptic, obtuse, 3–3.5 mm. long, 1.3–1.7 mm. wide. Petals circular, truncate or obtuse, 2–2.75 mm. long and wide. Lip entire, broadly orbicular or transversely elliptic, retuse, 2.7–3.75 mm. long, 3.5–4.7 mm. wide, with a low transverse callus at the mouth of the spur. Spur ellipsoidal-clavate, 2–3 mm. long, shortly pubescent in the mouth. Column 1–1.2 mm. long; stipites 2; viscidia 2; rostellum pendent, shortly spathulate.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: An epiphyte with an elongated pendent stem, ±10 mm. diameter. Leaves very fleshy, oblong or oblong-lanceolate, unequally bilobed at apex, 18–19.5 cm. long, 2.5–2.8 cm. wide, twisted at base to lie in one plane, articulated to a sheathing leaf-base ± 2.5 cm. long. Inflorescences several in upper part of stem, 1–2 per node, 8–16 cm. long, 7–16-flowered; peduncle 10–15 mm. long; bracts amplexicaul, conical, 3 mm. long. Flowers parchment white; pedicel and ovary 3–4 mm. long. Dorsal sepal lanceolate, acute, 8–9.5 mm. long, 3–3.6 mm. wide; lateral sepals falcate-ovate, subacute, 7.5–9 mm. long, 3–3.8 mm. wide. Petals falcate-elliptic, acute, 7.5–7.6 mm. long, 3–3.3 mm. wide. Lip obscurely 3-lobed, subcordate, apiculate, 7–7.5 mm. long, 8–8.6 mm. wide, erose, with a tooth in the mouth of spur. Spur pendent, fusiform-inflated, 8–9 mm. long. Column 3 mm. long; stipites 2; viscidium 1; rostellum tapering, reflexed. Fig. 124.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: An epiphyte or rarely a lithophyte with long pendulous stems 7–50 cm. long, 5–10 mm. diameter, covered in leaf-sheaths. Leaves up to 9, distichous, falcate, linear-oblanceolate, unequally bilobed at apex, 10–44 cm. long, 1–3.5 cm. wide, twisted at base, articulated to a sheathing base 1.2–3 cm. long. Inflorescences pendulous, 1–several, up to 60 cm. long, up to 60-flowered; peduncle 2–20 cm. long; bracts amplexicaul, 3–5 mm. long. Flowers usually borne in whorls of up to 4, greenish yellow, diurnally scented; pedicel and ovary 1–2.25 mm. long. Dorsal sepal linear-triangular, acute, 7–10.5 mm. long, 2–2.2 mm. wide; lateral sepals slightly falcate, linear, acute, 9.7–11.2 mm. long, 2–3 mm. wide. Petals linear to obovate, acuminate, 8.3–8.5 mm. long, 2–2.2 mm. wide, lip rectangular, 3-lobed at apex, 10–13 mm. long, 6.5–7 mm. wide, with erose lateral margins, with a marked tooth at the mouth of the spur; mid-lobe elongated and acuminate. Spur geniculate at base, fusiform, 6–9 mm. long. Column 2 mm. long, rostellum deeply bifid; stipites 2; viscidium 1.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: A large pendent epiphyte with a short stout stem 6–8 cm. long, 1.1–1.8 cm. diameter. Leaves 3–7, falcate, oblanceolate, unequally roundly bilobed at apex, 20–35 cm. long, 3–5.5 cm. wide, twisted at base to lie in one plane, articulated to a sheathing base 1–2 cm. long. Inflorescences pendent, 1–several, 10–12 cm. long, laxly 8–10-flowered; peduncle 3.5–4.5 cm. long, almost covered by loose bracts; bracts large, papery, broadly ovate, 10–15 mm. long and wide. Flowers pale translucent green; pedicel and ovary 2–2.4 mm. long. Dorsal sepal ovate, shortly apiculate or obtuse, 15–16 mm. long, 8.5–10.7 mm. wide; lateral sepals obliquely lanceolate, obtuse, 20–23 mm. long, 8–9.5 mm. wide. Petals subcircular, obtuse, 15–17 mm. long, 12–14 mm. wide, with strongly erose-lacerate margins. Lip flabellate, distantly 3-lobed, 18–20 mm. long, 22–24 mm. wide, erose on apical margin, with a tooth in the mouth of the spur; side lobes obliquely oblong; mid-lobe shortly triangular. Spur incurved-pendent, 12–14 mm. long. Column 4 mm. long; stipites 2; viscidia 2; rostellum pendent, 3-lobed. Fig. 125.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: An epiphyte with long hanging stems 8–27 cm. long, ± 5 mm. diameter, leafy in upper part. Leaves distichous, falcate, linear, unequally obtusely bilobed at apex, 14–26 cm. long, 1–1.8 cm. wide, twisted at base to lie in one plane, articulated at base to a rough sheath 1.5–2 cm. long. Inflorescences pendent, 1–several, 7–15 cm. long, laxly many-flowered; peduncle 1–2.5 cm. long; bracts usually amplexicaul, broadly ovate, 1–1.5 mm. long. Flowers pale yellowish, white or pinkish; pedicel and ovary 3–4 mm. long. Dorsal sepal lanceolate or narrowly elliptic, acute, 5.2–8 mm. long, 2–3 mm. wide; lateral sepals oblong-ovate, acute, 6.5–9 mm. long, 2.3–3.2 mm. wide. Petals lanceolate to oblong, acute, 5.4–6.6 mm. long, 1.8–2.6 mm. wide, slightly erose. Lip entire to obscurely 3-lobed, circular to broadly ovate, shortly apiculate, 5.3–6.3 mm. long, 6–8.3 mm. wide, erose, with a small tooth in the mouth of the spur. Spur slightly incurved, narrowly fusiform, 5–9.5 mm. long. Column 2.5–3 mm. long; stipites 2; viscidium 1; rostellum shortly ligulate, recurved.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: A small epiphyte with a pendent or spreading stem, 3–5 cm. long. Leaves 2–6 clustered towards apex of stem, falcate, linear-ligulate, unequally bilobed at rounded apex, 2–8 cm. long, 3–7 mm. wide, twisted at base to lie in one plane and articulated to a 4–6 mm. long sheathing base. Inflorescences 1–few, pendent, 5–10-flowered, 3.5–19 cm. long; peduncle 3–6 cm. long; bracts triangular, acute, 1–2 mm. long. Flowers pale green turning butterscotch yellow, unpleasantly scented; pedicel and ovary 6–8 mm. long. Dorsal sepal oblong-ovate, obtuse, 4.5–5 mm. long, 3 mm. wide; lateral sepals obliquely narrowly ovate, decurved, obtuse, 5–5.5 mm. long, 2.5 mm. wide. Petals orbicular, obtuse, 3 mm. long and wide. Lip decurved, entire, oblong, obtuse to emarginate, 2.5–3.5 mm. long, 2–3 mm. wide, ecallose. Spur incurved, cylindrical, 13–15 mm. long. Column 1 mm. long; stipites 2; viscidia 2; rostellum anchor-shaped at apex, fleshy, pendent-reflexed.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: An epiphyte with slender stems, 3–20 cm. long, 2 mm. diameter, often growing in tangled masses. Roots more prominent than the leaves, 2–10 cm. long, 0.5–2 mm. diameter. Leaves in apical part of stem, up to 6, linear to oblanceolate, rounded and unequally bilobed at apex, 6–15 mm. long, 2–4 mm. wide, articulated at base to a 4–5 mm. long leaf-sheath. Inflorescences 1–many, secund, 2–3 cm. long, up to 5-flowered; peduncle 1–1.2 cm. long; bracts amplexicaul, conical, 1 mm. long. Flowers greenish yellow, strongly fragrant; pedicel and ovary 4–5 mm. long, covered by scurfy hairs. Dorsal sepal oblong-elliptic, obtuse, 3 mm. long, 1.4–1.5 mm. wide; lateral sepals falcate, narrowly oblong, subacute, 3.5–4 mm. long, 1–1.5 mm. wide. Petals obliquely oblong-elliptic, obtuse, 2.5–3 mm. long, 1.5–1.6 mm. wide. Lip entire, elliptic, obtuse, 2.5–3 mm. long, 0.8–1 mm. wide. Spur strongly incurved, slenderly cylindrical, ± 7 mm. long. Column 1 mm. long; stipites 2; viscidia 2; rostellum pendent, rather bulbous.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: A dwarf epiphyte with a 5–10 cm. long stem, rather obscured by a dense mass of roots. Leaves linear or narrowly elliptic, unequally bilobed at apex, 1.5–6.5 cm. long, 2–6 mm. wide, twisted at base and articulated to a 4–8 mm. long leaf-sheath. Inflorescences 1–several, 1.5–3.5 cm. long, up to 9-flowered; peduncle very short, completely covered by sterile bracts; bracts amplexicaul, conical, 3–3.5 mm. long. Flowers greenish yellow; pedicel and ovary 3–5.5 mm. long. Dorsal sepal ovate, obtuse, 3.6–4.2 mm. long, 1.9–2 mm. wide; lateral sepals elliptic or ovate, obtuse, 4.6–5.2 mm. long, 1.6–2 mm. wide. Petals ovate, acute, 3.6–3.7 mm. long, 1.5–1.6 mm. wide. Lip concave, ovate, entire or very obscurely 3-lobed, acute, 3.2–3.3 mm. long, 2.6–3.7 mm. wide, with an obscure callus at the base. Spur cylindric, slightly recurved or straight, 5–5.5 mm. long. Column 1–1.2 mm. long; stipites 2; viscidia 2; rostellum pendent, tooth-like. Fig. 127, p.537.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: A dwarf epiphyte with a rarely branching stem, ±10 cm. long, 1.5–2 mm. diameter. Leaves 5–9, linear-oblong or oblong-ligulate, slightly falcate, unequally obtusely bilobed at apex, 2–3.5 cm. long, 3–6 mm. wide, twisted at base and articulated to a leaf-sheath 5 mm. long, drying almost black. Infloresences 1–few, 2–3-flowered, ±1.5 cm. long; peduncle ± 5 mm. long; bracts ovate, acute, 1–1.5 mm. long. Flowers minute, yellowish green; pedicel and ovary 1–2 mm. long. Dorsal sepal lanceolate-elliptic, acute, 3.5–3.7 mm. long, 1.2 mm. wide; lateral sepals oblong-lanceolate, acute, 3.5–3.9 mm. long, 1.3 mm. wide. Petals lanceolate, acute or acuminate, 4 mm. long, 1.4 mm. wide. Lip concave, entire, ovate-elliptic, obtuse, 4–4.5 mm. long, 3–3.3 mm. wide, ecallose. Spur pendent, cylindrical-clavate, 1.3–1.8 mm. long. Column 1 mm. long; stipites 2; viscidia 2; rostellum spathulate, dilated at apex.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: An epiphyte with a pendent stem, 6–30 cm. long, 1.5–2 mm. diameter. Leaves 2–10 in upper part of stem, falcate, linear, unequally bilobed at obtuse apex, 2.5–8.5 cm. long, 3–5 mm. wide, twisted at base and articulated to a sheathing base 7–10 mm. long. Inflorescences 1–several, 5–9 cm. long, laxly up to 20-flowered; peduncle 6–10 mm. long; bracts amplexicaul, conical, 1 mm. long. Flowers cream-coloured or buff; pedicel and ovary 2 mm. long, rugulose. Dorsal sepal elliptic, obtuse, 2.5–3 mm. long, 1.8–2 mm. wide; lateral sepals oblong-elliptic, obtuse, 3 mm. long, 1.4–1.6 mm. wide. Petals oblong to elliptic, obtuse, 1.8–2 mm. long, 1.6–1.7 mm. wide. Lip concave, entire or obscurely 3-lobed, ovate, obtuse, 2.3–3 mm. long, 2.4–2.7 mm. wide, ecallose. Spur incurved, cylindrical, 4–4.5 mm. long. Column 1 mm. long; stipites 2; viscidia 2; rostellum pendent, clavate. Fig. 126.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: An epiphyte with a short stem up to 12 cm. long and 1 cm. diameter. Leaves distichous in upper half of stem, oblanceolate, subacute and unequally bilobed at apex, 18–40 cm. long, 2–9 cm. wide, with prominent net-venation, articulated to rough overlapping leaf-bases 2–3 cm. long. Inflorescences 1–7, pendent, 20–50 cm. long, up to 50- or more-flowered; peduncle 2.5–8 cm. long; bracts broadly ovate, obtuse, amplexicaul, 6–10 mm. long and wide. Flowers pale yellow, lacking a scent; pedicel and ovary 2–3 mm. long. Dorsal sepal ovate, subacute, 7.8–13.5 mm. long, 2.8–6.2 mm. wide; lateral sepals lanceolate, subacute, 8–16.5 mm. long, 2.7–7.5 mm. wide. Petals linear to ovate, acute, 7.5–17.5 mm. long, 2.6–6.5 mm. wide, erose. Lip geniculate at base, obscurely 3-lobed, 7.5–15 mm. long, 7–18 mm. wide, with a lacerate margin, with a tooth in the mouth of the spur which is bordered on each side by a fleshy raised rim. Spur pendent, narrowly fusiform, inflated, 5–14.5 mm. long. Column 2.5–4.5 mm. long; stipites 2; viscidium 1; rostellum tapering, bifid. Fruit ellipsoidal, 10–20 mm. long. Fig. 123.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: An epiphyte or rarely a lithophyte with a 3–13 cm. long stem, 3–4 mm. diameter. Leaves distichous, leathery, oblanceolate-falcate, unequally bilobed at apex, 3–10 cm. long, 0.4–1 cm. wide, articulated to a 4–7 mm. long sheath. Inflorescences pendulous, 1–several, up to 25-flowered, as long as or longer than the leaves; peduncle 1.5–4 cm. long; bracts triangular, acute, 2 mm. long. Flowers pale yellow or cream-coloured, fragrant; pedicel and ovary 2–3 mm. long. Dorsal sepal ovate or obovate, obtuse or acuminate, 4.6–7.7 mm. long, 2.5–3.7 mm. wide; lateral sepals obliquely elliptic, obtuse, 5.7–11 mm. long, 2–3.6 mm. wide. Petals ovate to elliptic, acute, subacute or obtuse, 4.3–7.6 mm. long, 3.1–5.3 mm. wide, slightly erose, ± geniculate at the base. Lip flabellate to rectangular, obscurely 2–4-lobed, 6–9.5 mm. long, 7–9.6 mm. wide, deeply notched at apex, with a tooth in the mouth of the spur. Spur slightly fusiform, porrect, 8.6–14 mm. long. Column 2–3 mm. long; stipites 2; viscidia 2; rostellum decurved.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: An epiphyte with an irregular short stem 2–5 cm. long, 5–7 mm. diameter. Leaves 2–7, somewhat falcate, linear to obovate, slightly unequally bilobed at the apex, 5–15 cm. long, 0.7–2.2 cm. wide, articulated to a 5–10 mm. long base. Inflorescences 5–17 cm. long, laxly many-flowered; penduncle 3–4 cm. long; rhachis zig-zag; bracts amplexicaul, 2–8 mm. long. Flowers waxy, yellow; pedicel and ovary 4 mm. long, scabrid. Dorsal sepal oblanceolate, subacute, 3.6–4 mm. long, 1.5–2 mm. wide; lateral sepals linear to obovate, obtuse, 3.7–4 mm. long, 1–1.4 mm. wide. Petals linear, obtuse, 3.4–4.3 mm. long, 1 mm. wide. Lip ovate, acute, 3.4–3.8 mm. long, 1.7–2.3 mm. wide, with an obscure tooth in the mouth of the spur. Spur incurved, clavate, 11–12 mm. long. Column 2.4 mm. long; stipites 2, obovate, coherent, ciliate; viscidium 1; rostellum pointed, pendent. Fruit ellipsoidal, 7–10 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: A pendent or spreading epiphyte with stems 3–40 cm. long, 2–6 mm. diameter, occasionally branched. Leaves in upper part of stem, 3–10, linear to obovate or narrowly elliptic, unequally roundly bilobed at apex, 3–12 cm. long, 0.5–2.2 cm. wide, twisted at base and articulated to a sheathing base 7–10 mm. long. Inflorescences 1–many, pendent, 5–19 cm. long, as long as or longer than the leaves, densely up to 25-flowered or more; peduncle 12–30 mm. long; bracts amplexicaul, conical, 1–2 mm. long. Flowers dull pink with a purplish tinge; pedicel and ovary 1–2 mm. long. Dorsal sepal elliptic or obovate, obtuse, 1.5–3.3 mm. long, 1–2.5 mm. wide; lateral sepals slightly falcate-linear, obtuse, 2–4.3 mm. long, 1.2–2.1 mm. wide. Petals circular or broadly ovate, obtuse, 1.5–2.8 mm. long, 1.1–3.5 mm. wide. Lip flabellate, retuse at apex, 1.4–3.7 mm. long, 2.5–4.7 mm. wide. Spur incurved, cylindrical, 4.3–7 mm. long. Column 0.8–1.2 mm. long; viscidia 2; stipites 2; rostellum pendent, swollen.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: A pendent epiphyte or rarely a lithophyte with stems up to 40 cm. or more long, 3–5 mm. diameter. Roots smooth, 2–3 mm. diameter. Leaves falcate, narrowly oblong to oblanceolate, unequally and roundly bilobed at apex, 6.5–14 cm. long, 1.3–2.5 cm. wide, twisted at base to lie in one plane, articulated to a 1.4–1.7 cm. long sheathing base. Inflorescences 5.5–8.5 cm. long, laxly 5–10-flowered; peduncle 1–1.5 cm. long; bracts obconical, acute or apiculate, 2–3.5 mm. long. Flowers translucent white or cream; pedicel and ovary 2–4 mm. long. Dorsal sepal ovate, acute, 5–5.6 mm. long, 2.8–3.4 mm. wide; lateral sepals falcate, lanceolate, acute, 7–7.5 mm. long, 1.8–2 mm. wide. Petals obliquely triangular-ovate, acuminate, 5–5.7 mm. long, 3–3.6 mm. wide, erose. Lip obscurely 3-lobed in basal half, oblong-ovate in outline, emarginate to obtuse and shortly apiculate at apex, 6–7.7 mm. long, 6.6–7.5 mm. wide, with a tooth-like callus in the mouth of the spur. Spur incurved, slightly dilated in middle, 8–9 mm. long. Column 1.5 mm. long; rostellum pendent, subclavate; stipites 2; viscidia 2.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: A pendent to erect epiphyte with a 2–15 cm. long stem, 3 mm. diameter, somewhat laterally compressed. Roots branching, silvery green, to 20 cm. long, 3–4 mm. diameter. Leaves distichous, narrowly oblong, falcate, unequally bilobed at apex, 3.5–8.5 cm. long, 7–9 mm. wide, twisted at base to lie in one plane, articulated to a sheathing base 5 mm. long. Inflorescences 4–7-flowered, pendent or subpendent, 2–4 cm. long; peduncle terete, tapering to base, 1.5–2 cm. long; bracts ovate, acute, 1–2 mm. long. Flowers spirally arranged in a head, yellow-green, very fragrant; pedicel and ovary 5 mm. long. Dorsal sepal elliptic-lanceolate, acute, 4–5 mm. long, 2.2 mm. wide; lateral sepals similar. Petals lanceolate, acute, 3.8–4 mm. long, 1.2–1.3 mm. wide. Lip recurved, lanceolate to obscurely 3-lobed, acute, 4.2–5 mm. long, 2.5 mm. wide, with a low transverse callus at the base. Spur parallel to ovary, straight, cylindrical, 8–13 mm. long. Column 1 mm. long; stipites 2; viscidia 2, elliptic, yellow; rostellum pendent-recurved, anchor-shaped. Fig. 128.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: An epiphyte with long pendent, sometimes branching stems, 20–150 cm. long, 3–5 mm. diameter. Leaves distichous, in upper half of stem, oblong-obovate, unequally roundly bilobed at apex, 2.6–6 cm. long, 1–2 cm. wide, twisted at base and articulated to a 7–10 mm. long bilaterally flattened sheath. Inflorescences as long as or shorter than the leaves, 3–6.5 cm. long, densely many-flowered; peduncle 8–15 mm. long; bracts amplexicaul, conical, 2 mm. long. Flowers pale yellow, fragrant; pedicel and ovary 7.5–10 mm. long. Dorsal sepal lanceolate-elliptic, acute or obtuse, 8–9 mm. long, 3.2–4 mm. wide; lateral sepals falcate, oblong-elliptic to lanceolate, acute or obtuse, 8.8–14 mm. long, 2.3–3 mm. wide. Petals obliquely triangular-ovate, acute, 6.7–9 mm. long, 4.2–7 mm. wide. Lip flabellate, sometimes obscurely 2–4-lobed, emarginate to apiculate, 11–12 mm. long, 10–17 mm. wide, erose on apical margins, with a prominent tooth in the mouth of the spur. Spur cylindrical from a conical base, incurved or sigmoid, 15–21 mm. long. Column 3 mm. long; stipites 2; viscidia 2; rostellum pendent, clavate. Pl. 6.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: An epiphyte with 10–35 cm. long pendent stems, 3–4 mm. diameter. Leaves in apical half of stem, distichous, linear, unequally roundly bilobed at apex, 2.5–4.5 cm. long, 5–10 mm. wide, twisted at base and articulated to a 7–13 mm. long sheath. Inflorescences 1–several, 5–13-flowered, 1.5–8 cm. long; peduncle 2–4 mm. long; rhachis zigzag; bracts triangular, acute, 1–2.5 mm. long. Flowers pale yellow or pale green; pedicel and ovary 2.5–3 mm. long. Dorsal sepal oblong to ovate-elliptic, obtuse or rounded, 2.7–4 mm. long, 1.5–2 mm. wide; lateral sepals oblong to oblong-elliptic, obtuse, 3.3–4.5 mm. long, 1.3–1.6 mm. wide. Petals ovate, obtuse or acute, 2.8–3.5 mm. long, 1.7–2.7 mm. wide. Lip flabellate or obovate, obtuse or retuse, 2.5–3.6 mm. long, 2.8–3.5 mm. wide, with an obscure tooth in the mouth of the spur. Spur slightly incurved, cylindrical to narrowly fusiform, 4.5–6.8 mm. long. Column 1.2–1.5 mm. long; stipites 2; viscidia 2; rostellum pendent, clavate.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: A dwarf epiphyte often forming a tangled mass of stems and roots; stems erect to pendent, up to 20 cm. long, 2 mm. diameter, bearing prominent branching roots all along stem. Leaves fleshy, not at all obvious, linear, rounded at unequally bilobed apex, up to 4.5 cm. long, 1.5 mm. wide, articulated to an 8–10 mm. long leaf-sheath. Inflorescences 1–several, 4–7-flowered, 2–2.5 cm. long; peduncle 6–10 mm. long; rhachis somewhat zig-zag; bracts ovate, acute, 1 mm. long. Flowers tiny, glistening green; pedicel and ovary 2–2.5 mm. long. Dorsal sepal elliptic, rounded to subacute, 3.5 mm. long, 1.5–1.8 mm. wide; lateral sepals spreading, elliptic, rounded, 3–3.7 mm. long, 1.3–1.6 mm. wide. Petals elliptic-ovate, acute, 3–3.3 mm. long, 1.2–1.7 mm. wide. Lip entire, recurved, ovate, acute, 2.2–2.5 mm. long, 1.5 mm. wide, with an obscure bilobed callus at the base. Spur swollen towards apex, pendent-recurved, 3.8–4 mm. long. Column 1 mm. long; stipites 2; viscidia 2; rostellum pendent, peg-like.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: An epiphyte often growing in masses, with spreading or pendulous stems, 9–26 cm. long, 1–3 mm. diameter. Leaves 3–8, towards apex of stems, falcate, linear-lanceolate, obliquely bilobed at acute apex, 1–6 cm. long, 7–13 mm. wide, twisted at base and articulated to a sheathing leaf-base 5–11 mm. long. Inflorescences 1–many, shorter than or equal to leaf, 1–3 cm. long, up to 7-flowered; peduncle 5–7 mm. long; bracts amplexicaul, conical, 2 mm. long. Flowers white, sweetly scented; pedicel and ovary 4–12 mm. long. Dorsal sepal oblong-elliptic, obtuse, 4–4.5 mm. long, 2–2.8 mm. wide; lateral sepals obliquely ovate or elliptic, obtuse, 4.2–5.1 mm. long, 2–2.5 mm. wide. Petals obliquely ovate, obtuse or acute, 4.2–4.8 mm. long, 2.5 mm. wide. Lip flabellate, obscurely 2–4-lobed on apical margin, retuse, 4.5–6.5 mm. long, 6.2–7.6 mm. wide, with a tooth in the mouth of the spur. Spur slender, cylindrical from a broad mouth, 15–25 mm. long. Column 2 mm. long; stipites 2; viscidia 2; rostellum pendent, clavate.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: An epiphyte with an elongate stem, 8–9 cm. long. Leaves linear, unequally bilobed at apex, 6–12 cm. long, 0.5–0.8 cm. wide, articulated to a sheathing base 8 mm. long. Inflorescences 1–several, 6–18 cm. long, sublaxly many-flowered; peduncle ± 1 cm. long; bracts sheathing, 1–1.5 mm. long. Flowers yellowish green to pinkish; pedicel and ovary 3 mm. long. Dorsal sepal oblong-elliptic, obtuse, 4–5 mm. long; lateral sepals obliquely oblong-elliptic, obtuse, 4.5–6 mm. long. Petals elliptic, subacute or obtuse, 3.7–5 mm. long, 2.8–3.3 mm. wide. Lip obovate or broadly elliptic, notched at apex, 5.25–6 mm. long, 5.5–6.75 mm. wide, erose, with a tooth in the mouth of the spur. Spur 8–9 mm. long. Column 1.8–2 mm. long; stipites 2; viscidia 2; rostellum pendent, subclavate.
bibliographicCitation: Orchidaceae, V. S. Summerhayes. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1968

description: An epiphyte usually with long stems, 6–27 cm. long, 3–6 mm. diameter. Leaves up to 25 in upper half of stem, linear to oblanceolate, unequally roundly bilobed at apex, 3–15 cm. long, 5–7 mm. wide, articulated to an 8–15 mm. long leaf-base. Inflorescences 1–many, 3–9 cm. long, densely many-flowered; peduncle 5–10 mm. long; bracts ± amplexicaul, conical, obtuse, 1–2 mm. long. Flowers creamy yellow, diurnally sweetly scented; pedicel and ovary 1.5–2.5 mm. long. Dorsal sepal oblong-elliptic to ovate, obtuse, 2.8–3.5 mm. long, 1.7–2.7 mm. wide; lateral sepals obliquely elliptic, obtuse, 3.8–5 mm. long, 1.7–2.4 mm. wide. Petals circular to broadly ovate, obtuse, 2.4–3.6 mm. long, 2–3 mm. wide. Lip flabellate, obscurely 2–4-lobed on apical margin, emarginate, 3.3–4.5 mm. long, 3.2–5.7 mm. wide, erose on apical margin, with a low obscure transverse callus at the mouth of the spur.
