Sepals 5–9 mm. long; apical portion foliaceous, elliptic-oblong, often unequal, 1.5–6.5 mm. long, 1–3 mm. wide, adpressed pilose; basal part convex, densely long-pilose with ± spreading hairs. Corolla white, 5–7 mm. long, lobed. Capsule globose, pointed, about 4–5.5 mm. tall, hirsute above. Seeds glabrous, brown or black, 2.2–2.5 mm. long, 1.5 mm. wide.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Woody climber with glabrous stems. Leaf-blade ovate, 2.8–8.5 cm. long, 1.6–5.2 cm. wide, obtuse to acute and mucronate at apex, entire or cordate at the base, glabrous; petiole 1–3 cm. long, sometimes minutely pubescent. Flowers in axillary congested panicles with peduncles 0.3–2 cm. long and in terminal panicles; rhachis of the inflorescence adpressed pubescent. Sepals orbicular, 1.5 mm. in diameter, pubescent. Corolla white, about 5 mm. long; lobes 4 mm. long, 2.5 mm. wide, pubescent outside; margins hyaline and ± reflexed. Capsule ovoid, slightly compressed, 5.5 mm. long, 4.5 mm. wide, glabrous, brown or black. Seeds dark, orbicular, compressed, wrinkled and minutely reticulate in the dry state, 3 mm. in diameter. Fig. 9, p. 32.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Annual twiner; stems pubescent. Leaf-blade ovate-cordate, up to 4.5(–8) cm. long and 3.5(–5) cm. wide, acuminate at the apex, glabrescent above and sparsely pubescent beneath on the nerves or densely tomentose all over; petiole up to 2.5(–6) cm. long, pubescent. Flowers several to many in a ± dense cyme; peduncle up to 5.5 cm. long, pubescent; secondarypeduncles and pedicels up to 0.5 cm. long; bracts minute. Sepals ovate, acute, about 6 mm. long, 2.5–4 mm. wide, pubescent. Corolla white, pink or yellow, 1 cm. long. Capsule globose, 5–6 mm. in diameter, straw-coloured. Seeds dark, subtrigonous, 2.5 mm. long, with very narrow ± indistinct hyaline margins and pale raised roughenings.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Perennial climber; stems twining, rarely prostrate, up to 2 m. long, hairy. Leaf-blade triangular-oblong or oblong-ovate, rarely narrow, 3–8.5 cm. long, 2.3–6 cm. wide, acute at the apex, cordate or rarely subhastate at the base, pilose particularly on the veins below, becoming glabrescent or glabrous, rarely very hairy; petiole up to 3.5 cm. long. Inflorescence hairy, capitate, densely bracteate; peduncle 2.5–11.5 cm. long. Bracts ovate, ± hyaline, acute, up to 10 mm. long and 7.5 mm. wide. Sepals ovate, acute, apiculate, ± scarious, 9–13 mm. long and 5–8(–10) mm. wide. Corolla white, often with purple streaks or pink with dark centre (2.1–) 2.5–3 cm. long and 4 cm. broad at mouth, hairy on middle parts of the lobes. Capsule about 7 mm. in diameter. Seeds black. Fig. 11.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Annual herb; stems many, up to 0.6 m. long from a slender unbranched root, ascending or prostrate, pubescent. Leaf-blade ovate, oblong or elliptic, up to 5 cm. long and 1.1 cm. wide, obtuse or minutely apiculate at the apex, truncate or broadly cuneate and then narrowly cuneate at the base, glabrescent or with a few bristly hairs on the basal margins; petiole about 2 mm. long, ± winged. Inflorescence a many-flowered, globose, subsessile head, 1–2 cm. in diameter, pilose with brown hairs when dry; bracts similar to sepals and leaves. Sepals unequal, lanceolate, 5–7 mm. long and 0.5–1.5 mm. wide. Corolla blue, 8–10 mm. long and about 10–12 mm. in diameter. Capsule 2–3.5(–6) mm. in diameter, pale yellow. Seeds yellow-brown, about 1.5 mm. long, papillate.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Branched perennial; stems prostrate, up to 1 m. long, radiating from a woody rootstock, sparsely to densely covered with long yellowish patent bristly hairs, particularly near the nodes. Leaf-blade palmately 5–7-lobed to about 2/3–3/4 of its length, reniform in outline, 2–8 cm. long, 3–14 cm. wide, glabrous or pilose on the prominent nerves beneath; lobes lanceolate-elliptic or oblong, 2–8 cm. long, 0.4–4 cm. wide, irregularly and shallowly to deeply pinnately lobed and also acutely dentate, acute to emarginate at the apex, with the costa ending in a short mucro; petiole 1–2 cm. long, pilose. Flowers 1–3 in a loose cyme; peduncle 0.7–5 cm. long, pilose; pedicels 0.5–1.5 cm. long, glabrous; bracts small. Sepals toughly membranous, glabrous; outer shorter, ovate-lanceolate to orbicular, 8–9 mm. long, 3–6 mm. wide, acuminate, mucronate or blunt; inner longer, more lanceolate, 11–14 mm. long, 3.5–5 mm. wide. Corolla primrose-yellow with brownish-claret centre, about 2.5–3.5 cm. long, conspicuously lobed; lobes triangular, 4.5–6 mm. long, 6–10 mm. wide.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Trailing plant with stems about 0.5 m. long, hispid with long tubercular-based hairs. Leaf-blade round or reniform in outline, 2.7–8 cm. long, 3.4–11 cm. wide, palmately 3–5(–7)-lobed; lobes ovate, or oblong, up to 3 cm. long and 4 cm. wide, acute or obtuse at the apex; main nerves pale and usually hispid beneath, with lamina between glabrous but minutely punctate; petiole 1.5–10 cm. long, hispid. Inflorescences 3–5-flowered; peduncle 3–7 cm. long. Sepals lanceolate, 10–15 mm. long, 1.5–4 mm. wide, hispid with hairs 3–5 mm. long. Corolla yellow, 1.7–3 cm. long. Fruit not known.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Perennial; stems prostrate, up to 1.2 m. long, radiating from a tough rootstock, pilose with spreading and glandular hairs. Leaf-blade suborbicular in outline, much divided, 1.3–3.5 cm. long, 1.2–4 cm. wide, palmately 5–7(–9)-lobed, pilose above and below with spreading-bristly hairs; lobes obovate-oblong in outline, up to 3 cm. long, each twice or thrice pinnatifid, the individual lobes oblong to deltoid, the margin appearing crinkly; petiole 0.6–1.5 cm. long, spreading-bristly; nerves prominent beneath. Flowers solitary or paired; peduncle 1.5–2.5 cm. long, pilose; pedicels 5–20 mm. long; bracts small, linear. Sepals ovate-oblong, 6 mm. long, 2–3 mm. wide, bluntly acute or rounded at the apex, pubescent. Corolla yellow with purple centre, 1.5–2 cm. long, shallowly lobed; midpetaline areas and apices of lobes pubescent. Capsule unknown.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Perennial; stems trailing for about 0.3–1 m., hispid with rather long fine spreading tubercle-based hairs. Leaf-blade palmately divided to the base; lobes 3, linear, each lateral one again divided into 3 branches and the lowermost lobe often yet again divided, pilose or glabrescent; the longest leaf-lobes are 4 cm. long and 1.7 mm. wide; petiole 1.6–2.2 cm. long, pilose. Peduncle pilose, 1-flowered, 1.7–2 cm. long; pedicels 0.4–1 cm. long; bracts minute. Sepals subequal or the outer a little smaller, elliptic or oblong, 6(–9) mm. long, 3.5(–5) mm. wide, obtuse or truncate, rarely mucronulate or acute, glabrous. Corolla yellow with violet centre, 1.6 cm. long. Capsule not known.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Strong woody twiner; stems pubescent or glabrescent, yellow, ridged. Leaf-blade broadly ovate to suborbicular, 6.5–11 cm. long, 6–14 cm. wide, obtuse, shortly acuminate or rounded at the apex, deeply cordate-emarginate at the base, glabrous or slightly pubescent, particularly on theveins beneath, strongly punctate beneath; petiole 2–8 cm. long. Inflorescences axillary (1–) 2–several-flowered; peduncle usually very short, about 5 mm. long; pedicels up to 2.5 cm. long. Sepals oval, about 1.5–2 cm. long and 1 cm. wide, the outer shorter than the inner, ± emarginate but mucronate, glabrous. Corolla bright scarlet with paler tube, funnel-shaped, 5.5–7 cm. long; midpetaline areas pubescent at the apex. Capsule globose, straw-coloured, 1.8 cm. in diameter. Seeds subglobose, brown, shortly pubescent, 6 × 7 × 5 mm.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Glabrous twiner. Leaf-blade ovate, up to 9 cm. long and 6 cm. wide, acuminate at the apex, cordate at the base, very densely and minutely glandular-punctate beneath; petiole 2.5–13 cm. long. Inflorescences very lax, 1–4-flowered; peduncle 3.5–7.5 cm. long; secondary peduncles and pedicels 1–3.5 cm. long. Sepals rounded-oblong, 5.5–8 mm. long, 5–6(–7) mm. wide, ± truncate above, hyaline and minutely ciliate at the margin. Corolla pale mauve, narrowly funnel-shaped, 7.5–8 cm. long. Fruit not known.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Perennial climber; stems softly velvety with ± patent pubescence. Leaf-blade ovate, up to 19 cm. long and 14 cm. wide, acuminate at the apex, cordate at the base, silvery-velvety on both surfaces; petiole 7.5–15 cm. long. Flowers in loose, axillary, several- to many-flowered cymes; peduncle 0.5–5.5 cm. long; pedicels 1.0–1.5 cm. long. Sepals rather thin, wrinkled and with raised parallel nerves, ovate, 2.2–3 cm. long, 1.3–2.1 cm. wide, blunt or subacute at the apex, mucronulate, softly pubescent, below densely covered with pubescent filamentous outgrowths up to 6 mm. long. Corolla pale pink streaked with white, 7.5 cm. long; midpetaline areas softly pubescent. Fruit not seen.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Perennial herb about 0.3 m. tall; stems several, decumbent, about 1 m. long, at first brownish-tomentose, later glabrous. Leaf-blade round or squarish-reniform, 1.3–4 cm. long, 1.3–3.7 cm. wide, rounded or subacute at the minutely apiculate apex, cordate at the base, entire to coarsely dentate, stellately pubescent on both surfaces; petiole 0.7–3.5 cm. long. Flowers axillary, solitary; peduncle 0.8–2.4 cm. long; pedicels about 8 mm. long; bracts large, oblong-elliptic or cymbiform, 2.1–3.7 cm. long, 0.9–1.4 cm. wide, stellate-tomentose on both sides. Outer sepals larger, ovate or rounded-oblong; inner oblong-lanceolate to lanceolate, 1–1.5 cm. long, 4–12 mm. wide, tomentose outside, glabrous inside. Corolla white, glabrous; tube very narrow, 4.2–6 cm. long, 2–4.5 mm. wide; limb funnel-shaped, 3 cm. long, 4.8–6 cm. wide. Capsule subglobose, 1.3–1.5 cm. high, 1.0 cm. wide, glabrous; fruiting pedicels thickened. Seeds ovoid, 7 mm. long, 4.25–5.5 mm. wide, brown, shortly woolly.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Short-lived perennial up to 1.2 m. tall; stems erect, or rarely decumbent, unbranched or sparsely branched just above the ground, up to 2 cm. in diameter at point of junction with the root, densely stellately subferruginously tomentose. Leaf-blade broadly elliptic or obovate, 6.3–10 cm. long, 3.8–6 cm. wide, blunt but mucronate at the apex, narrowly cuneate at the base; margins coarsely wavy or lobed above, rarely entire; sparsely stellately hairy above, beset with ± dense grey granular tomentum beneath; petiole about 2.5 cm. long. Peduncle 1–9 cm. long, usually long; inflorescence a subcapitate (1–)6-flowered cyme; pedicels about 6 mm. long. Sepals ovate-lanceolate to lanceolate, 1–1.4 cm. long, acute. Corolla purple with lighter limb or white with a purple eye, (2–)2.5–3.5 cm. long. Capsule ovoid, 6–8 mm. tall.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Shrubby herb with robust stem; rootstock unknown; branches densely covered with subferruginous tomentum. Leaf-blade suborbicular or broadly ovate, 6–10 cm. in diameter, obtuse but ± mucronate at the apex, shallowly cordate at the base, with margin remotely shallowly dentate or undulate, tomentose above and beneath; venation prominent beneath; petiole 1.5–2.5 cm. long. Flowers in dense, many-flowered, capitate cymes; peduncle 3–5 cm. long; pedicels 5 mm. long; bracts small, oblong. Sepals lanceolate to ovate, 10 mm. long, 3–4 mm. wide, acute. Corolla very pale purple, funnel-shaped, 4.5 cm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Annual or biennial herb with long slender rootstock; stems 3–5, prostrate, 12–60 cm. long, densely white-pilose above, glabrescent beneath. Leaf-blade lanceolate to oblong-ovate in outline, 1.5–3.5 cm. long, 0.4–3.5 cm. wide; petiole 0.2–2 cm. long; upper leaves lanceolate, entire or with two small basal lobes; lower and radical leaves 3–13-lobed, with the lobes linear, 0.5–3 cm. long, 0.1–0.3 cm. wide, sometimes sparsely toothed, somewhat pilose. Flowers axillary, solitary; pedicels 3 mm. long. Outer sepals 6 mm. long, base ovate and coriaceous, often toothed on either side, apex narrow and foliaceous; inner much shorter, elliptic, hyaline. Corolla pink with dark centre, very narrowly tubular, 1.1 cm. long, tube 0.75 mm. wide and limb 5 mm. wide, opening in the evening. Capsule globose, glabrous, 5 mm. diameter, 6-valved. Seeds 4–6, collateral, together forming a sphere, pale brown with dark spots and patches of pubescence, 2.1 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Perennial; stems probably several from a woody rootstock, 0.3 m. long, trailing, densely bristly with long yellow hairs. Leaf-blade ovate, up to 5 cm. long and 3 cm. wide, ± acute or apiculate at the apex, cordate at the base, covered with somewhat scattered 2 mm. long bristly yellow hairs; petiole 0.5–3 cm. long, densely bristly. Peduncle 11 mm. long, 1-flowered; bracts ovate, 15 mm. long, 8 mm. wide, bristly; pedicels 5 mm. long. Outer sepals ovate, 12–14 mm. long, 6.5–8 mm. wide, acute, bristly. Corolla violet, very narrowly funnel-shaped, 4.5–5 cm. long; tube less than 2 mm. wide just above the base; limb 2 cm. wide at apex.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Perennial; stems ± pilose, trailing, up to 1.8 m. long. Leaf-blade ovate-orbicular or reniform, 5.5–7.8 cm. long, 5.4–7.8 cm. wide, rounded but apiculate at the apex, cordate with a broad sinus at the base, glabrous or pubescent above, ± hairy or glabrous on veins beneath; petiole 5–7.5 cm. long. Peduncle (1–)3(–6)-flowered, 1–7 cm. long, hairy; pedicels up to 2.6 cm. long; bracts broadly ovate, acute or acuminate, 0.9–1.8 cm. long, 0.7– 1.8 cm. wide. Outer sepals pilose, ovate, 1.2–1.6 cm. long, 1 cm. wide, cordate below or broadly expanded but rounded, tapering above; inner sepals narrower, 1.5 cm. long, 0.6 cm. wide. Corolla pale lilac with a dark centre or white, funnel-shaped, 3.3–4.5 cm. long, glabrous or pubescent. Capsule globose, 8–12 mm. in diameter, glabrous. Seeds glabrous or velvety pubescent, 4 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Perennial; stems slender, twining or prostrate, up to 3 m., pilose; sometimes flowering when stem very short. Leaf-blade ovate to oblong, 2.2– 12 cm. long, 0.7–7.5 cm. wide, acute to rounded at the apex, cordate at the base, entire, pubescent or hairy on both surfaces; petiole 2.5–8 cm. long, hairy. Inflorescences 2–5-flowered, often lax; peduncle 1.5–9 cm. long; pedicels 1–3.5 cm. long; bracts lanceolate, 3 mm. long (Fig. 22/10, p. 102). Sepals ovate to lanceolate, 7–12 mm. long, 1.5–3 mm. wide, narrowed at the apex, broad at the base, hairy (Fig. 22/1, p. 102); inner sepals narrower. Corolla white to mauve or purple, funnel-shaped, (2–)2.5–3.8 cm. long, pubescent. Capsule globose, 6–7 mm. diameter, tipped with indurated style-base, glabrous. Seeds brown, minutely velvety and with long white hairs on the angles.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Perennial herb, bristly-pilose with orange-brown hairs; stems several, annual, erect or semiprostrate, up to 25 cm. tall, from a tuberous rootstock. Leaf-blade linear to oblong, 1.7–8 cm. long, 0.15–1.8 cm. wide, more or less acute at the apex, cuneate at the base, sparsely bristly-pilose to densely pilose on both surfaces particularly on the margins and nerves beneath; petiole 2–5 mm. long. Flowers solitary in the upper axils; peduncle and pedicel together 0.3–3 cm. long; bracts linear, 0.6–2 cm. long. Sepals linear-triangular, bristly pilose, 0.75–1.7 cm. long, about 1.5 mm. wide. Corolla orange-yellow, pale yellow or white, tubular, little expanded above, 1.8–3.7 cm. long, glabrous below but tips of midpetaline areas hairy; interpetaline areas tenuously thin. Capsule not known.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Annual or perennial; stems erect or prostrate, up to 1.0 m. long, often reddish, adpressedly strigose. Leaf-blade discolorous, oblong or linear-lanceolate, 2.7–7.5 cm. long, 0.25–2.7 cm. wide, pilose above, densely to sparsely white-pilose beneath; petiole up to 7 mm. long. Flowers congested in small, densely pilose heads; peduncle up to 9 cm. long; bracts small, setaceous, ciliate. Sepals lanceolate, 6–10 mm. long, pilose. Corolla red or mauve, funnel-shaped, 1.7–3.3 cm. long, the tube narrow below; midpetaline areas silky. Capsule ovoid-globose, 5.5 mm. in diameter, glabrous. Seeds pubescent.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Annual herb with prostrate or twining stems up to 1 m. long, pilose with long, spreading, yellowish or silvery hairs. Leaf-blade ovate, up to 8.7 cm. long and 5 cm. wide, acute at the apex, ± cordate at the base, green but with long adpressed hairs above, silvery-velvety with dense adpressed hairs beneath; veins also pilose; petiole 1.2–7.5 cm. long, pilose. Flowers in dense heads about 3 cm. wide; peduncle 0.6–4 cm. long; outer bracts foliaceous, up to 3 cm. long and 1 cm. wide; inner bracts narrow, 1.4–1.7 cm. long, 2–4 mm. wide, all with an indumentum similar to that on the leaves. Sepals unequal, accrescent, the outer 6 mm. long, linear-lanceolate. Corolla purple or white, funnel-shaped, 1.7–2.4 cm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Perennial; stems several, bristly-pilose, prostrate, up to 1 m. long from a little-branched rootstock or sometimes flowering when stems very short. Leaf-blade orbicular in outline, either deeply 3-lobed, with reniform or obovate-orbicular lobes, or entire but with a conspicuously crenate margin, up to 4.5 cm. long and 6 cm. wide, obtuse or emarginate but mucronulate at the apex, with a deep sinus at the base, green and adpressedly bristly-pilose above, with dense white-cottony tomentum and yellow-bristly nerves beneath; petiole up to 7 cm. long. Flowers in few-flowered dense heads; peduncle up to 13 cm. long, pilose; bracts lanceolate, strigose, 9 mm. long. Sepals lanceolate, 7–9(–16) cm. long. Corolla white with mauve or purple centre or all pink, funnel-shaped, 2.5–3 cm. long. Capsule ovoid, 5 mm. tall, pubescent at the apex.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Perennial; stems twining, pilose with yellow-bristly hairs. Leaf-blade thin, ± orbicular in outline, up to 9 cm. long and 10 cm. wide, shallowly 3-lobed, with the lobes rounded and obtuse at the apex, and with a deep sinus at the base, adpressed pilose above and also with an understorey of shorter hairs, densely covered beneath with a white-cottony indumentum except on the nerves which are yellow-bristly; petiole up to 12 cm. long. Flowers in a dense bracteate head; peduncle up to 20 cm. long, densely yellow-setose; bracts ovate-lanceolate to ovate, up to 1.5 cm. long and 0.7 cm. wide, identical with the leaves in indumentum but bristles on veins are longer and glands are also present. Sepals similar to the bracts, about 1.2 cm. long, the white tomentum very dense. Corolla 4–5 cm. long, white with purple throat, partly covered (particularly below) with white tomentum outside.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: A robust rather woody climber; stems attaining over 15 m. in length, roughly hirsute in longitudinal lines or almost glabrous; older portions woody, pale brown and ridged. Leaf-blade ovate, 3.8–15.3(–18) cm. long and 2.2–12(–15.8) cm. wide, acute or acuminate at the apex, cordate at the base, glabrous or pilose above, glabrescent to densely hairy beneath with matted ± adpressed hairs but never with arachnoid tomentum; petiole usually densely hairy with spreading hairs 0.75–9(–13.5) cm. Flowers in rather lax to dense, few- to many-flowered cymes; peduncle 1.5–12 cm. long; bracts lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, acute, adpressed pilose and densely glandular, 4–13 mm. long and 2–8 mm. wide. Sepals similar to the bracts in shape and indumentum, 8–12 mm. long, 2.5–6 mm. wide. Corolla mauve with a deeper mauve centre, funnel-shaped, 3–4 cm. long; limb 4–5 cm. wide; midpetaline areas sparsely pubescent. Capsule globose, pilose, about 1 cm. in diameter. Seeds subglobose, blackish-brown, glabrous, about 4 mm. in diameter.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Perennial or rarely annual (fide Milne-Redhead & Taylor 10707); stems several from a woody tuberous rootstock, yellow-brown, ridged, pilose to glabrous. Leaf-blade ovate-cordate, triangular, oblong-triangular or lanceolate, 1–12 cm. long, 1–9.3 cm. wide, ± acuminate or acute at the apex, truncate, sagittate, hastate or with rounded lobes at the base, glabrous save for the margins which are minutely puberulous; petiole 1–4 cm. long. Inflorescences few–many-flowered, rather dense; peduncle 1.5–12(–23) cm. long; pedicels 0.75–1.2 cm. long. Sepals elliptic-oblong or ovate, 4–8 mm. long, obtuse to acutish, glabrous, the outer ones sometimes verruculose. Corolla lilac-pink or almost white, sometimes with a purple or maroon centre, 2–6 cm. long; limb almost salver-shaped; tube narrow. Stamens and style included or very slightly exserted. Capsule globose, glabrous, (4–)6–7 mm. in diameter. Seeds subtrigonous, pale, about 3 mm. diameter, densely tomentose and also with some longer hairs.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Perennial herb with a woody rootstock or globose tuber as big as a cricket ball; stems stiff, trailing, simple or branched, glabrous or minutely puberulous, 8–45 cm. long. Leaves often erect, glabrous or asperulous; blade linear-lanceolate to oblong, 4.5–12.5(–24) cm. long, 0.3–1.8 cm. wide or rarely more, acute at the apex, cuneate at the base, occasionally incised or trisected; petiole very short. Peduncle axillary, short, 1–3-flowered. Sepals lanceolate, 1–1.4 cm. long, 3.5 mm. wide, acuminate or subacute, glabrous or minutely puberulous. Corolla rose-pink or white with pink or mauve centre, funnel-shaped, 4.8–6 cm. long, ± minutely asperulous above. The plant sometimes flowers profusely when almost leafless.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Perennial herb; stems prostrate, up to 1.8 m. long, glabrous or with lines of hairs near the nodes. Leaves ovate-orbicular or broadly cordate, with an open sinus at the base, 4–11 cm. long and wide, obtuse or acuminate, apiculate at the apex, gland-dotted beneath; petiole 5–10.5 cm. long. Peduncle (1–)3–5-flowered, 2–10.5 cm. long; pedicels 1.3–3.2 cm. long. Calyx with sepals overlapping to form a loose tube; sepals 9–11 mm. long, about 7 mm. wide, obtuse at the apex, the inner three larger. Corolla magenta, very narrowly funnel-shaped, the tube very narrow at the base, 3.5–6 cm. long, 2–2.5 mm. in diameter at the base of the tube. Capsule 1.5 cm. in diameter, the accrescent sepals up to 2.2 cm. long and 1 cm. wide. Seeds brown, pilose near the hilum, 7–8 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Perennial; stems twining, glabrous but minutely muriculate. Leaf-blade round in outline, biternately or pedately or palmately 7–9-lobed, up to 3.5 cm. long and 5 cm. wide; lobes linear, ± acute and aristate or mucronulate, 2.5–3 cm. long and 2–3 mm. wide; petiole muriculate, 1.5–2.5 cm. long; pseudo-stipules present. Peduncle axillary, 1–few-flowered, 0.5–1 cm. long; pedicels up to 2–4 cm. long. Sepals suborbicular or elliptic, the inner larger, not noticeably gibbous at the base, 4–6.3 mm. long, 4 mm. wide, reflexed in fruit. Corolla pink or mauve, up to 7.5 cm. long. Capsule globose, about 8 mm. in diameter. Seeds subglobose-trigonous, about 4 mm. in diameter, brown with adpressed pubescence and with long white hairs on the angles. Fig. 23, p. 124.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Glabrous perennial; stems long, prostrate. Leaf-blade orbicular in outline, palmately 7-lobed to the base, 5–7.5 cm. long and wide; lobes narrow, lanceolate, 5–8 cm. long, 0.55–0.7 cm. wide; margin undulate; outer lobes often bifid; petiole 4 cm. long. Peduncle 7.5 cm. long, many-flowered; pedicels short. Sepals ovate, acute, 6 mm. long. Corolla purple, funnel-shaped, about 4 cm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Glabrous perennial; stems twining, smooth. Leaves compound, divided into 5 leaflets; leaflets narrowly elliptic, 7–8.5 cm. long and 1.5–2.4 cm. wide, acuminate and apiculate; petiolules 0.5–1.2 cm. long; petiole 4–5 cm. long. Peduncle 10–11 cm. long, many-flowered; pedicels about 1 cm. long. Sepals ovate, 7–7.5 mm. long, 4.2–8 mm. wide, acute and apiculate, the outer ones shorter. Corolla purple, violet or white, funnel-shaped, 4.5–7.5 cm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Very similar to the last species in habit and foliage. Leaf-blade small, orbicular in outline, palmately 5-lobed to the base with the basal lobes usually again bilobed, about 2.5–3.5 cm. in diameter; lobes obovate, up to 2.5 cm. long and 2.2 cm. wide, rounded in outline at the apex, strongly cuneate at the base, sharply toothed; petiole 0.5–2.5 cm. long. Peduncle 1.5–2 cm. long, often conspicuously winged, 1–2-flowered; bracts leafy, up to 2.0 cm. long, with 3 pinnatifid lobes; pedicels 5–7 mm. long. Sepals elliptic, 6–7 mm. long, 3–3.5 mm. wide, obtuse, the outer cuspidate, smooth, tuberculate or cristate. Corolla white; tube narrowly cylindric, 1.7–2.1 cm. long, 1.5–2 mm. in diameter; limb funnel-shaped, 9 mm. long, 13 mm. wide. Capsule globose, 6–7 mm. in diameter, 6-valved. Seeds 6, trigonous, about 3 mm. long, pubescent, brown.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Annual herb; stems erect or decumbent, up to 45 cm. high, pubescent. Leaf-blade pubescent, obovate or spathulate; apical part elliptic to orbicular, 4.7–5.5 cm. long, 3.7–4.8 cm. wide, ± acute at the apex, obscurely crenulate; basal part narrowly cuneate, 2 cm. long, 0.7–1.5 cm. wide at the apex; petiole about 1 cm. long. Peduncle up to 2 cm. long, often much shorter; inflorescence ± 6-flowered, the flowers clustered in an umbel-like cyme; bracts pubescent, ± 3-nerved, 3 mm. long, 1.5 mm. wide; pedicels 6 mm. long. Sepals linear-oblong, 5.5–9 mm. long, 2.5–3.5 mm. wide, obtuse, conspicuously 3-nerved. Corolla white, trumpet-shaped; tube narrow, 13 mm. long, 1.5–3 mm. wide; limb 7 mm. long. Ovary elongate-conic, 2.5 mm. long, 1 mm. wide, shortly pubescent. Capsule elongate-ovoid, 9–10 mm. long, slightly pubescent. Seeds black, somewhat obscurely tuberculate, sparsely pubescent with long hairs.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Annual herb, branched near the base; stems slender, twining, obscurely pubescent. Leaf-blade ovate in outline, 2.4–6.6 cm. long, 2.4–4.7 cm. wide, acute, widely cordate at the base, margins with 2 or 3 deltoid acute or subacute lobes on each side of basal half, the whole leaf appearing ± 5(–7)-lobed, thin, very sparsely pubescent; petiole about 3 cm. long. Flowers solitary or in 2-flowered cymes; peduncle 6–10 mm. long; pedicels 5–12 mm. long. Sepals 3-nerved, spathulate; apical part ovate, apiculate, 4 mm. long,3 mm. wide; basal part linear-oblong, 3 mm. long, 2 mm. wide. Corolla white, with narrow tube and ± salver-shaped limb, 2.5 cm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Woody twiner; stems roughened, muriculate, puberulous when young. Leaves often not present at the time of flowering; blade ovate-triangular, 6 cm. long, 3.7 cm. wide, prominently cuspidate at the apex, subtruncate at the base; petiole about 2.5 cm. long, slender. Peduncle short, up to 0.5 cm. long, arranged on short woody branchlets, 1–few-flowered (usually 3); pedicels up to 1.5 cm. long. Sepals oblong-elliptic, 10–12 mm. long, 5–5.5 mm. wide, obtuse but mucronulate at the apex, glabrous, margins pellucid. Corolla white or greenish-yellow with purple or crimson centre, funnel-shaped or narrowly campanulate, with tube not prominently constricted at the base, 3.7–4.5 cm. long; in bud densely bristly pubescent at extreme apex. Capsule elongate-ovoid, 1.7 cm. long. Seeds with long silky hairs.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Perennial herb with twining stems. Leaf-blade cordate, about 7 cm. long, and 8 cm. wide, markedly acuminate at the apex, shaped like those of a Tilia but sometimes truncate at the base, glabrous but somewhat punctate below. Flowers 3–4 in lax cymes; peduncle 1–6.5 cm. long; pedicels 1–2.5 cm. long. Sepals lanceolate, 6 mm. long and 2 mm. wide, edges hyaline. Corolla white, funnel-shaped, 8.5 cm. long. Capsule not known.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Stout liane; stems angular, pubescent or glabrescent, twining, up to 9 m. long. Leaf-blade ovate, slightly cordate, entire or slightly lobed to deeply pinnately or subpalmately divided into 5–11 lobes, 7.5–16 cm. long, 7.5–14(–30) cm. wide, green and glabrous above, with mottled white pubescence below, mainly on the veins, strongly bullate; lobes oblong, up to 8 cm. long and 1.5 cm. wide; petiole 5–7.5 cm. long. Flowers several in a lax cyme; peduncles 1–2 cm. long; pedicels about 1.6 cm. long. Sepals suborbicular, truncate at the apex, finely white-tomentose or rarely glabrescent, 1.3–2 cm. long, 0.9–1.1 cm. wide. Corolla red-purple or crimson, funnel-shaped, the tube not at all slender, 7–7.5(–9) cm. long, hairy outside when in bud, later glabrescent (Fig. 22/9, p. 102). Capsule not seen.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Robust herb with tuberous root; stems glabrous or pubescent, hollow, coarse, twining (rarely prostrate). Leaf-blade ovate in outline, usually deeply pinnately or subpalmately divided into 7–11 lobes, about 11 cm. long and 17 cm. wide, ± cordate, green and glabrous above, pubescent beneath, particularly on the nerves, crenate and bullate between the lateral nerves; lobes linear-oblong, obtuse or subacute, 5.2–8 cm. long, 0.8–2 cm. wide; rarely the lamina is entire, lobed or very coarsely toothed, particularly in cultivated specimens; petiole 4–14 cm. long. Flowers several in a lax cyme; peduncle 2.5–10 cm. long; pedicels 1.5–5.5 cm. long, striate, enlarging in fruit; bracts 6 mm. long. Sepals elliptic, 1.2–1.8 cm. long, 0.8–1.2 cm. wide, pubescent or glabrescent, accrescent in fruit. Corolla-limb red-purple or white, salver-shaped, 7 cm. diameter, with frilly margin; tube narrow, 7.5– 8 cm. long, 0.7 cm. in diameter (Fig. 22/8, p. 102). Capsule ovoid, 2.6 cm. long. Seeds elongate-ovoid, 9–10 mm. long, 7–8 mm. wide, densely covered with white woolly hairs up to 2 cm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Erect subwoody shrub up to 0.6 m. tall, often flowering when leafless; young stems tomentose, soon becoming glabrous. Leaf-blade orbicular or reniform, 6–9 cm. long, 7.5–12.5 cm. wide, acute, rounded or retuse at the apex, velvety-pubescent or glabrescent above, densely velvety-tomentose beneath, sometimes only on the nerves; petiole 6 cm. long, biglandular at the apex. Flowers solitary, clustered at the apex of the shoots; peduncle 0.5–1.1 cm. long; pedicels up to 2.5 cm. long, very thick in fruit. Sepals ovate-oblong or elliptic, 1.6–2.3 cm. long, 0.8–1.6 cm. wide, with the outer two a little shorter, obtuse or emarginate at the apex, coriaceous, glabrous or sparsely tomentose. Corolla opening at night, white, (9.5–)12.5–16 cm. long; tube slender, 8–10 cm. long, 6–13 mm. in diameter; limb salver-shaped, 7.5 cm. in diameter, frilly at the edge. Capsule ovoid, obtuse or truncate, shortly beaked with the persistent style-base, ridged, 2.2–2.7 cm. long, 1.7 cm. wide. Seeds ovoid, 1 cm. long, densely covered with purple-brown hairs about 1.8 cm. long. (Fig. 24/6, p. 131.)
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Woody liane; stems slender, yellowish or greyish, ridged, tomentose at first, later glabrescent. Leaves rapidly deciduous; blade ovate or orbicular, 2.5–9 cm. long, 1.6–9 cm. wide, broadly acute or rounded but apiculate at the apex, cordate at the base, floccose-pubescent, later glabescent above, velvety or pubescent beneath; petiole 2–6.0 cm. long, biglandular at the apex. Flowers 1–4 at the apices of the shoots; peduncle and pedicels together 1.5–5 cm. long. Sepals elliptic-oblong, 1.8 cm. long, 1.1–1.4 cm. wide, enlarging in fruit up to 2.2 cm. long, obtuse, tomentose or glabrous. Corolla white; tube cylindrical, 5–6 cm. long, about 6 mm. in diameter; limb salver-shaped, about 6 cm. wide, frilly-edged. Capsule ovoid, glabrous, 2.3 cm. long, 1.8 cm. in diameter. Seeds oblong-ovoid, compressed, brown, 10–11 mm. long, 6 mm. wide, covered with long, white, tangled, cottony hairs about 3 cm. long. The dehisced fruits strongly resemble cotton-bolls.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: A woody liane with perennial branches ascending trees up to a distance of 9 m.; rootstock probably tuberous; young branches tomentose at first, later glabrous. Leaves rapidly deciduous, often not present in flowering and fruiting stages; blade ovate, 3–10.5 cm. long, 2.2–8 cm. wide, obtuse and mucronulate at the apex, cordate at the base, glabrous above, the nerves impressed, densely tomentose on the nerves beneath when young, bullate; petiole 3–5 cm, long, biglandular at the apex. Flowers solitary, clustered atthe apices of the shoots; peduncle about 3 mm. long; pedicels 6–7 mm. long, thickening and lengthening in fruit to 1 cm. Sepals elliptic-oblong, 1–1.3 cm. long, 7–9 mm. wide, enlarging in fruit up to 1.4 cm. long, very obtuse, glabrous. Corolla opening at night, white, sweetly scented; tube cylindrical, slender, 5.5–7.5 cm. long, (4–)6–9 mm. in diameter; limb salver-shaped, 9 cm. in diameter, with a frilly edge. Capsule ovoid, about 2 cm. long, 1.5 cm. wide. Seeds shaped like an orange-segment, elongate-ovoid, 11 mm. long, 6.0 mm. wide, covered with long, white, pale brown or whitish hairs about 1.7 cm. long and also scaly under the hairs.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Shrub; stems erect or sprawling-decumbent, up to 1 m. long, which usually die back annually, tomentose when young; rootstock tuberous. Leaf-blade ovate (see note), 3–15 cm. long, 2–12 cm. wide, subacute, or obtuse and mucronulate at the apex, cuneate or truncate at the base, glabrous or glabrescent above, with impressed nerves, densely tomentose beneath particularly on the nerves, later often glabrescent; petiole 1.2–9 cm. long, biglandular at the apex. Flowers solitary, clustered at the apices of the shoots; peduncle and pedicels together about 1 cm. long, elongating to 2.5 cm. or more in fruit. Sepals elongate-elliptic, 10–17 mm. long, 5–8 mm. wide, scarcely enlarging in fruit, very obtuse, glabrous. Corolla opening at night, white, up to 16 cm. long; tube cylindrical, very slender, (7.5–)9–11 cm. long, 3.5–4 mm. in diameter; limb salver-shaped, 7–9 cm. in diameter, frilly-edged. Capsule ovoid, up to 3.0 cm. long, 1.7–2 cm. wide; valves with rather prominent nerves. Seeds as in last species, 15 mm. long, 5 mm. wide, covered with very pale purplish-brown hairs 2–2.5 cm. long. Fig. 24/7, p. 131.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Large subscandent shrub with tuberous root; stems stout, subwoody, up to 7.5 m. long, at first tomentose, later glabrescent. Leaves and flowers borne on short erect shoots. Leaf-blade broadly ovate, 11–14 cm. long, 7–10 cm. wide, cuspidate at the apex, subtruncate or slightly cordate at the base, glabrous above, minutely pubescent beneath, particularly on the veins when young; petioles up to 6 cm. long. Flowers in lax cymes; peduncle 2.5 cm. long; pedicels 0.6–1.3 cm. long; bracts large, obovate, boat-shaped, 3.2 cm. long, 2.4 cm. wide, pubescent or glabrescent, deciduous. Sepals subequal, oblong, 2.3–2.5 cm. long, 1–1.3 cm. wide, obtuse or emarginate at the apex, minutely pubescent, strongly reflexed in fruit. Corolla white, funnel-shaped, 11–12.5 cm. long; tube cylindrical, 8 cm. long, 1.1 cm. in diameter; midpetaline areas shortly pubescent when young. Capsule ovoid, brown, 1.8 cm. long. Seeds ovoid, 1.0 cm. long, with white hairs 1.8 cm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: A perennial, woody-based, erect subshrub up to 1.2 m. tall; stems stout, velvety-tomentose. Leaf-blade ovate, 7–13 cm. long, 4.75–9 cm. wide, obtuse or subacute and apiculate at the apex, cordate at the base, entire, pubescent above, with a dense white woolly tomentum beneath; petiole 3.5 cm. long. Flowers solitary; peduncle 1.6–2.5 cm. long; pedicel about 4 mm. long; bracts elliptic, 3.9–4.5 cm. long, 3.2–4 cm. wide, closely adpressed to the calyx, costate, densely velvety outside, glabrous and with impressed venation inside (Fig. 22/7, p. 102). Sepals elliptic, very similar to the bracts, 2.3–2.7 cm. long, 1–1.6 cm. wide. Corolla white, narrowly funnel-shaped, 11 cm. long; tube narrow, silky-pubescent; limb with silky midpetaline areas. Capsule globose, 2.5 cm. in diameter, glabrous. Seeds ovoid, 11 mm. long, 6 mm. wide, covered with cream hairs 2 cm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Erect shrubby herb to 1.8 m. tall; stems numerous, unbranched, ridged, angular, tomentose or glabrous. Leaf-blade oblong to ovate, 7.5–12.5 cm. long, 3.7–8.5 cm. wide, rounded or acute and shortly apiculate at the apex, rounded or cuneate at the base, undulate or entire, rarely base subhastate or lamina deeply trilobed, upper surface puberulous or tomentose, lower covered with a dense floccose tomentum or entirely glabrous all over; petiole 1–3 cm. long, biglandular at the apex. Flowers solitary; peduncle 1.3–5.3 cm. long, pubescent; pedicel about 5 mm. long; bracts obovate, 1.6–4 cm. long, 1.3–3.0 cm. wide, tomentose or glabrous, venose. Sepals elliptic, obtuse, tomentose or glabrous, 1.7–3.2 cm. long, 1–l.3(–3) cm. wide. Corolla white or pale rose or purplish at the base of the tube, narrowly funnel-shaped, (7–)9–12.5 cm. long; tube cylindrical, about 1.2–1.6 cm. in diameter and 8 cm. long; limb glabrous save for sparsely lanate apical part of the midpetaline areas outside. Capsule ovoid, 2.6 cm. long. Seeds ovoid, 9 mm. long, covered with long hairs.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Subshrubby climbing herb; stems ± pubescent. Leaf-blade oblong-ovate, up to 18(–24) cm. long and 9(–12.5) cm. wide, obtuse or subacute at the apex, truncate, rarely cordate at the base, with traces of floccose pubescence above, densely velvety beneath with yellowish-white tomentum; petiole 5(–8) cm. long, densely tomentose. Flowers several in a dense cyme; peduncle 2 cm. long; pedicels 1–1.5 cm. long; bracts oblong-obovate, thinly velvety, 3.5–4.5 cm. long, 1.6–4 cm. wide. Sepals elliptic, 1.2–1.5 cm. long, 5 mm. wide, tomentose. Corolla crimson, funnel-shaped, (3.8–)6 cm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Shrub 1–2 m. tall with erect or ascending, blackish or purple-brown branchlets which become spine-tipped or at least pointed; young shoots woolly-pubescent. Leaves borne on short shoots; blade very small, reniform, 5–9 mm. long, 5–14 mm. wide, very obtuse, glabrous above and pubescent beneath or pubescent on both surfaces; petiole pubescent, 4–11 mm. long. Flowers solitary, axillary; peduncle 10–12 mm. long. Sepals oval or suborbicular, the outer 3.5–4 mm. long, 2–2.5 mm. wide and the inner 4–5 mm. long, 4 mm. wide, very obtuse, glabrous or pubescent; margins ciliate. Corolla purple or white with a purple centre, silvery-pubescent on the midpetaline areas, broadly funnel-shaped, 2–2.8 cm. long. Capsule ovoid, 7–9 mm. long. Seeds ovoid, 6 mm. long, 3.5 mm. wide, densely covered with woolly hairs 5–10 mm. long (Fig. 24/2, p. 131).
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Shrub with suberect or partly twining or scrambling branches to 2.4 m. long, densely covered with grey or yellowish spreading pubescence. Leaf-blade orbicular, 8.5–13(–23) cm. long, 8.5–11(–25) cm. wide, very obtuse at the apex, cordate and palmately 7-nerved at the base, glabrous or minutely papillate above, finely adpressed silky-pubescent beneath; petiole 5–10 (–16) cm. long. Flowers several to many in pedunculate branched cymes; bracts broadly ovate-spathulate to orbicular, (1.0–)1.2–1.8 cm. long, (0.4–)0.7–1.3 cm. wide, softly grey-pubescent. Sepals oblong-spathulate or elliptic, the outer 1–1.8 cm. long and 3–9 mm. wide, broadest near the apex, the inner linear or lanceolate, grey-silky. Corolla white, cream or yellow with a purple centre, funnel-shaped, 5–7.5 cm. long; midpetaline areas pilose. Capsule ovoid, 1.3 cm. long, 1.1 cm. wide, glabrous. Seeds ovoid, 13 mm. long, 6 mm. wide, densely clothed with patent, pale golden hairs about 1 cm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Shrub with suberect or twining, pubescent stems up to 6 m. long; roots probably tuberous. Leaf-blade ovate to reniform, 3.5–14.5 cm. long, 3.2–16 cm. wide, obtuse, apiculate, acuminate or even bilobed at the apex, cordate at the base, sparsely pubescent or glabrous above, finely pubescent or glabrescent beneath; petiole 1–10 cm. long. Flowers few to many in cymes; peduncle 3.5–20 cm. long; pedicels and secondary peduncles 0.2–2 cm. long; bracts linear-lanceolate, 1.1–1.4 cm. long, 2 mm. wide. Sepals linear-lanceolate to ovate, 0.7–2.1 cm. long, 2.5–5 mm. wide, silky-pubescent or pilose. Corolla white, cream or yellow with a purple centre, funnel-shaped, 5–8 cm. long; midpetaline areas pubescent or pilose; tube narrowed below. Capsule ellipsoidal, 1.7–2 cm. long, 1.2–1.3 cm. wide. Seeds ovoid, 9 mm. long, 6 mm. wide, covered with long golden hairs about 1 cm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Perennial, twining, subshrubby herb; stems covered with spreading or reflexed bristly hairs. Leaf-blade orbicular-reniform or ovate, 7.5–12 cm. long and wide, obtuse at the apex, cordate at the base, glabrous or minutely scaly above, very densely covered with adpressed bristly hairs beneath; petiole 2–15 cm. long, bristly hairy. Flowers several in ± dense to lax, often trifid cymes; peduncle bristly hairy, 7–19 cm. long; pedicels and secondary peduncles 2–20 mm. long; bracts small, oblong-lanceolate, 4 mm. long, 1 mm. wide. Sepals rigid, sometimes with reflexed tips, oblong or lanceolate, 8.5–12 mm. long, 2–4 mm. wide, acute or acuminate at the apex, closely imbricate, strigose-pubescent. Corolla white or pale mauve with a purple centre, funnel-shaped, 4–6 cm. long, densely strigose-pilose. Unripe capsule white, ovoid, quite unlike that in apparently related species, narrowed to a neck below and also narrowed above to the pointed apex, 3 cm. long, 1.7 cm. wide; diameter at basal neck 5.5–6.5 mm. Seeds oblong-ovoid, bluntly 3-angled, curiously like a spider’s body, dark brown, 10 mm. long, 6 mm. wide, glabrous save for a short but conspicuous tuft of golden hairs near the hilum.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Erect subshrub covered with yellow hairs or glabrescent. Leaf-blade ovate, 10–11 cm. long, 6–7 cm. wide, acuminate or cuspidate at the apex, narrowed but obtuse at the base; petiole 4 cm. long. Inflorescences about 10-flowered, cymose; peduncle up to 9 cm. long. Sepals subequal, herbaceous, “ subulate ” (linear-oblong ?), 8–10 mm. long and 1.5–2 mm. wide, hairy on backs. Corolla violet, narrowly funnel-shaped with rather cylindrical tube, 5 cm. long, hirsute in bud. Capsule not known.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Liane with terete, hollow stems covered with adpressed bristly pubescence. Leaf-blade elliptic-rhomboidal or oblong, 7–15.5 cm. long, 3.5–7 cm. wide, acute and aristate at the apex, narrowed but ± rounded at the base, glabrous above, sparsely adpressed pilose (densely so when very young) beneath; petiole 3 cm. long, bristly-pubescent. Flowers several in dense cymes; peduncle 9–17 cm. long; bracts 1.9 cm. long, 0.5 cm. wide, spathulate or linear, acuminate; or inflorescences branched and lax with secondary peduncles 0.5–5 cm. long. Sepals lanceolate, 1.0–1.3 cm. long, 3–5 mm. wide, outer densely covered with adpressed bristly pubescence. Corolla purple, pink or white, funnel-shaped, 5–6 cm. long; midpetaline areas sparsely hairy. Capsule ovoid, obtuse, 1.5 cm. long, 3-valved, with persistent reflexed sepals. Seeds 3, compressed-ovoid, 6 mm. long, very dark brown, densely covered with brown hairs about 1 cm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Subshrub with twining stems; young parts densely villous, later glabrous. Leaf-blade broadly ovate, 10 cm. long, 8 cm. wide, acuminate at the apex, rounded or slightly cordate at the base, covered with adpressed yellow hairs beneath and on the nerves above; petiole yellow-villous, 2.5 cm. long. Inflorescence cymose, few-flowered; peduncle yellow-villous, 2–4 cm. long. Sepals herbaceous, “ subulate ” (linear-lanceolate), 1.4–1.6 cm. long and 2 mm. wide, hairy on backs. Corolla rose, campanulate above, tubular below, 5 cm. long, hairy. Capsule not known.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Erect shrub; stems silvery-hairy or glabrescent, up to 2 m. tall, covered with prominent leaf-scars. Leaf-blade elliptic-ovate to almost orbicular, (0.5–)1.4–6 cm. long, (0.15–)0.8–4.5 cm. wide, obtuse or slightly emarginate at the apex, rounded at the base, glabrescent or obscurely pubescent above, adpressed silvery-hairy beneath; petiole 0.2–1.5 cm. long, silvery-hairy, biglandular at the apex. Flowers solitary, sessile, clustered on abbreviated branchlets; bracts lanceolate or triangular 5–9 mm. long, 2–2.5 mm. wide, densely silvery-white pubescent. Sepals similar to the bracts. Corolla mauve, funnel-shaped, 2.7–4.2 cm. long; midpetaline areas silky-pilose. Capsule ovoid, 1.1 cm. long. Seeds ovoid, 6 mm. long, 4 mm. wide, densely covered with pale golden-buff hairs 1 cm. long (Fig. 24/3, p. 131).
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Large, glabrous liane with tuberous roots; stems twining. Leaf-blade orbicular in outline, entire or palmately 3–9-lobed, 6–24 cm. long, 6–18 cm. wide, cordate or truncate at the base; lobes lanceolate to ovate, acuminate at the apex, entire; petiole 3–11 cm. long. Inflorescences few- to many-flowered; peduncles 2.5–20 cm. long; pedicels 0.9–2.5 cm. long; flower-buds globular. Sepals markedly convex, clasping the corolla-tube, orbicular or elliptic, 6–12 mm. long. Corolla reddish-purple, funnel-shaped, with the tube narrow below, 5–6 cm. long. Capsule ovoid, obtuse, 1.2–1.4 cm. long. Seeds 6–7 mm. long, black, covered with ± 7 mm. long silky hairs.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Erect subsucculent shrub to 0.75 m.; shoots silvery-pubescent, later glabrous. Leaf-blade linear-oblong to oblong-oblanceolate, 1.5–9 cm. long, 0.5–1.1 cm. wide, obtuse at the apex, cuneate at the base, green and glabrous above, silvery-pubescent, woolly or glabrescent beneath; petiole 5–7 mm. long, biglandular at the apex. Flowers solitary; peduncle and pedicels short, 2–3 mm. long; bracts linear, 3–8 mm. long, silvery-pubescent. Sepals lanceolate, acuminate, 0.6–1.8 cm. long, 2–2.5 mm. wide, silvery-pubescent. Corolla white or pink with darker centre, funnel-shaped, 2.7–5 (–6.3) cm. long; midpetaline areas silvery-pilose. Capsule ovoid, obtuse, 1.6 cm. long. Seeds subglobose, 8 mm. in diameter, densely covered with closely adpressed silky golden hairs.
bibliographicCitation: Convolvulaceae, B. Verdcourt (East African Herbarium). Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1963

description: Glabrous perennial herb up to 2 m. high. Leaves long-petiolate; lamina oblong-ovate, up to 30 cm. long and 15 cm. wide, apex acute, base subcordate, margins crenate or doubly crenate, slightly pruinose, green; petiole up to 7 cm. long, subterete, grooved above, broadened at the base, ± purplish. Inflorescence a paniculate cyme to 50 cm. long and 30 cm. broad; pedicels 9–15 mm. long. Calyx-lobes narrowly lanceolate, 7–13 mm. long, 1.5–2.5 mm. wide, connate at the base for 0.5–1 mm. Corolla yellowish green with cream or yellow lobes; tube 17–19 mm. long; lobes 9–10.5 mm. long, 5–6.5 mm. wide. Anthers with apical glands 0.2 mm. in diameter; episepalous stamens included 2 mm. within the tube, anthers ± 1.5 mm. long, 0.85 mm. wide; epipetalous anthers exserted, 1.3 mm. long, 0.7–0.8 mm. wide. Nectary scales linear, 3–4 mm. long. Carpels 10–12 mm. long; styles 3–4 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Crassulaceae, G.E. Wickens. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1987

description: Glabrous pruinose perennial, 0.2–1 m. high. Leaves petiolate; blade lanceolate-elliptic, sometimes 3-lobed or 3-foliate on upper leaves, median leaves 7.5–15 cm. long, 2.5–5.5 cm. wide, apex acute, base cuneate, margins deeply crenate-serrate, glaucous or grey-green, dark purple-spotted beneath; petiole up to 4 cm. long, terete, not dilated at the base. Inflorescence a paniculate cyme 10–30 cm. long; pedicels 5–20 mm. long. Calyx-lobes narrowly lanceolate, 8–15 mm. long, 2–3 mm. wide, connate at the base for 1–2 mm. Corolla creamy white or yellow; tube 19–27 mm. long; lobes 10–16 mm. long, 4–6 mm. wide. Anthers with apical glands 0.1–0.2 mm. in diameter; episepalous stamens included 1–3 mm. within the tube, 1.8–2 mm. long, 1 mm. wide; epipetalous stamens with anthers exserted, 1.3–1.5 mm. long, 0.6–0.7 mm. wide. Nectary scales linear, 5–7.5 mm. long. Carpels 10–15 mm. long, attenuated into styles 7–10 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Crassulaceae, G.E. Wickens. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1987

description: Glabrous pruinose perennial; stem erect or decumbent at the base, 0.5–1.3 m. or more tall. Leaves opposite, sessile, obovate to broadly obovate or subcircular, up to 20(–25) cm. long, 13 cm. wide, apex obtuse, base cuneate and semi-amplexicaul, margins entire, undulate, crenate or serrate, glaucous, often with purple markings above and beneath. Inflorescence a paniculate cyme borne on a flowering stem up to 30 cm. or more long; pedicels ± 15(–25) mm. long. Calyx-lobes linear-triangular, (5–) 10–17 mm. long, (2–)3–6 mm. wide, long-attenuate, connate at the base for 1–2 mm. Corolla white, rarely cream, sometimes flushed with pink, greenish on the lower part of the tube; tube (19–)45–120 mm. long; lobes overlapping in bud, lanceolate to broadly obovate, (6–)10–25 mm. long, 6–13 mm. wide, mucronate (mucro ± 2 mm. long). Anthers oblong, with apical glands ± 0.3–0.4 mm. in diameter; episepalous stamens included within the corolla-tube, anthers ± (1.5–) 4–5 mm. long, (0.7–)1.5–2.5 mm. wide; epipetalous stamens barely protruding, anthers ± (0.9–)2–2.5 mm. long, (0.5–)1–1.5 mm. wide. Nectary scales linear, (4–)4.5–9(–12.5) mm. long. Carpels ovate-lanceolate, (9–)15–30 mm. long, attenuate into styles (9–)30–80 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Crassulaceae, G.E. Wickens. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1987

description: Low-growing perennial up to 15 cm. high; stem erect to decumbent, glabrous. Leaves glabrous, petiolate; blade obovate or suborbicular, up to 7 cm. long, 5 cm. wide, apex obtuse, base cuneate to sometimes rounded, margins entire, sinuate or remotely crenate, green to reddish; petiole up to 1.5(–2) cm. long, 0.1–0.15(–0.2) cm. wide, flat, semiamplexicaul. Inflorescence ± dense, corymbose, 2–3(–7) cm. long, with a few glandular hairs or glabrous; pedicels 1–3 mm. long. Calyx-lobes lanceolate to linear-lanceolate, 3.5–4.5 mm. long, 1–1.8 mm. wide, connate at the base for ± 0.3 mm. Corolla bright red, light green on the lower part of the tube; tube 7–9.5 mm. long; lobes narrowly to broadly oblong-ovate, ± 5 mm. long, 2–3 mm. wide, mucronate (mucro ± 0.3 mm. long). Episepalous stamens included 0.5–1 mm. below the epipetalous stamens; epipetalous stamens with tips attaining the throat of the tube or included by up to 1.5 mm.; anthers with apical glands ± 0.1 mm. in diameter; anthers of both whorls nearly the same size, broadly oblong, 0.65–7 mm. long, 0.6–0.65 mm. wide. Nectary scales linear, 2–2.5 mm. long. Carpels linear-lanceolate, 6.5–7 mm. long, abruptly terminating in styles 2–2.5 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Crassulaceae, G.E. Wickens. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1987

description: Glabrous pruinose perennial; stem erect or decumbent at the base, 0.4–1.5(–2.3) m. high. Leaves petiolate; blade ovate, oblong or obovate, sometimes 3-lobed or 3-foliate, median leaves 6–20(–25) cm. long, 2.5–10(–13) cm. wide, apex obtuse, base cuneate, narrowed into the petiole or petiole distinct, margins coarsely bluntly serrate to crenate or subentire, glaucous or glaucescent, sometimes with maroon or purple spots near the margin beneath; petiole 0.5–2.5 cm. long, flattened and usually slightly grooved above. Inflorescence a paniculate cyme up to 35 cm. long; pedicels 5–15(–20) mm. long. Calyx-lobes lanceolate to lanceolate-subulate, 6–13(–22) mm. long, (1.5–)2–3(–4) mm. wide, connate at the base for 0.5–2 mm. Corolla-tube whitish- or yellowish-green, limb cream with a yellow throat or yellow, rarely yellowish pink; tube (13–)15–28 mm. long; lobes oblong-ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 6–15(–18) mm. long, 3–6(–7) mm. wide, mucronate (mucro 0.5–1.5 mm. long). Anthers with apical glands 0.15–0.2(–0.45) mm. in diameter; episepalous stamens included 1–3(–5) mm. within the tube, anthers oblong, 1.1–1.9(–2.3) mm. long, 0.7–1.2 mm. wide; epipetalous stamens barely exserted to entirely included, anthers oblong, 0.8–1.5 mm. long, 0.6–1 mm. wide. Nectary scales linear-subulate, 2–9 mm. long. Carpels linear-lanceolate, 7–14 mm. long, attenuated into styles 4–13 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Crassulaceae, G.E. Wickens. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1987

description: Glabrous pruinose perennial or sometimes annual; stem erect or sometimes decumbent at the base, 0.2–1.2(–2) m. high, simple or sometimes with a branch near the base. Leaves petiolate; blade oblong to oblong-lanceolate, spathulate or triangular, (1–)2.5–4(–8.5) cm. long, (0.5–)1.5–2.5(–5.5) cm. wide, apex acute to obtuse, base cuneate, margins entire to shallowly crenate sometimes ± deeply 3-lobed (but not in E. Africa); petiole 0.3–1.2 cm. long (elsewhere lower and median leaves sometimes peltate with petiole 1.7–4.7 cm. long), subcylindrical, not broadened at the base, slightly constricted at the point of attachment and easily detachable from the stem. Inflorescence a paniculate cyme up to 20(–48) cm. long; pedicels 2–5(–8) mm. long. Calyx-lobes lanceolate or triangular, (0.5–)1–2 mm. long, 0.8–1.1 mm. wide, acute, connate at the base for 0.1–1 mm. Corolla red or orange-red, yellowish to greenish in the lower part of the tube; tube (6–)7–10 mm. long, twisted in the upper part during fruiting and colour fading; lobes lanceolate or elliptic, (2.5–)4–5 mm. long, 1.5–2 mm. wide, very acute but not apiculate. Stamens included within the corolla-tube; anthers with small apical glands, both episepalous and epipetalous ones broadly oblong, (0.3–)0.5–0.7(–0.8) mm. long, 0.4–0.5 mm. wide. Nectary scales linear-subulate, 1–2.5(–3.5) mm. long. Carpels linear-lanceolate, 4–6(–7) mm. long, terminating in styles 0.3–1 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Crassulaceae, G.E. Wickens. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1987

description: Glabrous pruinose perennial; stem erect or decumbent at the base, 0.3–1.2 m. high. Leaves petiolate; blade narrowly to broadly ovate, up to 10 cm. long, 7 cm. wide, apex acute to obtuse, base cuneate, margins bluntly serrate to crenate, rarely subentire, glaucous or glaucescent, sometimes with maroon or purple spots beneath; petiole 0.5–2.5 cm. long, slightly flattened and grooved above, not broadened at the base, often ± slightly constricted at point of attachment and easily detachable from the stem. Inflorescence a paniculate cyme 25 cm. or more long; pedicels 2–5(–8) mm. long. Calyx-lobes linear-lanceolate to linear-subulate, (2–)3–6 mm. long, 1–2 mm. wide, connate at the base for (0.2–) 0.5–1 mm. Corolla orange-yellow to pink, vermillion, crimson or scarlet, lower part of tube greenish; tube (5–)10–12(–14) mm. long; lobes lanceolate-ovate, (3–)5–6.5 mm. long, (1–)1.8–2.5 mm. wide, acute, mucronate (mucro 0.2–1 mm. long). Anthers with apical glands 0.05–0.1 mm. in diameter; episepalous stamens 1–2 mm. included within the tube, anthers oblong (0.6–)0.85–0.9 mm. long, 0.55–0.6 mm. wide; epipetalous stamens 0–1 mm. included within the tube, anthers oblong (0.55–) 0.7–0.75 mm. long, 0.5–0.6 mm. wide. Nectary scales linear, 2–3.5 mm. long. Carpels linear-lanceolate, (4.5–)6.5–8(–10) mm. long, terminating in styles 1–2 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Crassulaceae, G.E. Wickens. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1987

description: Glabrous pruinose perennial; stem erect or decumbent at the base, 0.6–2 m. high. Leaves petiolate, peltate or auriculate; basal leaves suborbicular, cuneate or slightly cordate at the base, margins entire; upper leaves lanceolate; petioles of median leaves 3–10 cm. long, ± terete, slightly broadened at the base. Inflorescence a paniculate cyme, up to 35 cm. long. Calyx-lobes lanceolate, 9–16 mm. long, 3–5 mm. wide, acute, connate at the base for 1–2 mm. Corolla-tube greenish, limb cream outside, cream, yellow, pink or salmon-pink inside; tube 17–21 mm. long; lobes ovate-lanceolate, 8–11 mm. long, 3–5.5 mm. wide, mucronate (mucro ± 1 mm. long). Anthers with apical glands ± 0.25 mm. in diameter; episepalous stamens included 1–2.5 mm. within the tube, anthers oblong, ± 2 mm. long, 1 mm. wide; epipetalous stamens exserted, anthers oblong, 1.4–1.6 mm. long, 0.8–0.9 mm. wide. Nectary scales linear-subulate, 2.5–5 mm. long. Carpels linear-lanceolate, 10–12 mm. long, attenuate into styles 6–9 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Crassulaceae, G.E. Wickens. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1987

description: Tomentose perennial herb 20–90(–150) cm. high; hairs pointed, non-glandular; stem grey or brownish-grey below, grey-green above. Leaves sessile or petiolate, blade lanceolate to ± rhombic, or ovate to subcircular, up to 12 cm. long, 4 cm. wide, cuneate at the base, margins dentate or dissected, velvety, grey or brownish green; petiole, if present, up to 2 cm. long, flattened and grooved above, not broadened at the base. Inflorescence up to 15 cm. long; pedicels 1–2 mm. long, stout. Calyx-lobes subulate to triangular-lanceolate, 4–8 mm. long, 1–1.8 mm. wide, connate at the base for 0.1–1 mm., tomentose without, also on lobes within. Corolla pale, lemon or golden yellow or buff-orange-pink, tomentose without; tube 10–12 mm. long; lobes obovate, 5–7 mm. long, 2.8–3.5 mm. wide, mucronate (mucro 0.3–1 mm. long). Episepalous stamens included, 1–2 mm. below the epipetalous stamens; epipetalous stamens barely protruding to 1.5 mm. included within the corolla-tube; anthers with apical glands ± 0.8 mm. in diameter, both whorls nearly the same size, oblong-ovate, 0.7–1.1 mm. long, 0.5–0.65 mm. wide. Nectary scales linear-lanceolate, 2.5–3.5 mm. long. Carpels linear-lanceolate, 6–8.5 mm. long, terminating in styles 1–2 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Crassulaceae, G.E. Wickens. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1987

description: Perennial herb (0.2–)0.4–1 m. high; stem glandular-pubescent or glabrous below, pubescent above. Leaves petiolate; blade ovate to suborbicular, up to 11 cm. long, 10 cm. wide, apex obtuse, base abruptly contracted into the petiole, margins crenate to crenate-serrate, glandular pubescent, sometimes sparsely so or ?glabrous; petiole up to 3 cm. long. Inflorescence up to 20 cm. long, densely glandular-hairy, sticky; pedicels 5–20 mm. long. Calyx-lobes lanceolate, 10–30 mm. long, 3–6 mm. wide, nearly free or connate for up to 1 mm. at the base, densely glandular-pubescent. Corolla white, glandular-pubescent; tube 50–65 mm. long; lobes oblong-ovate to broadly obovate, (10–)15–20 mm. long, 8–14 mm. wide, mucronate (mucro ± 2 mm. long). Anthers with apical glands; episepalous stamens 1–5 mm. included within the corolla tube; anthers oblong, ± 2.3 mm. long, 1.3 mm. wide; epipetalous stamens with anthers partly or entirely exserted, anthers oblong, ± 2 mm. long, 1.2 mm. wide. Nectary scales linear-subulate, 3.5–7 mm. long. Carpels oblong-lanceolate, 18–22 mm. long, attentuated into styles 32–40 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Crassulaceae, G.E. Wickens. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1987

description: Perennial herb up to 1.2 m. high; stem glabrous. Leaves glabrous, sessile, oblong-spathulate, up to 20 cm. long, 6 cm. wide, apex obtuse, base cuneate, semiamplexicaul, margins entire or irregularly undulate. Inflorescence lax, ± 12 cm. long; pedicels up to 5 mm. long, glabrous or with very sparse, short-stalked glandular hairs less than 0.1 mm. long. Calyx-lobes lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, 3.5–6 mm. long, 1–2 mm. wide, connate at the base for ± 1 mm., very sparsely glandular-pubescent. Corolla coral pink to brick red, very sparsely glandular pubescent; tube 8–12 mm. long; lobes obovate, 4.5–6.5 mm. long, 2.5–3.5 mm. wide, mucronate (mucro ± 0.5 mm. long). Episepalous stamens included, ± 1.5 mm. below the epipetalous stamens; epipetalous stamens 0.5–1 mm. included within the tube; anthers without apical glands, broadly oblong, both whorls nearly the same size, ± 0.6 mm. long, 0.4 mm. wide. Nectary scales linear, 2–2.5 mm. long. Carpels linear-lanceolate, ± 6.5 mm. long, terminating in styles 0.5–1.5 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Crassulaceae, G.E. Wickens. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1987

description: Herb to 10(–20) cm. high, perennial from a tuberous rootstock; aerial parts probably dying back annually; stem erect, simple, hairy. Leaves opposite, mainly basal, oblong-ovate to broadly ovate, (3–)4–8 cm. long, (1.8–) 2–4.5 cm. wide, apex obtuse, base cuneate or attenuate, margins entire to shallowly and irregularly crenate, sparsely hairy to glabrescent; petiole 1–2 cm. long, subamplexicaul. Inflorescence a terminal compound cyme, branching ± dichotomously at first, becoming monochasial and flowers secund; the occasional flowers 5-merous; bracts linear-lanceolate, 2–3 mm. long, soon falling; pedicels short, ± 1.5 (3–4 fide Chiovenda) mm. long. Calyx 2.5(–2.8) mm. long; lobes triangular to linear-triangular, connate at the base for ± 0.2 mm. Corolla orange, flecked with longitudinal purple markings; tube cylindrical, slightly inflated, 13 (12–14 fide Chiovenda) mm. long; lobes ovate, 3.5 mm. long, 2 mm. wide (± 6 × 1.5 mm. fide Chiovenda), acute. Stamens in 2 series, included, episepalous stamens ± 1 mm. within the corolla-tube, epipetalous stamens 2 mm.; filaments 2 mm. long; anthers with apical gland, oblong, 0.4 mm. long, 0.3 mm. wide. Nectary scales linear, ± 2(–3) mm. long. Carpels cylindrical-lanceolate, 9(–11) mm. long, rather fleshy, with longitudinal purple markings, connate at the base for ± 1 mm. (gynophore), tapering into styles ± 2 mm. long. Seeds numerous, oblong-ovoid, ± 0.4 mm. long, 0.2 mm. wide, longitudinally striate (slightly immature). Fig. 8.
bibliographicCitation: Crassulaceae, G.E. Wickens. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1987

description: Glabrous perennial herb; stem erect, 0.3–3 m. high. Leaves petiolate; blade oblong, ovate or suborbicular, up to 18 cm. long, 10 cm. wide, apex obtuse, base cuneate, margins crenate, light green; petiole up to 3 cm. long, flattened and grooved above, slightly broadened at the base. Inflorescence a densely flowered paniculate cyme up to 30(–70) cm. long; pedicels 1–4 mm. long, conspicuously broadened below the flower, glabrous, rarely sparsely pilose (var. subpilosa Cuf. from Ethiopia). Calyx-lobes triangular-subulate, 2–8 mm. long, 1–1.5 mm. wide, long-attenuate, connate at the base for 0.1–0.3 mm., glabrous, rarely sparsely pilose (var. subpilosa). Corolla-tube pale to greenish yellow, limb yellow to dark orange, reddish orange or red; tube 8–12 mm. long; lobes oblong-lanceolate to broadly obovate, 2–5 mm. long, 1.5–4 mm. wide, truncate or retuse, mucronate (mucro 0.2–1 mm. long). Episepalous stamens with anthers included within the tube by 1.5–2.5 mm., epipetalous stamens with tip of anthers almost attaining the throat of the tube or included with the tube by up to 1 mm.; anthers with apical glands 0.05–0.1 mm. in diameter; anthers of both whorls nearly the same size, broadly oblong, 0.7–0.85 mm. long, 0.5–0.7 mm. wide. Nectary scales linear-subulate, 1–3.5 mm. long. Carpels linear-lanceolate, 5–9 mm. long, terminating in styles 1–3.5 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Crassulaceae, G.E. Wickens. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1987

description: Herb ± 10 cm. high, probably perennial, glabrous; stem decumbent, branched, erect portions densely leafy. Leaves opposite, suborbicular, broadly ovate or obovate, 1.5–5 cm. long, 1.3–4 cm. wide, apex obtuse, base attenuated, margins entire or serrate-crenate; petiole semiamplexicaul, up to 5 mm. long, 6 mm. wide and 2 mm. thick. Inflorescence a terminal compound cyme, branching ± dichotomously at first, becoming somewhat monchasial and flowers secund; pedicels 3–4 mm. long. Calyx 2.5–3 mm. long; lobes triangular, connate at the base for ± 0.5 mm. Corolla pale reddish yellow-brown; tube cylindrical, 13–14 mm. long, somewhat 4-angled and slightly inflated below the middle; lobes elliptic, 9–10 mm. long, 3.5–4 mm. wide, conspicuously mucronate in bud. Stamens in 2 series, included, episepalous stamen ± 1 mm. within the corolla-tube, epipetalous stamens attaining the throat; anthers oblong, 0.7–0.75 mm. long, 0.4–0.5 mm. wide, with globose apical gland. Nectary scales linear, 2–2.5 mm. long. Carpels cylindrical-lanceolate, 10–11.5 mm. long, connate at the base for 1–1.5 mm. (gynophore), tapering into styles ± 2 mm. long. Seeds numerous, oblong-ovoid, 0.6–0.65 mm. long, 0.45 mm. wide, longitudinally striate.
bibliographicCitation: Crassulaceae, G.E. Wickens. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1987

description: Glabrous pruinose presumably hapaxanthic herb; stem robust, erect, 0.5–3 m. high. Leaves petiolate; blade subovate or cordate, usually boat-shaped, up to 15 cm. long, 6 cm. wide, apex acute to acuminate, median leaves usually with 2 small lobes or auricles at the base, margins entire to subentire, glaucous above, pale green and usually with purple or maroon mottling beneath; petiole up to 5 cm. long, ± round and slightly broadened at the base. Inflorescence lax, many-flowered, up to 30 cm. or more long; pedicels 5–10(–15) mm. long. Calyx-lobes lanceolate-subulate, 2–5.5 mm. long, 1.5–2 mm. wide, acute, connate at the base for 0.5–1 mm. Corolla-tube greenish white or cream, limb cream or pale yellow; tube 17–22 mm. long; lobes lanceolate-ovate to obovate, 4.5–6.5 mm. long, 2.5–4 mm. wide, obtuse-apiculate. Anthers with apical glands ± 0.15 mm. in diameter; episepalous stamens included 0–2 mm. within the tube, anthers oblong, ± 1.3 mm. long, 0.75–0.85 mm. wide; epipetalous stamens with anthers exserted to half included, anthers oblong, ± 1.1 mm. long, 0.7–0.8 mm. wide. Nectary scales linear, 2.5–4 mm. long, ± 3-fid. Carpels linear-subulate, 10–14 mm. long, attenuated into styles 6–8 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Crassulaceae, G.E. Wickens. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1987

description: Glabrous pruinose perennial; stem erect, 0.6–1.3 m. high. Leaves petiolate; blade oblong or ovate, up to 20 cm. long, 16 cm. wide, apex obtuse, base truncate or auriculate, margins crenate, bluntly serrate or dentate, subsinuate towards the apex, glaucous or glaucescent; petiole 2–6 cm. long, flattened and grooved above, slightly broadened at the base. Inflorescence a racemose cyme, up to 20 cm. or more long; pedicels 5–7(–12) mm. long. Calyx-lobes triangular-subulate, 7–11 mm. long, 1.5–2.5 mm. wide, attenuated, connate at the base for 0.5–1(–2) mm. Corolla ivory white, greenish white on the lower part of the tube; tube 27–33(–38) mm. long; lobes obovate, 10–16 mm. long, 5–8 mm. wide, mucronate (mucro 0.5–1 mm. long). Anthers with apical glands ± 0.25 mm. in diameter; episepalous stamens included 1–2 mm. within the tube, anthers oblong 2.5–3 mm. long, 1.2 mm. wide; epipetalous stamens exserted by 0.5–1.5 mm., anthers oblong, ± 2 mm. long, 1 mm. wide. Nectary scales linear-subulate, 4–13 mm. long. Carpels linear-lanceolate, 12–16(–18) mm. long, attenuated into styles 12–15(–18) mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Crassulaceae, G.E. Wickens. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1987

description: Perennial herb, up to 1.2 m. high; stem erect or decumbent at the base and rooting at the lower nodes, glabrous. Leaves glabrous, sessile, obovate or oblong, up to 10 cm. long, 5 cm. wide, apex obtuse, base cuneate and semi-amplexicaul, margins entire or slightly sinuate, green. Inflorescence ± globose, up to 15(–25) cm. long, glandular-pubescent with short-stalked glandular hairs up to 0.1 mm. long; pedicels 2–3(–5) mm. long. Calyx-lobes lanceolate, 3–4 mm. long, 1–2 mm. wide, connate at the base for 0.7–1 mm. Corolla bright red, green on the lower part of the tube; tube 9–12 mm. long; lobes oblong-ovate, 3.5–5 mm. long, 1.5–2.5 mm. wide, apex obtuse or obtuse-apiculate (apiculum only visible in buds or young flowers). Episepalous stamens included ± 1 mm. below the epipetalous stamens, epipetalous stamens included 1–2 mm. within the corolla-tube; anthers without apical glands, broadly oblong, both whorls nearly the same size, ± 0.7 mm. long, 0.5 mm. wide. Nectary scales linear, ± 2 mm. long. Carpels linear-lanceolate, 5.5–7.5 mm. long, terminating in styles ± 1.5 mm. long.
bibliographicCitation: Crassulaceae, G.E. Wickens. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1987

description: Slender decumbent annual herb with erect simple or branched stems up to 5 cm. high (10 cm. fide Hedberg (1975)), glabrous. Leaves sessile, tightly clustered, obovate, 4–5 mm. long, 2–2.5 mm. broad, apex obtuse, upper surface concave, lower convex, succulent, margin entire, blue-green or red; lower leaves opposite, upper alternate. Inflorescence a few-flowered cyme, usually barely extending beyond the leaves; pedicels 2–2.5 mm. long. Flowers 5-merous or sometimes with 4-merous flowers on the same plant. Calyx-tube subcampanulate, 2.2–2.5 mm. long; lobes shallowly triangular to semiorbicular, 0.6–0.7 mm. long, 1.6 mm. broad, obtuse. Petals free, attached to the rim of the calyx-tube, broadly obovate, 2 mm. long, 1.5–1.8 mm. broad, obtuse, white, pink or purplish, persistent. Stamens 8 or 10 (or possibly 5 fide Hedberg (1957)); outer stamens opposite the sepals, filaments slender, 1.2 mm. long, base dilated; inner stamens adnate to the petals for 0.1 mm. free for 1.2 mm.; anthers orbicular, ± 0.6 mm. long. Nectary scales subcylindrical-subspathulate, ± 0.6 mm. long, 0.9 mm. broad. Carpels immersed in the calyx-tube below, free for 1.5 mm., divergent, free portion tuberculate, opening along an equatorial furrow. Style slender, ± 0.5 mm. long, apex inflated. Seeds 1–3, ovoid, ± 1.4 mm. long, 0.6 mm. broad.
bibliographicCitation: Crassulaceae, G.E. Wickens. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1987

description: Succulent subshrub, with trailing subterranean or surface stems and erect sparsely branched leafy stems up to 60 cm. high (2 m. fide Hedberg (1957)), glabrous. Leaves ternate, subsessile, oblong-elliptic to oblong-oboval, 1.5–3 cm. long, 0.7–1.4 cm. broad, apex obtuse, base rounded-attenuate, flat, entire. Inflorescence a many-flowered terminal corymbose cyme; bracts resembling the leaves but smaller; pedicels 7–13 mm. long. Flowers 5-merous. Calyx-tube infundibuliform, ± 1 mm. long; lobes triangular-ovate, 4–5 mm. long, apex acute. Petals yellow, free, oblong-lanceolate, 10–15 mm. long, 4–5 mm. broad, long-acute. Stamens 10; filaments 9–11 mm. long; antipetalous filaments inserted 3–5 mm. above the base of the petal, free for 5–6 mm; anthers oval-orbicular. Nectary-scales spathulate, 1–1.2 mm. long, 0.8 mm. broad, retuse. Carpels 5, united at the base for 1.5 mm., 8–9 mm. long; style recurved, 2.5–3 mm. long. Seeds numerous, oblong-lanceolate, 1.5 mm. long, acute at both ends, striate. Fig. 3.
bibliographicCitation: Crassulaceae, G.E. Wickens. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1987

description: Slender decumbent perennial herb, with long trailing branched square or slightly winged stems up to 1 m. long, often rooting at the nodes to just below the inflorescence. Leaves sessile, mostly alternate at the base, ternate above; lamina fleshy, flat, oblong-spathulate to oblong-lanceolate, up to 2(–2.5 fide Raym.-Hamet (1957)) cm. long, 0.8 cm. broad, apex obtuse, base shortly spurred, margins entire. Inflorescence a corymbose-cyme; bracts obovate-spathulate to linear-lanceolate, 5–5.5 mm. long, 1.5–2.5 mm. broad, spurred; pedicels 2–6(–18) mm. long. Flowers 5-merous. Sepals oblong-ovate to oblong-lanceolate, 2.5–5 mm. long, 1–2 mm. broad, obtuse, connate at the base for 0.5 mm. and spurred. Petals lanceolate to oblong, 4.5–7 mm. long, 2–2.4 mm. broad, mucronate, connate at the base for 0.4–0.7 mm., yellow. Stamens 10; antisepalous filaments 3–3.5 mm. long; antipetalous filaments free 0.5–1 mm. from above the base of the petal, 2–3 mm. long; anthers ovate-reniform, ± 0.7 mm. long. Nectary scales linear-spathulate, ± 0.8 mm. long, 0.2 mm. broad, slightly retuse. Carpels subdivergent, united at the base for 1.5–2 mm., 2.5–3.5 mm. long; style recurved, ± 1 mm. long. Seeds numerous, narrowly oblong-ovoid, 1–1.2 mm. long, 0.2 mm. broad, finely mamillate.
bibliographicCitation: Crassulaceae, G.E. Wickens. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1987

description: Decumbent succulent perennial herb, with erect reddish usually pustulate branched stems, woody at the base, up to 30 cm. high. Leaves alternate to subopposite, sessile, generally tightly clustered on sterile shoots, oblong to oblong-ovoid, 5–20 mm. long, 2–3.5 mm. broad, apex obtuse, often papillose, base shortly auriculate-peltate, upper surface concave, lower convex, succulent, reddish in exposed places, green in shaded places. Inflorescence a terminal few-flowered corymbose cyme; bracts similar to the leaves but smaller; pedicels 1–4(–6) mm. long. Flowers 5-merous. Calyx-lobes united at the base for 0.5 mm., oblong-lanceolate, 2.5–6 mm. long, 1.5–2 mm. broad, apex obtuse and ± papillose, base spurred. Petals united at the base for 0.2–0.4 mm., oblong-lanceolate to oblong, 4–6(–12 fide Raym.-Hamet (1957)) mm. long, 1.5–2 mm. broad, obtuse. Stamens 10; antisepalous filaments 2.5–3 mm. long; antipetalous filaments inserted 1 mm. above the base of the petals, free for 1.5–2 mm.; anthers oval-orbicular, 0.6–0.8 mm. long. Nectary scales oblong-ligulate, 0.8 mm. long, 0.4 mm. broad, shortly retuse. Carpels 5, shortly united at the base for 0.5 mm., 5–6 mm. long; style 1 mm. long. Seeds numerous, ellipsoid, ± 1 mm. long, finely tuberculate.
bibliographicCitation: Crassulaceae, G.E. Wickens. Flora of Tropical East Africa. 1987

description: Climber or trailer to 6 m. Stems herbaceous, arising from a woody subterranean tuber, green, glabrous or somewhat hairy especially at the nodes, becoming more woody and grey-barked when older; basal stems gnarled and thickened with pale flaking bark. Leaves pedately 3(–5–6–9–15)-foliolate, foetid when crushed; terminal leaflet largest, ovate, equal-based, slightly apiculate, subentire to sinuate and obscurely to distinctly toothed, 15–90 mm. long, 9–64 mm. broad; lateral leaflets similar but smaller and somewhat unequal-based; median petiolule or central rhachis 5–32 mm. long, longer than the petiole; other petiolules up to 22 mm. long; petiole 4–22 mm. long. Tendrils simple. Dioecious.
